poems.title: Genesis 3:21: Clothed with the skins of victims slain
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Clothed with the skins of victims slain.
Our parents turn'd on Christ their eyes.
The Lamb whom God did then ordain.
The grand vicarious Sacrifice:
By faith they knew the blood was shed.
For them, and all their race to' atone,
And trusting in His merits, made
His perfect righteousness their own.

poems.title: Genesis 3: O Thou slaughter'd Lamb of God
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O Thou slaughter'd Lamb of God,
From the world's foundations slain,
By Thy sacrificial blood
Wash out all my guilty stain,
Clothe my spirit's nakedness
With a covering from above,
Put me on my spotless dress,
Wrap me up in heavenly love.

poems.title: Genesis 3:24: So He drove out the man: and He placed, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Spoil'd of the bliss to Adam given,
Out of my Maker's presence driven,
My fallen state I mourn;
But fondly sigh my Eden lost;
The flaming sword and angel-host
Prohibit my return.

A fallen, sinful child of man,
By innocence I seek in vain"
That Edeji to retrieve;
I cannot find the blissful place.
Or, banish'd from Jehovah's face.
Behold my God, and live.

Then let me die to see my Lord!
I rush upon that flaming sword
Which doth the sinner slay:
But he who by Thy justice dies,
By this shut out of paradise,
Shall find another way.

I find it now: most gracious God,
I enter boldly through the blood
Of my redeeming Lord;
By faith I see the bar removed,
I feel lost man again beloved,
And paradise restored.
Happy who in Christ delight,
And His commandments love.
They shall keep their gracious right
To paradise above,
Eat the' immortalizing tree,
From which they can no more be driven.
Feast on full felicity.
And live the life of heaven.

poems.title: Genesis: Principled with godly fear
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Principled with godly fear.
Righteousness he might have wrought,
Cain himself, in faith sincere,
Might have his oblation brought;
Cain had then accepted been.
The old murderer abhorr'd,
Conquer'd the besetting sin,
More than conquer'd through his Lord.

poems.title: Genesis 4:7: Though every sinful act increase
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Though every sinful act increase
Our strong propensity to sin.
Into our heart it need not press.
We need not let the evil in:
Though sin lie knocking at the door.
Admittance we may still refuse.
For Jesus doth to all restore
The power or life or death to choose.

poems.title: Genesis 4:7: Lusting to shed his brother's blood
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lusting to shed his brother's blood,
Must Cain to the desire submit?
He might have still superior stood,
And trampled sin beneath his feet:
And may not all, O Lord, embrace
The power o'er sin obtain'd by Thee?
Sufficient is Thy saving grace
For every reprobate, and me.

poems.title: Genesis 4:10: How loud the blood of Abel cries
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How loud the blood of Abel cries,
Demanding vengeance from the ground I
But louder still throughout the skies
Thou hear'st the blood of Jesus sound:
It pleads for the apostate race.
That all His murderers may live.
It asks for me Thy sparing grace,
And every drop cries out. Forgive!

poems.title: Genesis 5:22: O That I might walk with God
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O That I might walk with God!
Jesus my companion be,
Lead me to Thy bless'd abode.
Through the fire, or through the sea:
Join'd to Thee by humble love
Nothing I desire beside.
Only let me never move.
Never stir without my Guide.

poems.title: Genesis 5:29: This same shall comfort us concerning our work, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thou that Noah art!
Earth again in Thee is bless'd:
Comfort Thou my troubled heart.
Be my weary spirit's rest:
Then I shall no more complain,
Never at my lot repine:
Welcome toil, and grief, and pain!
All is well, if Christ be mine.

poems.title: Genesis 6:3: Yet for a time He strives with all
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Yet for a time He strives with all:
O may He strive with me,
Till quite recover'd from its fall
My soul is all like Thee!

poems.title: Genesis 6:3: Had God foreknown it could not be
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Had God foreknown it could not be,
That sinners should accept His grace.
Vain were that added century,
Which mock'd them with a longer space:
But O, they wilfully went on
Rebellious, till their day was pass'd,
And forced the lingering deluge down.
And perish'd in their sins at last.

How loath is God to strike, who stays
So long, before He gives the blow.
Threatens, and warns; yet still delays;
That sinners may His mercy know!
His wrath He wills us to prevent,
His timely warnings to receive,
And 'scape the threaten'd punishment,
And saved from sin for ever live.

poems.title: Genesis 6:5: And dare we our perfection boast
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
And dare we our perfection boast?
With haughty Luciferian scorn
Deny our innocency lost,
As still in God's resemblance born?
Great Author of our second birth,
Give us, our fallen souls to feel
As godlike as the beasts on earth,
As perfect as the fiends in hell.

poems.title: Genesis 6:6: He mourns His frustrated intent
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
He mourns His frustrated intent,
Who bade the rebel be:
But never doth my Lord repent
That He hath ransom'd me.

poems.title: Genesis: Grieved at His heart is God for me
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Grieved at His heart is God for me,
For sin which I have done?
And yet (alas, how can it be?)
And yet my heart is stone!
Wearied, and broke, and pierced, and torn,
My injured God and Friend,
Give me to look on Thee, and mourn,
Till grief with life shall end.

poems.title: Genesis 8:20, 21: Noah, descended from the skies
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Noah, descended from the skies,
Our faithful, merciful High-Priest,
The Lord accepts Thy sacrifice,
A savour of perpetual rest.
Thy death did once for all atone.
And God and man in Thee are one.

poems.title: Genesis 8:21: Father, if Thou my Father art
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, if Thou my Father art.
If Jesus made my sins His own,
Speak it into my listening heart,
Assure me that I am Thy son.
Comfort and rest in Christ restore.
And vow to curse this earth no more.

poems.title: Genesis: Lord, may not I Thy promise claim
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, may not I Thy promise claim
Made to the isles xwJaphetfCs name?
In mercy then to me impart
The largeness of a loving heart:

poems.title: Genesis 8: An heart to no one sect confined
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
An heart to no one sect confined,
But compassing the ransom'd kind,
Capacious of the Deity,
And grasping all Thy gifts and Thee.
Almighty to persuade Thou art,
Thou Friend of helpless woe,
Persuade me with my sin to part,
To let my misery go;
Persuade me to repent, believe,
Thine easy yoke to prove,
And then into Thine arms receive
The captive of Thy love.

poems.title: Genesis: Thou hast enlarged Thy church's bound
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou hast enlarged Thy church's bound,
Hast call'd us by Thy name,
Poor Gentiles we in Christ are found.
And Japheth dwells with Shem:
We dwell in tents, co-heirs with Thee,
Till Thou our souls remove.
With all the first-born church to see
Our Father's house above.

poems.title: Genesis 12:3: In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I Come Thou universal Blessing,
Abraham's long-expected Seed,
Perfect peace, and joy unceasing
Through the ransom'd nations spread;
Devilish pride, and brutal passion
Far from every heart remove,
Bless us with Thy full salvation.
Bless us with Thy heavenly love.

poems.title: Genesis 15:6, 17: Happy is the man forgiven
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Happy is the man forgiven:
This let every sinner feel,
Taste in Thee his present heaven,
Pant for greater blessings still:
O that all anew created
Might Thine image here retrieve,
Then to paradise translated
In Thy glorious presence live.

poems.title: Genesis 15: What can we ask or covet more
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What can we ask or covet more,
Who Abraham's Lord and God adore,
Who treading in his footsteps plead
The promise made to all his seed,
And trust in Jesu's faithful love.
Our shield on earth, our heaven above!

poems.title: Genesis 15:5: So shall thy seed be
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
His spiritual, believing seed
In glory shall excel,
Numbers of Israelites indeed.
Which only God can tell,
Distinguish'd by their Saviour's love
With dignity Divine,
And brighter than the stars above
They shall for ever shine.

poems.title: Genesis 15:6: Father, in Abraham's steps I tread
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, in Abraham's steps I tread,
Receive Thine evangelic word,
Who gav'st to suffer in my stead
Thine only Son, my God and Lord:
The faith, which now I act on Thee,
Who didst again my Surety raise,
Is counted righteousness to me,
And I am saved through Jesu's grace.

poems.title: Genesis: Thou Godseeslme
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Where'er I am, whate'er I do,
My heart is naked to Thy view:
O may I ever mindful be
The' all-seeing eye is fix'd on me!

poems.title: Genesis 17:1: God of all-sufficient grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
God of all-sufficient grace,
My God in Christ Thou art;
Bid me walk before Thy face.
Till I am pure in heart,
Till transform'd through faith Divine
I gain that perfect love unknown.
Bright in all Thine image shine,
By putting on Thy Son.

poems.title: Genesis: When first we of Thy promise heard
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
When first we of Thy promise heard,
Through unbelief we smiled,
Impossible the birth appear'd
Of Christ the holy Child:
But when Thou dost Thy Son reveal.
And show'st our sins forgiven.
We laugh for joy unspeakable,
For joy of present heaven.

poems.title: Genesis 18:14: Nothing too hard can be
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Nothing too hard can be
For mine almighty Lord:
Sufficient is Thy grace for me,
Who hang upon Thy word;
Thou canst. Thou wilt forgive,
My nature's sin erase,
And bid me in Thine image live,
And die to see Thy face.

poems.title: Genesis 18:17: Stupendous grace of the Most High
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Stupendous grace of the Most High!
What hath the Lord on worms bestow'd,
Call'd to the council of the sky,
And number'd with the friends of God I

poems.title: Genesis 18:19: Fain would I, Lord, my household lead
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Fain would I, Lord, my household lead
In all the paths of righteousness.
And train them up, an holy seed.
To serve Thy will, and spread Thy praise:
Implant in me the patriarch's mind,
My sacred cares and toils approve,
And bless the church I leave behind,
The children of my faith and love.

poems.title: Genesis 18:27: Despicable, frail, and dying
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Despicable, frail, and dying.
Vile before my God I am,
On Thine only grace relying;
Dust and ashes is my name:
Fallen, and corrupt my nature,
Yet I dare address Thy throne,
Speaking through a Mediator,
Him who makes my prayer His own.

poems.title: Genesis 18:32: WouLD-ST Thou for fifty righteous men
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
WouLD-ST Thou for fifty righteous men,
For ten, the wicked city spare,
And shall ten thousand plead in vain.
And mention Jesus in their prayer?
Thou, Lord, in answer to the just,
Hast long deferr'd Britannia's doom,

poems.title: Genesis 18:33: The Lord went His way, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Unwearied let us still request
By instant prayer whate'er we want:
The patriarch from asking ceased,
Before the' Almighty ceased to grant.

poems.title: Genesis 19:11: Tis thus the Lord His judgment shows
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Tis thus the Lord His judgment shows
On all that slight His mercy's voice,
Infatuating His harden'd foes.
He blinds them first, and then destroys.

poems.title: Genesis 19:16: Did I not lingering stand
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Did I not lingering stand.
Till mercy seized my hand.
Nor sufifer'd me to look
Tow'rd those I had forsook;
And rescued as a brand I am,
Pluck'd out of the infernal flame!

poems.title: Genesis 19:17: Escape for thy life, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O May I never look behind.
To sin and Satan turn again.
Rest in the world, or comfort find
In self, or linger on the plain.
But reaching tow'rd the mountain, fly,
And 'scape to Jesus in the sky.

poems.title: Genesis 19:22: Haste thee, escape thither
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jehovah for His servants cares.
Whene'er He makes His anger known,
The vessels of destruction spares,
Till mercy hath secured its own:
He cannot seal the sinner's doom
In storms of vengeance from above,
Till Lot is unto Zoar come.
And shelter'd safe in Jesu's love.

poems.title: Genesis 19:22: I cannot do anything till thou be come thither
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Kept off by Lot the fiery rain
On Sodom cannot yet descend,
The presence of one righteous man
Doth God's impending plagues suspend:
But woe to that devoted race,
Whom their despised protectors leave!
The wrath shall all on them take place,
The yawning gulf its prey receive.

poems.title: Genesis 19:24: Jehovah from Jehovah pours
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jehovah from Jehovah pours
His plagues on sinners unforgiven,
The Lord on earth in flaming showers
Hurls vengeance from the Lord in heaven;
For God with Christ, in essence one.
Hath given all judgment to His Son.

poems.title: Genesis: Is it a moral sense in man
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Is it a moral sense in man,
Reason, or pride, or virtue's power.
Which doth from passion's rage restrain,
And save us in the' unguarded hour?
No; but a secret force of Thine,
O Christ, preserves through ways unknown
Withheld from sin by grace Divine,
I give the praise to God alone.

poems.title: Genesis 19: A THOUSAND secret checks within
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
A Thousand secret checks within,
To unacknowledged grace I owe;
A thousand times preserved from sin,
I now my kind Preserver know;
Thou didst support my yielding heart,
Thou didst to good my will incline;
And when I chose the better part,
The virtuous thought was all Divine.

I envied oft the swine their meat,
But none the husks of pleasure gave:
Oft by my bosom-sin beset,
Mercy cofitfived my soul to save:
The grace I trembled to receive.
Escaping from the broken snare;
And scarcely durst my heart believe
That mercy could redeem so far.

Still on a precipice I stand,
Or seem on solid waves to tread;
Secure in an Almighty hand,
When raging flames surround my head;
Nigh is my sin, but Thou art nigher.
And while to Thee my soul I give,
I hang in air, I walk in fire,
In death by miracle I live!

poems.title: Genesis 19: I KNOW the power was Thine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I Know the power was Thine,
Which did from sin restrain,
And saved so oft by grace Divine,
I ask Thy grace again:
From sin withhold me still,
For Jesu's sake alone;

And though inclined to every ill,
I shall consent to none.
To my own net I dare
No longer sacrifice.
Myself to publicans prefer.

Or scorn the slaves of vice:
The slave of vice I am,
If left in danger's hour;
And virtue is an empty name.
Without Thy Spirit's power.

poems.title: Genesis 19: Lord, if indeed from Thee I know
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, if indeed from Thee I know
I cannot my own helper be,
Thy strength in utter weakness show,
Thy grace miraculous in me:
Me from my bosom-lust restrain.
By perfect love's indwelling power;
And I shall never sin again.
Shall never grieve Thy goodness more.

poems.title: Genesis 20:11: thought, surely the fear of God is not in this place
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Forgive my partial selfishness.
My rash, censorious thought:
"Among this people, in this place,
Surely the Lord is not!
If strangers to my sect and name,
Strangers they are to Thee,
God is not fear'd, except by them
Who know and honour me."

poems.title: Genesis 22:2: Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Tremendous oracle Divine!
Who can the harsh command obey!
"That son, that only son of thine,
That son beloved, that Isaac slay!"
Whoe'er the God oi Abraham kijow,
I'heir faith by like obedience prove.
And offering v their Isaacs show
The power supreme of Jesu's love.

Father, Thou call'st me by my name,
Thy sovereign pleasure to fulfil.
And lo, through grace I ready am
To answer all Thy awful will.
By faith I climb the mountain-top,
Thy blessings cheerfully resign,
And yield my dearest comforts up
A bleeding sacrifice Divine.

poems.title: Genesis 22:10: Resolved, O God, with all to part
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Resolved, O God, with all to part,
I bring the victim crown'd.
The dearest partner of my heart
Is on the altar bound!
Spirit and soul asunder tear,
I say. Thy will be done;
And thus, by Thee required, I bare
Mine arm to slay my son!

poems.title: Genesis 22:9, 10: Abraham bound Isaac his son, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let angels wonder at the sight!
Fond Abraham's laughter and delight
Is sacrificed at God's command:
The church's hope, behold him lie,
The promised heir, prepared to die.
To die by a paternal hand!
One only act did this exceed,
When Christ, our Sacrifice indeed.
Was by His Father's goodness given,
Deliver'd up for all to' atone,
His Son beloved, His only Son,
The Lord, the joy of earth and heaven!

poems.title: Genesis 22:12: Safely we may our Isaacs give
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Safely we may our Isaacs give,
And leave them on the altar laid:
If best for us that they should live,
A way for their deliverance made
Shall lift our hearts to things above.
And perfect us in heavenly love.

poems.title: Genesis 22:16–18: Because thou hast done this thing, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Was not our father Abraham tried,
And found completely justified,
By offering up his only son?
The Lord His faithful servant bless'd,
His offspring as the stars increased.
Because he had this action done:
The blessing of the promised Seed
(Received like Isaac from the dead)
Through him to all mankind is given;
And all who with their darlings part,
Shall find the Blessing in their heart,
Joy, righteousness, and Christ, and heaven.

poems.title: Genesis 22:18: Who that promised Seed receive
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who that promised Seed receive,
They the truth Divine confess,
Happy they in Jesus live.
Conscious of their happiness:
Yes, we know the grace bestow'd,
(When He doth His Son impart)
Feel the favour of our God,
Feel the image in our heart.

poems.title: Genesis 23:20: Acquiring h s first spot of ground
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Acquiring h s first spot of ground,
A burying-place the patriarch found:
May I, like him, a stranger rove,
Heir of the promised land above;
The settlement on earth I crave,
The sole possession is — a grave!

poems.title: Genesis: Is God's peculiar people mine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Is God's peculiar people mine?
To them I then sliall be
Gather'd beneath the Saviour's sign,
And Christ in glory see.
Gather'd into the church above,
Whoe'er to Christ belong
Shall meet to sing the song of love.
The Lamb's eternal song.

poems.title: Genesis 27:15: Father, to that first-born of Thine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, to that first-born of Thine
Thou hast the blessing given,
The power, and dignity Divine,
The' inheritance of heaven.
O how shall I the younger son
The Elder's right obtain?
I'll put my Brother's raiment on.
And thus the blessing gain.

poems.title: Genesis 27: Father, I joyfully believe
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)

poems.title: Genesis 27:36: Hast thou not a blessing for me?
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
My Saviour, my God,
I trust in Thy blood.
To bring me the blessing on many bestow'd:
For all it is free.
Though purchased by Thee,
And I know it is mine, when my Lord is in me.

poems.title: Genesis 27:41: Esau hated jacob, because of the blessing, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Hated by fiends and men, who feel
Our sins through Christ forgiven.
We glory to be cursed by hell,
For being bless'd by heaven.

poems.title: Genesis 28:12, 13: What doth the ladder mean
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What doth the ladder mean,
Sent down from the Most High?
Fasten'd to earth its foot is seen,
Its summit to the sky:
Lo! up and down the scale
The angels swiftly move,
And God, the great Invisible,
Himself appears above!

Jesus that ladder is.
The' incarnate Deity,
Partaker of celestial bliss
And human misery;
Sent from His high abode,
To sleeping mortals given.
He stands, and man unites to God,
And earth connects with heaven.

poems.title: Genesis 28: Let Jacob's favour'd race
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let Jacob's favour'd race
The wondrous scale approve.

Through which alone we have access
To that bright throne above:
The foot on earth is fix'd.
He in our nature dwells.

Sinners and God He stands betwixt,
And God to man reveals.
The top our faith adores,
The top transcends our sight,
Above all earthly things it soar.s.
And all created height!
His glorious majesty
Our heavenly Lord maintains,
As God He dwells above the sky,
As God for ever reigns.

poems.title: Genesis 28: Pursue the mystery
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Pursue the mystery!
The duteous angel-train
Ascending and descending see
Upon the Son of Man!
The ministerial host
Their heavenly Lord attend;
And us who in His mercy trust
He bids His guards defend:

Through Christ our living way
Sent from above they come,
Our spirits safely to convey
To our eternal home:
They watch each glorious heir,
And when from flesh released,
Up to our Father's throne they bear,
And lodge us in His breast.

poems.title: Genesis 28: Redeemer of mankind
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Redeemer of mankind.
Who on Thy name rely
A constant intercourse we find
Open'd 'twixt earth and sky:
Mercy and grace and peace
Descend through Thee alone,
And Thou dost all our services
Present before the throne.
On us Thy Father's love
Is for Thy sake bestow'd;

Thou art our Advocate above,
Thou art our way to God:
Our way to God we trace,
And, through Thy name forgiven,
From step to step, from grace to grace.
On Thee we climb to heaven.

poems.title: Genesis 28:17: In heavenly majesty and grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
In heavenly majesty and grace
When God doth to His church appear,
We cry, How dreadful is this place!
W ith holy joy, and humble fear,
That dares not in His presence move,
Our souls adore His glorious love.

poems.title: Genesis 28:17: This is none other but the house of God, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Our hearts o'erflow with praise and prayer,
Whene'er He doth His Son reveal,
His presence makes a Bethel there.
His glory doth the temple fill,
We find in Christ to sinners given
The house of God, the gate of heaven!

poems.title: Genesis 30:1: Give me children, or else I die
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
She could not live, she could not rest
Content, if children were denied:
And lo! indulged in her request,
She bore her second son, and died!

poems.title: Genesis 32:10: Less than Thy least of mercies
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Less than Thy least of mercies I
Myself would every moment feel,
Worthy the second death to die.
Worthy the hottest flames of hell;
I would the smallest crumbs of grace
Beneath the Master's table eat,
And till I see Thy glorious face
Lie here, self-loathing at Thy feet.

poems.title: Genesis 42:21: How often, Lord, hath trouble brought
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How often, Lord, hath trouble brought
My long-forgotten sins to mind!
And by this fresh affliction taught,
I tremble at the woes behind:
But while I guilty, guilty plead,
O do not from Thy presence cast,
Nor leave me at my greatest need,
To perish in my sins at last.

Ah! rid me of this fear and doubt,
Doubt that I shall not persevere,
Fear that my sin will find me out,
And plague with all Thy judgments here.
Jesus, whom I to death have sold;
My guilty burden to remove.
Tell me. Thou hast redeem'd of old,
And save me by Thy dying love.

poems.title: Genesis 46:4: Jesus, I cast my soul on Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, I cast my soul on Thee,
Mighty and merciful to save:
Thou wilt to death go down with me.
And gently lay me in the grave:
This body there shall rest in hope,
This body which the wornls destroy;
For surely Thou wilt bring me up
To glorious life, and endless joy.

poems.title: Genesis 46:4: And Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
A Few more days preserve me here;
And when from earth my spirit flies,
O let a child of mine be near,
A child of God, to close mine eyes!

poems.title: Genesis 47:29: Before its strong arrest I feel
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Before its strong arrest I feel.
Give me my death's approach to see,
And having lived to serve Thy will,
Lord, let me then depart in Thee.

poems.title: Genesis 48:16: The great redeeming Angel, Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The great redeeming Angel, Thee,
O Jesus, I confess:
Who hast through life deliver'd me,
Thou wilt my offspring bless;
Thou that hast borne my sins away,
My children's sins remove,
And bring them through their evil day,
To sing Thy praise above.

poems.title: Genesis 48:16: Mv name be on the children? no
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Mv name be on the children? no:
But mark them, Lord, with Thine:
Let all the heavenly offspring know
By characters Divine;
Partakers of Thy nature make.
Partakers of Thy Son,
And then the heirs of glory take
To Thine eternal throne.

poems.title: Genesis 49:4: Unstable as water, thou shall not excel
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Unstable, Lord, by nature 1,
And weak as water am,
Till Thou empower me to rely
On Thine almighty name:
Excelling then in holiness
I never shall remove.
Firm as the Rock of Israel's peace.
The rock of heavenly love.

poems.title: Genesis 49: Soon as Shiloh came, L tJnvs
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Soon as Shiloh came, L tJnvs
Beheld their sceptre broke,
Who their heavenly King refuse
Must wear a foreign yoke:
But when David's Son we bless,
And sing hosannahs to our Lord,
Then our joyful hearts confess
The kingdom is restored.

poems.title: Genesis 49:10: Unto Him shall t)ie gathering of the people be
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Centre of Unity,
Our precious Corner-stone,
Collect Thy people into Thee,
And perfect them in one;
Break down the wall between.
Even as Thou hast foretold.

And all the wandering sheep bring in,
And make us all one fold.
lo-
Object of the world's desire
Jesus we fain would see,
O might every heart aspire
With ours to rest in Thee!

O might all our Saviour know.
Where'er by sin or Satan driven,
Gather'd to Thy church below,
And to Thy throne in heaven!

poems.title: Genesis 49:18: Jesus, throughout my threescore years
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, throughout my threescore years
I have for Thy salvation stay'd,
And leaving now the vale of tears,
I dare not doubt Thy promised aid;
Kept by Thy power from acting sin.
The end of faith I here shall see,
Thy perfect righteousness brought in,
And pure in heart return to Thee.
Genesis xlix. lo — Exodus i. lo.

poems.title: Genesis 49:19: Troops of violent sins and lusts
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Troops of violent sins and lusts
Have oft my soul subdued,
Yet my soul in Jesus trusts,
And His victorious blood;
Held by Him, I hold Him fast,
In humble confidence to prove
More than conqueror at last
Through my Redeemer's love.

poems.title: Genesis 49:33: Jacob gathered up his feet into the bed, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Shrinking from the cold hand of death,
I too shall gather up my feet,
Shall soon resign this fleeting breath.
And die, my father's God to meet;
Number'd among Thy people, I
Expect with joy '''hy face to see.
Because Thou didst for sinners die.
Thou wilt in death remember me.

poems.title: Exodus 1:10: Let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Stii.i, to make our numbers less.
The world their wisdom try,
But the more the world oppress,
The more we multiply:
Though to sin and Satan sold,
We soon to Christ their foe shall fall.
Fight against our masters old.
And more than conquer all.

poems.title: Exodus 1:13: The world and their infernal god
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The world and their infernal god
Have ruled us with an iron rod,
And long our slavish souls have been
Gall'd by the rigorous yoke of sin:
Yet drudging on with abject fear
We served our haughty lords severe,
And hardly daring to complain,
We kiss'd the rod, and hugg'd the chain.

poems.title: Exodus 3:2: See here the miracle renew'd
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
See here the miracle renew'd,
A bush that doth the fire abide,
A burning bush, bedew'd with blood,
A church, preserved in Jesu's side!

poems.title: Exodus 3:6: Moses hid his face, for he was afraid, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thus may I humbly hide my face,
When God vouchsafes to' appear,
And never count it genuine grace
Which is not mix'd with fear.

poems.title: Exodus 3:7, 8: Jesus, Thou hear'st Thine Israel groan
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thou hear'st Thine Israel groan.
Our sorrows all to Thee are known,
(Who struggle from our sins to part.
From man's and Satan's tyranny,)
And while Thou dost our sufferings see,
Thy pitying eye affects Thy heart:

The cruel taskmasters oppress,
Till Thou our captive souls release,
With outstretch'd arm and mighty hand,
Now, Lord, in our behalf come down.
Thine arm extend, Thy strength put on,
And bring us to the promised land.

poems.title: Exodus 3:8: To bring them up unto a good land, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Faithful and True, we trust in Thee;
Thou art come down to set us free
From Pharaoh's yoke, and sin's command:
Now bring us forth, Thy chosen race.
Now in the land of promise place,
The good, and large, and pleasant land!

Good; for 'tis there our Lord we find,
And large enough for all mankind,
With honey and with milk o'erflow'd;
The land which heaven delights to bless,
The land of rest and righteousness,
The earthly paradise of God.

poems.title: Exodus 3:14: Being of beings, make
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Being of beings, make
In me Thy nature known.
Who didst Thyself my nature take
In Thine incarnate Son;
Thy majesty display.
Thy name on me impress.
And what I am, my soul shall say,
I am by Jesu's grace.

poems.title: Exodus 4:10: How ready is the man to go
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How ready is the man to go
Whom God hath never sent!
How timorous, diffident, and slow
His chosen instrument!
Lord, if from Thee this mark I have
Of a true messenger,
By whom Thou wilt Thy people save,
And let me always fear.
Slow of speech, and slower still
Of heart, alas! am I,
Cannot utter what I feel,
Or speak to the Most High:
But I to my Brother look,
Mighty both in word and deed:
He my cause hath undertook.
And lives for me to plead.
Jesus is my great High-priest,
Who doth in heaven appear;
Him presenting my request,
The Father loves to hear:
Jesus, (if His wrath arise.

And justice on the sinner frown,)
Jesus speaks and pacifies,
And prays His anger own.
Jesus is a mouth to me,
Expressing all my wants;

God is vanquish'd by His plea,
And every blessing grants:
O how eloquent His blood
Which echoing from the throne Divine.
Tells me, I am dear to God,
And all He is is mine.

poems.title: Exodus 4:11: Maker of the mouth of man
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Maker of the mouth of man,
And Opener too, the Lord
Sends the dumb His will to' explain.
And minister His word;
Deaf, to a deaf world I go
With joyful news of sin forgiven.
Blind, at Jesu's call, I show
The blind their way to heaven.

poems.title: Exodus 5:17: Ve are idle, ye are idle, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Soon as in earnest we begin
Our God to serve and please.
Our labour to escape from sin
Is counted idleness:
Yet will we labour on, till He,
Our great Redeemer come.
And set our hearts at liberty.
And take His servants home.

poems.title: Exodus 5:23: Sure token of redemption near
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Sure token of redemption near,
Our servitude is more severe,
And heavier is our chain,
Thou hast not rescued us at all;
Of harder tasks, and sorer thrall,
More deeply we complain.

By this assuredly we know
The tyrant soon shall let us go,
Compell'd by power Divine;
We then to hberty restored
Shall worship our redeeming Lord,
And live for ever Thine.

poems.title: Exodus 6:6: Witness of my extreme distress
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Witness of my extreme distress
How long shall I these burdens feel,
Egyptian burdens, that depress,
And sink my abject soul to hell!
If Thou Thy promised help defer,
And suffer me in sin to' expire,
I must a hotter furnace bear,
A furnace of eternal fire.

poems.title: Exodus 6:7: Jesus, Lord, to Thee I look
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Lord, to Thee I look,
Crush'd by my oppressor's yoke;
From this grievous slavery
Thou alone canst set me free:
Then, and only then shall I
Thy redemption testify,
Lighten'd of my guilty load,
Know, Thou art my Lord, my God!

poems.title: Exodus 7:12: Men in vain with fiends combine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Men in vain with fiends combine
Thy servants to withstand:
Can they match the rod Divine
With the magician's wand?

poems.title: Exodus 7: Truth prevails, and conquers all
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Truth prevails, and conquers all,
Like Aaron's rod-devouring rod;
Sin, the world, and Satan fall
Before the church of God.
So, when the Saviour shows His face.
And in our hearts vouchsafes to shine,
Our sins are swallow'd up by grace.
Our creature-loves by love divine.

poems.title: Exodus 7:20: The waters were turned to blood
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
He turn'd their water into blood,
When vengeance was His dread design:
But, thanks to the incarnate God,
He turn'd our water into wine!

poems.title: Exodus 8:15: How oft have I, like Pharaoh, proved
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How oft have I, like Pharaoh, proved
A penitent in pain.
And when I saw the plague removed,
Return'd to sin again!
Hardening my heart, I still rebel.
The worse for each reprieve:
But try if grace cannot prevail.
And now, O Lord, forgive.

poems.title: Exodus 8:19: This is the finger of God!
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Till by Thy mighty signs compell'd.
The world. Thine old Egyptian foe,
The persecutor scorns to yield,
And will not let Thy people go.
Jesus appear, extort the word
From those who now Thy plagues defy,
"This is the finger of the Lord,
This is the work of the Most High!"

poems.title: Exodus 8:25: Pharaoh said, Go ye, sacrifice to your God, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thy people, Lord, if Thou command,
Are tolerated by Thy foe:
We sacrifice, or in the land,
Or to the fields and deserts go:
This liberty to serve our God
With faith unfeign'd, and conscience pure,
By providential love bestow'd,
Let it from age to age endure.

poems.title: Exodus 9:12: There needed, Lord, no act of Thine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
There needed, Lord, no act of Thine,
If Pharaoh had an heart like mine:
One moment leave me but alone.
And mine alas, is turn'd to stone!
Thus if the blessing Thou restrain,
The earth is harden'd by the rain
Withheld: and thus, if God depart,
Jehovah hardens Pharaoh's heart!

poems.title: Exodus 9:14: I will send all My plagues upon thine heart
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
If punish'd after my desert,
Inflicted on my senseless heart
I shall Thy judgments bear;
(The sorest plagues Thou hast to send,)
Presumption now, and at my end
The blackness of despair.

poems.title: Exodus 9:17: Such is the stubbornness of man
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Such is the stubbornness of man!
So deep in me the evil lies!
Chastised a thousand times in vain,
I still against Thy judgments rise:
Not all Thy judgments can convert
This sinner, or this sin remove,
Unless Thou find it in Thy heart
To soften mine by pardoning love.

poems.title: Exodus: How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself before, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Till Tophet takes me in,
I shall rebellious prove,
Unless I feel a power within
Of self-abasing love;
Unless my Saviour's grace
Constrain me to submit,
Grieved that by sin I marr'd His face.
And pierced His hands and feet!

poems.title: Exodus 10:17: Forgive my sin only this once
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Times without number have I pray'd.
This only once forgive.
Relapsing, when Thy hand was stay'd
And suffer'd me to live:
Yet now the kingdom of Thy peace.
Lord, to my heart restore,
Forgive my vain repentances,
And bid me sin no more.

poems.title: Exodus 10:17: Take away this death
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Alas, when seeming to repent.
My first concern has been
How to escape the punishment,
More than the guilt of sin!
But now, O God, for grace I pray,
For more than life I cry,
O take this death of sin away,
And let my body die!

poems.title: Exodus 10:23: While the world is wrapp'd in night
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
While the world is wrapp'd in night,
Nor yet the darkness feel,
We the children of the light
In joy and comfort dwell;
Walking in the light of grace,
A brighter day we soon shall prove.
Dazzled with the glorious blaze
Of God's eternal love.

poems.title: Exodus 12:7: Christ, our Passover, is slain
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Christ, our Passover, is slain,
To set His people free,
Free from sin's Egyptian chain.
And Pharaolis tyranny:
Lord, that we may now depart,
And truly serve our pardoning God,
Sprinkle every house and heart
With Thine atoning blood.

poems.title: Exodus 12:13: The blood shall be to you for a token, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let the angel of the Lord
His awful charge fulfil,
Let His pestilential sword
The first-born victims kill;
Safe in snares and deaths we dwell.
Protected by that crimson sign.
From the rage of earth and hell.
And from the wrath Divine.

poems.title: Exodus 12:13: Wilt Thou not a difference make
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Wilt Thou not a difference make
Betwixt Thy friend and foe,
Vengeance on the' Egyptians take.
And grace to Israel show?
Know'st Thou not, most righteous God,
We on the paschal Lamb rely?
See us cover'd with the blood,
And pass Thy people by.

poems.title: Exodus 13:17: How wisely. Saviour, doth Thy love
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How wisely. Saviour, doth Thy love
In our behalf appear,
Unequal enemies remove.
And trials too severe!
Thou dost Thy feeble people hide,
While unprepared for war.
Nor e'er permit us to be tried
Above what we can bear.

poems.title: Exodus 13:21: Captain of IsracPs host, and Guide
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Captain of IsracPs host, and Guide
Of all who seek that land above,
Beneath Thy shadow we abide,
The cloud of Thy protecting love,
Our strength Thy grace, our rale Thy word.
Our end, the glory of the Lord.

By Thine unerring Spirit led.
We shall not in the desert stray,
The light of man's direction need,
Or miss our providential way,
As far from danger as from fear.
While Love, almighty Love, is near.

poems.title: Exodus 13:22: Enter'd on the vast wilderness
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Enter'd on the vast wilderness,
Jesus, Thy helpless people see,
With comfort and protection bless
Thy gospel-church, redeem'd by Thee;
A cloud by day, a fire by night,
Defend us with Thy heavenly light.

Take not the sacred signs away,
The tokens of Thy guardian power;
Preserved by night, refresh'd by day.
Baptized in many a gracious shower,
Cover us with Thy cloudy shrine.
And in Thy fiery column shine.

To all believers visible.
Who in Thy pardoning love confide,
With us Thou promisest to dwell,
And to that pleasant country guide,
Where Israel finds, of Thee possess'd,
The land of everlasting rest.

poems.title: Exodus 14:13: Out of the iron furnace brought
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Out of the iron furnace brought,
Whither shall we for refuge fly?
Ere by our fierce pursuers caught,
Jesus, Thou hear'st our suppliant cry;
Thou bidd'st us humbly wait on Thee:
And lo, in patient faith we stand,
The wonders of Thy grace to see,
The saving power of Thy right-hand.

poems.title: Exodus 14:15: Without a voice he cried
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Without a voice he cried.
Without a word he pray'd:
O might that Spirit in me abide
Which still demands Thine aid!
Jesus, Thy church to save.
Appear as heretofore.
And bring us through the parted wave
To the celestial shore.

poems.title: Exodus 14:15: Forward! but whither shall we go
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Forward! but whither shall we go?
The desert is on either side,
Behind us the Egyptian foe,
Before, the interposing tide!
Yet while we Thy command obey,
Our road impassable pursue,
The ocean yields an open way.
And lets Thy ransom'd people through.

poems.title: Exodus 14:19: The angel removed, and went behind them, Gt'c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Angel Divine, who goest before
Thine Israel in protecting power,
The cloudy pillar interpose,
To stop the fury of our foes,
Behind our threaten'd camp appear.
And let 1'hy gloiy guard our rear.

poems.title: Exodus 14:20: It was a cloud and darkness to them, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Shout to the Lord, who stands between.
Whose symbols by our faith are seen!
We now behold His presence shine,
The glorious Shechinah Divine:
Its light to us the pillar shows,
And turns its darkness on our foes.

poems.title: Exodus 14:20: The one came not near the other all the night
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Why should believing Israel fear
The tyrant with his armies near?
In darkness wrapp'd we wait the day:
And till the Lord His arm display,
They cannot reach (for God is nigher)
Or wound us through our 'all of Fire!

poems.title: Exodus 14:24, 25: The Lord looked n)ito the host, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O Almighty Lord, rebuke
Our foes' outrageous boast,
Through the fiery column look,
And blast the murderers' host;
Force them, Jesus, to confess
Jehovah doth for Israel X.;
Then the' infernal powers oppress
With everlasting night.

poems.title: Exodus 15:1: In Moses's song The Lamb we proclaim
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
In Moses's song The Lamb we proclaim:
The praise doth belong To Jesus's name!
Triumphantly glorious Our Jesus hath been,
And more than victorious O'er hell, earth, and sin.

The world and its prince No longer are found;
Our tyrannous sins Are buried and drown'd,
O'erwhelm'd by a motion Of Moses's rod.
And plunged in the ocean Of Jesus's blood!

poems.title: Exodus 15:2: The Lord is my strength and song, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The Lord is my might: Redeem'd by His grace,
I pay Him His right, I sing of His praise:
Our Lord's habitation, In us He shall dwell,
And all His salvation To sinners reveal.

poems.title: Exodus 15:4: Our sins are o'erthrown, Which rose against Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Our sins are o'erthrown, Which rose against Thee,
They sank as a stone Into the red-sea:
Thou, Lord, hast forgot 'em. As hid from Thine eyes.
And sunk to the bottom They never shall rise.

poems.title: Exodus 15:18: The Lord shall reign for ever, and ever
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The Lord is king till that great day,
When all His foes are slain:
When heaven and earth are pass'd away,
He shall for ever reign:
And we shall by His side sit down,
His praises to repeat,
Or cast our crowns before the throne,
And wonder at His feet.

poems.title: Exodus 15:25: The Lord hath to His servants shown
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The Lord hath to His servants shown
The tree on which our Saviour died,
Its virtue in our souls made known.
Its bleeding balm, by faith applied,
Converts our nature's bitterness
To sweetest streanis of heavenly grace.

poems.title: Exodus 15:26: Physician of the sin-sick soul
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Physician of the sin-sick soul.
Thou heal'st us when Thou dost forgive.
Thy mercy makes, and keeps us whole,
In perfect health it bids us live,
In perfect holiness renew'd.
And fiU'd with all the life of God.

poems.title: Exodus 16:15: Truth of the legal sacrament
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Truth of the legal sacrament,
He was the manna which He sent:
And daily still to Israel given,
The living Bread comes down from heaven.
That mortals who through faith receive.
By Christ eternally may live.

poems.title: Exodus 16: Pardon admits of no degrees
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Pardon admits of no degrees,
Whether we more rejoice, or less.
But who the Bread of life receive,
As really by faith I live,
As much, as perfectly forgiven.
Through Christ, as the first saint in heaven.

poems.title: Exodus 16: Tis not so much the bulk of grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Tis not so much the bulk of grace
God minds, as the sincerity;
Our goodness, whether more or less.
Is equal all, O Lord, to Thee.

Of the true manna from above
Who gathers much, has none to spare;
And with the smallest taste of love
Fill'd, as with all Thy heaven, we are.

How can we then complain or boast.
Who feel our interest in that blood j
Possessing either least or most.
By faith we all are sons of God.

Fathers their heavenly Father knew
Whom children have but lately known,
Yet proving God benignly true.
Fathers, and babes in Christ, are one.

poems.title: Exodus 16:20: Not so the true immortal Bread
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Not so the true immortal Bread,
By which our hungry souls are fed:
If kept by us it always be.
It keeps us from corruption free:
And soon the' incorruptible grace
Shall these vile putrid bodies raise,
Long as our heavenly Food to' endure.
And pure as God Himself is pure.

poems.title: Exodus 16:27: On the seventh day they found none
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
But on the day of sacred rest
Above His ancient people bless'd,
Who call our dying Lord to mind,
We each a double portion find,
Gather the manna from above,
And banquet on His richest love.

poems.title: Exodus 17:3: Would God Himself His people lead
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Would God Himself His people lead,
Intending to betray,
His people out of Egypt freed
With thirst and famine slay?
Our souls into this wilderness
Thou couldst not. Lord, allure.
By keeping back Thy special grace
To make our ruin sure.

poems.title: Exodus 17:6: Thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Saviour, from Thine open side,
When smote with Moses" rod,
Issued forth the sacred tide
Which slakes our thirst for God:
Rock of never-failing love.
Let Thy refreshing streams pursue.
Till with Thee we drink above
The wine for ever new.

poems.title: Exodus 17:7: Not all the miracles of love
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Not all the miracles of love
Which Thou hast wrought for me
Can out of this base heart remove
Its incredulity:
One hour without the sweets of grace
In peevish haste I mourn,
"The Lord hath left me in distress,
And never will return."
vol. IX. E

But, O Thou patient God, forgive
A murmuring Israelite
And learn me how to wait and grieve
When Thou art out of sight;
By dryness tried, and want, and pain,
I fain in Thee would trust.
Most present with Thy people then
When Thou chastisest most.

poems.title: Exodus 17:10: Joshua fought with Amalek: and Moses, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Two shadows of one substance see!
The Lord, who set His people free,
Persists to save the ransom'd race;
Jesus doth all the work alone.
Our Captain and High-priest in one.
In Joshua fights, in Moses prays.

High on the hill behold Him stand.
The rod of wonder in His hand;
His prayer inclines the hovering scale:
And through our Advocate above.
And through His Spirit of faith and love,
His fighting church shall still prevail.

poems.title: Exodus 17:11: When Moses held tip his hand, Israel, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Long as our hands are lifted up.
We triumph o'er sin, earth, and hell;
But when in prayer we faint and droop,
Our rallying foes again prevail:
O Thou whose hand is stretch'd out still.
Our sinking hands confirm, and stay,
And wrestle for us on the hill,
And in us here incessant pray.
Exodus xvii. lO — xx. i.

poems.title: Exodus 17:12, 13: His hands were steady until the going, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Steady in continued prayer
Howe'er our hands may be,
We QViX Joshua' s praise declare,
Who gets the victory:
He shall Amalek o'erthrow,
Before our sun of life goes down.
By His Spirit destroy the foe,
And crown us with His crown.

poems.title: Exodus 17:14: I will utterly put out the remembrance, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, we dare believe on Thee,
Against this Amalek within,
He soon extirpated shall be,
The name, the last remains of sin;
In all to whom Thy nature's given,
He perishes — on this side heaven.

poems.title: Exodus 19:4: I bare you on eagles wings, and brought you, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
As an eagle cleaves the air,
Whose wings support her young,
Jesus doth His people bear.
As swift, as smooth, as strong!
Saviour, urge Thy rapid flight.
Soar to that sublime abode,
Bear us far above all height,
And bring us home to God.

poems.title: Exodus 20:1: God spake all these words
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Would (lod. His greatness to display,
In)practicable laws enjoin,
Laws which we never can obey
With all the helps of grace Divine?
Nay, Thou most gracious Lord and just,
We know Thy sanctifying will,
And through Thy Spirit's power we trust
All Thy commandments to fulfil.

poems.title: Exodus 20:24: In all places where I record My name, I will, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
To the temple of the Lord
Where He doth His name record,
Us who humbly still repair,
Still He meets, and blesses there:

Find we in the hallow'd place
Blessings of peculiar grace;
Double power His word imparts,
Prays His Spirit in our hearts.

Strangely at His table fed,
Nourish'd with immortal Bread,
While He doth Himself make known,
Christ, we cry, is all our own.

Whom we everywhere may find;
Chiefly in the means enjoin'd,
With His gracious fulness given,
Jesus lifts our souls to heaven.

poems.title: Exodus 22:18: "Thou shalt not suffer her to live:"
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
"Thou shalt not suffer her to live:"
But Deists can a witch reprieve.
And Britain's senators reply
"Thou shalt not suffer her to die."

poems.title: Exodus 23:2: Better be wise among the few
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Better be wise among the few.
Than with the many stray,
Than a mad multitude pursue
Down the destructive way:
While millions, blind in sin, rush on,
Like Lot in Sodom dwell,
And rather go to heaven alone,
Than with a world to hell.

poems.title: Exodus 23:22: What Thou hast spoke I have not done
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What Thou hast spoke I have not done;
Yet Jesus takes the sinner's part,
With me, in Thy beloved Son,
Well pleased, and reconciled Thou art:
My God in Christ the sinner's Friend,
Thou wilt my sure Defender be,
Wilt with my stronger foes contend,
And more than conquer all for me.

poems.title: Exodus 32:10: Let Me alone, (amazing word!)
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let Me alone, (amazing word!)
The' Almighty to His creature cries!
His creature binds the' almighty Lord,
And will not let His anger rise:
Jehovah must the rebels spare,
While Moses doth for mercy groan:
Jehovah hears, in Moses' prayer,
The pleading Spirit of His Son.

poems.title: Exodus 32:34: But canst Thou not the whole remit
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
But canst Thou not the whole remit,
Nor ever visit for my sin?
See the poor leper at Thy feet,
Exert Thy power to make me clean.
Chase by a touch my guilt away.
And take me from the evil day.

poems.title: Exodus 33:18: T beseech Thee, shew mc Thy glory
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, show to me Thy glory,
Prostrate at Thy gracious throne,
Make Thy goodness pass before me,
All Thy goodness, in Thy Son.
By Thy purifying presence
All my guilt and sin remove.
Speak it to mine inmost essence
Christ is God, and God is love.

poems.title: Exodus 34:5: The Lord descended in the cloud, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Great God, to me the sight afford
To him of old allow'd.
And let my faith behold its Lord
Descending in the cloud:
In that revealing Spirit come down.
Thine attributes proclaim.
And to mine inmost soul make known
The glories of Thy name.

poems.title: Exodus 34:6: Jehovah-el, I Thee adore
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jehovah-el, I Thee adore,
Who gav'st my soul to be,
Fountain of being, and of power,
And great in majesty;
The Lord, the mighty God Thou art:
Yet let me rather prove
That name inspoken to my heart,
That favourite name of Love.

poems.title: Exodus 34:6: Merciful God, Thyself proclaim
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Merciful God, Thyself proclaim
In this polluted breast,
Mercy. is Thy distinguish'd name.
Which suits a sinner best:
Our misery doth for pity call,
Our sin implores Thy grace,
And Thou art merciful to all
Our lost apostate race.

poems.title: Exodus 34:6: Gracious, long-suffering
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thy causeless unexhausted love,
Unmerited and free,
Delights our evil to remove,
And help our misery
Thou waitest to be gracious still,
Thou dost with sinners bear,
That saved, we may Thy goodness feel,
And all Thy grace declare.

poems.title: Exodus 34:6: Thy goodness and Thy truth to me
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thy goodness and Thy truth to me,
To every soul abound,
A vast unfathomable sea.
Where all our thoughts are drown'd;
Its streams the whole creation reach,
So plenteous is the store,
Enough for all, enough for each,
Enough for evermore.

poems.title: Exodus 34:6: Abundant in truth
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Faithful, O Lord, Thy mercies are,
A rock that cannot move,
A thousand promises declare
Thy constancy of love:
Throughout the universe it reigns
Unalterably sure.
And while the truth of God remains,
The goodness must endure.

poems.title: Exodus 34:7: Keeping mercy for thousands
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Reserves of unexhausted grace
Are treasured up in Thee,
For myriads of the fallen race;
For all mankind, and me;
The flowing stream continues full,
Till time its course hath run,
And while eternal ages roll,
Thy mercy shall flow on.

poems.title: Exodus 34:7: Forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Merciful God, long-suffering, kind,
To me Thy name is show'd;
But sinners most exult to find
Thou art a jDardoning God:
Our sins in deed, and word, and thought,
Thou freely dost forgive
For us Thou by Thy blood hast bought,
And died, that I may live.

poems.title: Exodus 34:7: Yet wilt Thou not the guilty clear
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Yet wilt Thou not the guilty clear.
If we to sin return:
Thy wrath vindictively severe
From age to age shall burn;
Unless our sinful misery
We self-condemn'd bemoan.
And find an Advocate in Thee
Before Thy Father's throne.

poems.title: Exodus 34:28: Moses fasted forty days
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Moses fasted forty days.
Nor miss'd his outward food,
Nourish'd by his Maker's grace.
The partial sight of God:
We shall live completely bless'd,
When face to face our God we see,
On the blissful vision feast
To all eternity.

poems.title: Exodus 34:29: Thine image if Thou stamp on me
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thine image if Thou stamp on me,
Let others. Lord, the brightness see
By me unseen, unknown S'
Nor let them on a creature gaze,
But all the glory of Thy grace
Ascribe to God alone.

poems.title: Exodus 34:33: He put a veil on his face
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Before he put the covering on.
They could not on his visage gaze:
But brighter through the veil it shone,

poems.title: Exodus 34: The blessings God on man bestows
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The blessings God on man bestows.
The things He doth, 'tis gooil to tell:
Tis good, at times which Jesus shows,
Our glittering graces to conceal.

poems.title: Exodus 34:34: Will a meek, modest man of God
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Will a meek, modest man of God
Rejoice to make the fairest show.
Expose his graces to the crowd.
And charm the dazzled world below?
Or rather take with jealous fear
The veil of true humility,
And glorious as he is appear
To none but that all-seeing Eye? J

poems.title: Leviticus 2:11: Thee that my sacrifice may please
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thee that my sacrifice may please,
Assist me, Lord, to lay aside
The leaven of all wickedness.
All spite, hypocrisy, and pride:
Anger, and doubt, and anxious care
Out of my heart if Thou remove,
I '11 lift up holy hands in prayer
With truth, sincerity, and love.

poems.title: Leviticus 2:11: From nature's different mixtures free
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
From nature's different mixtures free,
Honey the joy, and grief the leaven,
I bring my sacrifice to Thee,
Jesus, my great High-priest in heaven:
That God my offering may receive,
I set my heart on things above.
The sour of worldly sorrow leave.
The cloying sweets of creature-love.

poems.title: Leviticus 2:13: With all thine offerings thou shall offer salt
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Unsavoury all our offerings are.
Till acceptable through Thy Son:
But hear well-pleased our praise and prayer
Presented in His name alone:
The salt we borrow from our Lord,
His meritorious righteousness.
And every deed, and thought,.and word
Is season'd now with Jesu's grace.

poems.title: Leviticus 6:13: I O Thou who earnest from above
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I O Thou who earnest from above.
The pure, celestial fire to' impart.
Kindle a flame of sacred love
On the mean altar of my heart;

There let it for Thy glory burn
With inextinguishable blaze,
And trembling to its Source return,
In humble prayer, and fervent praise.

Jesus, confirm my heart's desire
To work, and speak, and think for Thee;
Still let me guard the holy fire.

And still stir up Thy gift in me:
Ready for all Thy perfect will,
My acts of faith and love repeat,
Till death Thy endless mercies seal,
And make my sacrifice complete.

poems.title: Leviticus 8:8: Our High-priest the breast-plate wears
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Our High-priest the breast-plate wears.
His IsracPs Oracle,
Full of truth and grace declares
The Father's perfect will,
Makes His people priests and kings,
His fulness to His church imparts,
The Urim and the Thummitn brings
To all believing hearts.

poems.title: Leviticus 8: Who for us went up, we know
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who for us went up, we know,
Resides on earth again,
Lights, perfections to bestow
On poor rebellious men;
Gifts for men He now receives
Our prevalent High-priest above,
Now into our bosom gives
The Spirit of faith and love.

poems.title: Leviticus 8: Faith and love the breast-plate make
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Faith and love the breast-plate make
Of perfect righteousness;
Let us then the blessing take,
Whom God delights to bless:
Beautified my will and mind
With wisdom and integrity,
I shall all perfections find,
When Jesus dwells in me.

poems.title: Leviticus 8: Happy, Lord, Thy people are
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Happy, Lord, Thy people are,
By full possession Thine!
In their faithful hearts they bear
The Oracle Divine,
Thee consult in all their ways,
And all Thy will rejoice to prove,
Answer'd by the light of grace,
And by the truth of love.

poems.title: Leviticus 8:35: Keep the charge of the Lord, that ye die not
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
A Charge to keep I have,
A God to glorify,
A never-dying soul to save.
And fit it for the sky;
To serve the present age.
My calling to fulfil:
O may it all my powers engage
To do my Master's will!

Arm me with jealous care,
As in Thy sight to live,
And O! Thy servant. Lord, prepare
A strict account to give:
Help me to watch and pray,
And on Thyself rely,
Assured, if I my trust betray,
I shall for ever die.

poems.title: Leviticus 9:22: Aaron lift up his hand towards the people, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Aaron lifts up his praying hands,
To show from whence the blessing flow'd.
He craves the grace which Christ commands.
Our great High-priest, who sent of God
Blesses this dear-loved world of His
With glorious everlasting bliss.

Aaron a transient blessing gave,
A mortal, typical high-priest;
Jesus for ever lives, to save
The people He at parting bless'd;
Aaron came down, the blessing given.
His Antitype went up to heaven.

poems.title: Leviticus 9:24: Sent, through Jesus, from the skies
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Sent, through Jesus, from the skies,
Spirit of burning, come;
Kindle on the sacrifice,
And all our sins consume:
While Thou dost Thyself reveal.
Our persons, and our works ai)prove.
All our ravish'd souls shall feel
