The fire of heavenly love.

Father, trusting in Thy Son,
I bow to Jesu's name,
Glows my heart with warmth unknown.
With pure seraphic flame:
Lost in wonder at Thy grace,
I fall the pardoning God before,
Breathe unutterable praise,
And silently adore.

poems.title: Leviticus 10:2: There went out fire from the Lord, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Warm'd by fond nature's wild desire,
I brought strange uncommanded fire:
Inflamed with persecuting zeal,
I served Thee — with the fire of hell:
Yet undevour'd, O God, I sing
Thy grace; and now my offering bring,
Pure incense, kindled from above
By the true fire of Jesu's love.

poems.title: Leviticus 10:3: Aaron held his peace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Why should a living man complain
That sinners are struck dead?
Reprieved myself I still remain,
If punish'd in my seed:
Howe'er Thou deal'st with mine, or me,
O stop the murmuring groan;
Or let my only answer be.
Father, Thy will be done!

poems.title: Leviticus 11:45: Ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Unholy, of an holy God
The people we can never be:.'
But sanctify us by Thy blood,
Jesus, and we Thy face shall see,
Shall bear Thy spotless image here.
And pure before Thy throne appear.

poems.title: Leviticus 17:11: Not the alms, or works of man
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Not the alms, or works of man
Can for his sins atone,
But the Lamb for sinners slain
Hath satisfied alone:
Jesus to His Father paid
The ransom we could never find,
By His blood atonement made
For me, and all mankind.

poems.title: Leviticus: Thou shall )iot hate thy, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Through fear of feeble man,
Through want of social love.
Lord, I have made Thy jjrecept vain.
Neglecting to reprove;
The' offender in mine eye
I suffer to go on,
A thousand sins in him pass'd b-,
And made them all my own.
Ah! save me from a worse extreme,
When sin in others I condemn:
Assist me first to lay aside
The spiteful bitterness of pride,
Reflecting on myself, to see
A soul not half so vile as me,
And then my neighbour to reprove
In meekness, humbleness, and love.

poems.title: Leviticus: Father, let Thy faithfulness
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, let Thy faithfulness
And love in Christ appear,
The true tabernacle place
Among 'i hy people here,
Jesus to Thy church reveal
Delighted with an humble shrine,
Give Him in our hearts to dwell
The Shcchiiiah Divine.

poems.title: Leviticus 26:12: Walking in the church below
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Walking in the church below,
The garden of the Lord,
Jesus, by Thy presence show
Our paradise restored:
Grant us fellowship with Thee,
Our God in all our souls reside,
Then we shall Thy people be
For ever sanctified.

poems.title: Leviticus 26:13: I have broken the bands of your yoke, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, if Thou from me hast broke
The power of outward sin,
Burst this Babylo?iish yoke,
And make me free within;
Bid mine inbred sin depart.
And I Thine utmost word shall prove,
Upright both in life and heart,
And perfected in love.

poems.title: Leviticus 26:41, 42: If they then accept of the punishment, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, I do at last relent,
My length of painful punishment
I do as just receive;
Think of the covenant in Thy Son,
And O! forget what I have done,
And all my sins forgive.

poems.title: Numbers 6:24: The Lord bless thee, and keep thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Come, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
One God in persons three.
Bring back the heavenly blessing, lost
By all mankind, and me:
Thy favour, and Thy nature too.
To me, to all restore;
Forgive, and after God renew,
And keep us evermore.

poems.title: Numbers 6:25: Eternal Sun of Righteousness
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Eternal Sun of Righteousness,
Display Thy beams Divine,
And cause the glory of Thy face
Upon my heart to shine;
Light in Thy light O may I see,
Thy grace and mercy prove.
Revived, and cheer'd, and bless'd by Thee,
The God of pardoning love.

poems.title: Numbers 6:26: The Lord lift up His countenance upon thee, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lift up Thy countenance serene,
And let Thy happy child
Behold without a cloud between
The Godhead reconciled:
That all-comprising peace bestow
On me through grace forgiven,
The joys of holiness below.
And then the joys of heaven.

poems.title: Numbers 9:16: Where is the Hebrews'' God
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Where is the Hebrews'' God,
Who kept them night and day,
Where is the heavenly fire and cloud,
Which show'd Thy church their way?
No symbol visible
We of Thy presence find,
Yet all who would obey Thy will
Shall know their Father's mind.

Father, Thou still dost lead
The children of Thy grace.
The spiritual, believing seed
Throughout this wilderness:
Our chart Thy written word,
Thy Spirit is our guide,
And Christ, the glory of the Lord,
Doth in our hearts reside.

Thy providential care,
Lord, we with joy confess.
Assured Thou wilt our paths prepare.
And order all our ways;
Thy presence shall direct
Our journeys here beneath,
And convoy home Thine own elect
Through a triumphant death.

poems.title: Numbers 9:18: Who in Thy word confide
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who in Thy word confide.
From nature's haste set free,
Our patient souls by faith abide.
And fix their eyes on Thee:
Till Thou Avouldst have us go.
We wait Thy Spirit's sign;
And cannot lose our time, we know,
By tarrying, Lord, for Xhine.

To work for God is good,
If God our work ordain;
But stay'd by the incumbent cloud,
We in our place remain:
To cease from work is best.
If after Jesu's will;
For when at His command we rest,
We please our Saviour still.

Saviour, we wait the day.
The awful day unknown.
To quit our house, this tent of clay,
To lay our bodies down;
Expecting from above
The certain sign we stand.
As ready always to remove.
And die at Thy command.

poems.title: Numbers 9:23: At the commandment of the Lord they rested, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Most gracious God, reveal
Thy will concerning me;
Whate'er I do, whate'er I feel,
I follow Thy decree.
Myself, and all my ways
To Thee I still resign.
Led by the Spirit of Thy grace,
And by the word Divine.

Jesus, I here abide,
Thy pleasure to fulfil;
My soul and all its motions guide
By Thy most holy will;
The counsels of Thy love
Be on my heart impress'd,
It then shall at Thy bidding move,
And at Thy bidding rest.

Eternal Spirit, spread
Thy love throughout my breast,
Who didst Thine ancient people lead,
And causedst them to rest:
While Thou my leader art.
And mak'st me Thine abode,
I find the witness in my heart
That I am born of God.

Father, Thy will be done!
To Thee I all resign,
The sole Disposer of Thine own,
Dispose of me, and mine:
At Thy command I go.
Or quietly attend,
Till all my rests, and toils below j
In rest eternal end.

poems.title: Numbers 9:23: They kept the charge of the Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, I Thy charge obey
Who bidd'st my soul be still,
Whose cloud doth on my body stay.
And stops my acting zeal:
But while withheld I am
From labouring in Thy cause,
Thou bidd'st me suffer for Thy name.
And glory in Thy cross.

Whate'er my God ordain.
Contented and resign'd,
I wait, I watch, in ease, in pain,
The tokens of Thy mind;
To labour on for Thee,
If Thou appoint, I come;
Or let the cloud remain on me,
And sink me to the tomb.

poems.title: Numbers 11:4: Whoe'er for sensual pleasures burn
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Whoe'er for sensual pleasures burn,
Or wish their lusts to gratify,
Back in their hearts to Egypt turn,
And basely for the fleshpots sigh;
And such, without repentance, shall
Death's victims in the desert fall.

poems.title: Numbers 11:15: Meekest of all the sons of men
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Meekest of all the sons of men.
Did Moses peevishly complain,
And weak impatience show?
The holiest in that virtue fail'd.
In that wherein they most excell'd,
Till God appear'd below.

But now the better hope brought in
Gives perfect liberty from sin,
And Christ vouchsafes to' impart
The Spirit of holiness complete.
To make His saints for glory meet,
To make them meek in heart.

poems.title: Numbers 11:23: No, Lord; it cannot shorten'd be
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
No, Lord; it cannot shorten'd be.
That hand which plagued the' Egyptian race,
Which brought Thy people through the sea,
Which led them o'er the wilderness;
Which hath to us so often given
Drink from the rock, and bread from heaven!

That hand hath open'd wide mine eyes:
That hand, which now by faith I see,
Measures the floods, and spans the skies,
And grasps the winds, — and covers me!
It brings the bHnd through ways unknown,
It holds; it Lifts me to a throne.

Kept by that hand, I cannot fear
Lest earth or hell should pluck me thence
I trample on temptation near,
Supported by Omnipotence,
Possess'd of boundless power Divine,
Of boundless love — for Christ is mine!

poems.title: Numbers 11:28: My lord Moses, forbid them
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How often have I blindly done
Vhat zealous Joshua did.
Impatient to the rulers run,
And cried " My lords, forbid!
Silence the schismatics; constrain
Their thoughts with ours to' agree;
And sacrifice the souls of men
To idol unity!"

poems.title: Numbers 11:29: Moses, the minister of God
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Moses, the minister of God,
Rebukes our partial love.
Who envy at the gifts bestow'd
On those we disapprove:
We do not our own spirit know,
WIio wish to see suppress'd
The men that Jesu's spirit show,
The men whom God hath bless'd.

poems.title: Numbers 11:29: Would God that all the Lord's people, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Shall we the Spirit's course restrain,
Or quench the heavenly fire?
Let God His messengers ordain,
And whom He will inspire:
Blow as He list, the Spirit's choice
Of instruments we bless;
We will, if Christ be preach'd, rejoice.
And wish the word success.

Can all be prophets then? are all
Commission'd from above?
No; but whome'er the Lord shall call
We joyfully approve:
O that the church might all receive
The spirit of proj)hecy,
And all in Christ accepted live.
And all in Jesus die!

poems.title: Numbers 11:33: Alas for sinners that obtain
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Alas for sinners that obtain
Their passionate request!
Lidulged in nature's lust, they gain
A grief, a curse, a pest:
But our imaginary want
Thou wilt not, Lord, supply;
To them Thou dost in anger grant,
To us in love deny.

poems.title: Numbers 12:8: Wherefore were ye not afraid to speak, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Earth and hell Thy law opposes,
Cannot the commandment bear;
Speaking 'gainst Thy servant Moses,
Thee to contradict they dare:
O omnipotent Redeemer,
End their antinomian lore,
Still the undisguised blasphemer.
Let him vex Thy flock no more.

poems.title: Numbers 13:28: What say the false faint-hearted spies
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What say the false faint-hearted spies?
"Why should we make the world our foe?
Satan's strongholds that reach the skies
Can feeble flesh and blood o'erthrow?
The walls of our corruptions must.
Till death demolish them, remain:
The ruin of all pride, all lust
The Lord hath promised us — in vain."

poems.title: Numbers 13:28: How madly rash for puny man
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How madly rash for puny man,
The world, the fiend, and flesh to' oppose!
Our passions will their sway maintain,
Our terrible gigantic foes:
We must, who doubt the gospel-word.
With Satan and the world comply.
We must, who cannot trust the Lord,
Sin on, till we for ever die.

poems.title: Numbers 13:30: Silence, yc unbelieving fears
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Silence, yc unbelieving fears,
Who clamorously deny the word!
The promise on our side appears.
The power and goodness of our Lord:
Let us go up in Jesu's name:
Our sins shall all to Christ submit,
And who for us the world o'ercame.
Shall bruise the fiend beneath our feet.

Is anything too hard for God?
Through Jesus we can all things do;
Who Satan and his works destroy'd.
Shall make us more than conquerors too:
Let us at once the land possess.
And taste the blessings from above,
The milk sincere of pardoning grace,
The honey of His perfect love.

poems.title: Numbers 13:30: In vain, ye fearful, faithless spies
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
In vain, ye fearful, faithless spies,
Ye mis-report the land so good;
We stop our ears against your lies
"That sin can never be subdued."
There's no unconquerable sin:
If God lead forth His host to fight.
We may, we must, the battle win,
And all o'ercome in Jesu's might.

poems.title: Numbers 13:31–33: "Ah, no," the faithless spies reply
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
"Ah, no," the faithless spies reply.
Who search'd with us the happy land,
"We cannot scale the forts so high,
Or 'gainst the sons of Anak stand:
Stronger than us our foes we deem." —
But are they stronger than your Lord?
Giants are grasshoppers to Him,
To all who venture on His word.

poems.title: Numbers 13:31: Our mighty sins they need not still
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Our mighty sins they need not still
O'er us dominion have,
Less mighty to enthrall and kill,
Than Jesus is to save:
We hear our King and Captain's shout
Against our foes abhorr'd.
And leave them now to fight it out
With our almighty Lord.

poems.title: Numbers 14:2: Would God that we had died in the land, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Poor abject souls that disbelieve
The promise, when it comes so nigh!
To God who dare not credence give.
For fear of death they wish to die:
They have the death for which they call;

But justly first their burden bear.
Their bodies in the desert fall,
Their souls are saved by Moses prayer.
Have I not often wish'd the same.
In peevishness of mad despair.
Repined I out of Egypt came.

And vex'd I had not perish'd there?
While hopeless the good land to see,
I question'd. Lord, Thy truth and pov/er,
And cried, " A saint I cannot be,
I cannot live, and sin no more."

poems.title: Numbers 14:4: Let us make a captain, and let us return, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Oft as our hearts to sin turn'd back,
Impatient of Thy rule, we cried.
Of self let us a captain make,
And fly to Egypt with our guide:
And did not mercy stand between.
Our unbelief would still prevail,
Our guide would bring us back to sin.
And nature lead us down to hell.

poems.title: Numbers 14:8: The Lord doth in His Son delight
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The Lord doth in His Son delight,
Doth us for Jesu's sake approve,
Our faith is pleasing in His sight
Productive of obedient love:
And all who thus in Him believe.
Already with the earnest bless'd,
God unto them the land shall give,
The gracious, and the glorious rest.

poems.title: Numbers 14:9: Only rebel not ye against the Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Nothing but sin can sinners slay,
Denied by Him they first deny,
Left by the God they chase away.
Because they will not live, they die;
Compell'd by no decree unknown
Who will not bow to Christ's command,
They perish, by themselves alone
Excluded from that heavenly land.

poems.title: Numbers 14:9: Neither fear ye the people of the land, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Come on ye faithful souls, come on,
T s Joshua cries, " Be of good cheer,"
Your Leader to the land unknown.
Who knows your hearts forbids your fear:
Led by almighty truth and grace,
To sure and easy conquest led,
The promise claim, the land possess.
And eat up all your foes like bread.

The Lord Himself is on our side,
His presence in our camp we have,
And those that in His name confide
Jesus shall to the utmost save:
Then let us go with boldness up
Gainst sin, the world, and Satan's powers.
And never faint, and never stop.
For God, and Christ, and all is ours.

poems.title: Numbers 14:10: "Stone the blasphemers vile," they cry
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
"Stone the blasphemers vile," they cry,
"Who urge us the good land to win.
And tell us, we may scale the sky,
And talk of living without sin I"
They say, sin never need prevail.
All sin ye may with ease subdue:
They contradict their fellows' tale.
And dare avouch that God is true.

poems.title: Numbers 14:11: Ah! Lord, with Thee we ask. How long
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Ah! Lord, with Thee we ask. How long
Shall men Thy patient Spirit grieve,
Thy power mistrust, Thy goodness wrong,
Thy faithful promise disbelieve?
Not all the wonders Thou hast wrought
Can yet embolden them to seize
The' inheritance Thy blood hath bought,
The land of rest and righteousness.

poems.title: Numbers 14:17: On us, almighty Lord, bestow
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
On us, almighty Lord, bestow
The blessing which we humbly crave,
The greatness of Thy mercy show,
And magnify Thy power to save;
Take all Thy people's sin away,
Its being with its guilt remove.
And thus in our behalf display
Thy whole omnipotence of love.

poems.title: Numbers 14:19: Pardon, I beseech Thee, the iniquity, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Since first we did from Egypt fly.
Hast Thou not shown Thy patient grace,
A thousand times our sin pass'd by.
And pardon'd a rebellious race?
Wherefore by all Thy mercies past
We pray Thee yet again forgive.
And let our souls, subdued at last.
To praise Thy love for ever live.

poems.title: Numbers 14:20: Would the great God His rebels spare
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Would the great God His rebels spare.
According to a creature's word?
He heard His Son in Moses' prayer:
And still He hears our pleading Lord:
The prayer of but one righteous man.
If Jesus in His servant breathe.
Can the Almighty's wrath restrain.
And millions save from endless death.

poems.title: Numbers 14:21: As truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, Thy promise we embrace
Seal'd with the oath Divine,
The brightness of Thy heavenly face
Throughout our earth shall shine:
That all may do Thy perfect will
As angels do above,
Thou every ransom'd soul shalt seal
With Jesu's glorious love.

poems.title: Numbers 14:24: My servant Caleb, because he had another, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Would we after Christ fulfil
The righteous law of love?
Careful to perform His will,
We shall His promise prove:
Who that other Spirit have,
The Spirit of faith to Ca/el given,
Christ from all our sins shall save.
And settle us in heaven.

poems.title: Numbers 14:24: And his seed shall possess it
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
All that in his footsteps tread,
And dare their faith confess.
They are valiant Caleb'' s seed,
And shall the land possess:
Trusting God to bring us in,'
We shall be perfected in love.
Enter here the rest from sin.
And then the rest above.

poems.title: Numbers 14:29: And let my carcase fall j
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
And let my carcase fall j
Here in this wilderness,
So Thou my soul in mercy call,
And bid me die in peace;
For my rebellions past
Condemn'd till death I rove:
But give me to behold at last
InunanueV s land above. 1

poems.title: Numbers 14:34: The saving promise is for all
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The saving promise is for all,
And all may live of Christ possess'd,
Yet thousands in the desert fall,
And never enter into rest:
By God ordain'd to life alone,
Through wilful incredulity
Destroy'd, they in that day shall own
It was no absolute decree!

poems.title: Numbers 14:44: Who the strength of God distrust
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who the strength of God distrust
Will in their own confide,
On their own destruction thrust
By selfishness and pride:
Marching up without the Lord,
Smitten before their foes they fly.
Fall on the destroyer's sword,
And unbelievers die.

poems.title: Numbers 16:10: Raised from the people's lowest lees
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Raised from the people's lowest lees,
Guard, Lord, Thy preaching witnesses,
Nor let their pride the honour claim
Of sealing covenants in Thy name:
Rather than suff"er them to dare
Usurp the priestly character,
Save from the arrogant offence.
And snatch them uncorrupted hence.

poems.title: Numbers 16:21: When once the devils are enter'd in
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
When once the devils are enter'd in,
And make the frantic herd rebel,
Following a multitude to sin,
We surely follow them to hell.

poems.title: Numbers 16:26: Depart, I pray you, from the tents, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus obtain'd.us the reprieve;
Yet must we use the means and fly,
The world, the tents of sinners, leave.
Or blended with the wicked die.

poems.title: Numbers 16:41: While yet they hear the rebels' cries
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
While yet they hear the rebels' cries,
Sent quick to hell before their eyes,
Again Thy wrath they dare:
What, Lord, can, all Thy judgments do.
Unless Thy love our hearts renew,
And reign for ever there!

poems.title: Numbers 16:48: Jesus, the merciful and true
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, the merciful and true.
Between the dead and living stand.
The numerous dead, the living few
Who now divide Britannia's land!
Thou dost as in the midst appear,
Thou hast for all atonement made,
And through the incense of Thy prayer
The plague of unbelief is stay'd.

poems.title: Numbers 20:28: Happy, for ever happy
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Happy, for ever happy I,
If call'd, like him, the mount to' ascend;
Thine all-sufficient grace supply.
And bless me. Saviour, with his end:
O that without a lingering groan
I might the welcome word receive,
My body with my charge lay down,
And cease at once to work and live!

poems.title: Numbers 21:5: Who murmur in the wilderness
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who murmur in the wilderness
By daily wonders fed,
May loathe the comforts of Thy grace
As despicable bread:
But nourish'd still with fresh supplies
Of blessings from above, i
The more we taste, the more we prize
The manna of Thy love.

poems.title: Numbers 21:9: Faint my head, and sick my heart
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Faint my head, and sick my heart.
Wounded, bruised, in every part,
Satan's fiery sting I feel
Poison'd with the pride of hell:
But if at the point to die
Upward I direct mine eye,
Jesus lifted up I see.
Live by Him, who died for me.

poems.title: Numbers 22:18: Jesus, mighty to convert
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, mighty to convert,
A secret power from Thee
Turn'd the covetous wizard's heart,
And caused his eyes to see;
"Now I must observe the word,
Beneath the government Divine,
Now," he saith, "I serve the Lord,
And JsratTs God is mine."

poems.title: Numbers: O The resistless power of grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O The resistless power of grace
On an old prophet false, who loved
The wages of unrighteousness,
Till by almighty grace reproved
He with his sin his change confess'd,
And bless'd the men whom God had bless'd.

poems.title: Numbers 23:10: Let me die the death of the righteous!
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Did God reject the pious prayer,
To' avenge his former wickedness?
His body might the judgment bear,
His soul depart in perfect peace,
A sinner slain, yet justified;
For thus the good Josiah died!

poems.title: Numbers 23:10: Let my last end be like his!
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Saviour, thus o'errule Thy foes,
Thee and Thine who now oppose,
By that Spirit from above
Turn their hatred into love;
Let them here our order see,
Share our happiness in Thee,
Die of Israel's God possess'd.
Live with us for ever bless'd!

poems.title: Numbers 23:10: Let me die the death of the righteous, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
His life alas, I have not lived!
But from this instant turn'd, and grieved
For my transgressions past,
I live the life of righteousness;
And O my God, with pardon bless,
And give me peace at last.

Saved at my latest hour receive,
And bid Thy joyful servant live
Where grief is chased away.
My lot among the saints assign,
And let their final state be mine
In that triumphant day.

poems.title: Numbers 23:21: He hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jacob then was free from blame,
And uncorrupted stood,
Israel, answering to his name,
Was prevalent with God.
While I keep my conscience clean,
Eschew mine own iniquity,
God, who sees my nature sin,
Imputes not sin to me.

poems.title: Numbers 23:21: Christ, the Lord our God, Thou art
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)

poems.title: Numbers 23:23: According to this time it shall be said, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Reflecting on this gospel-day,
And Britain s happy lot.
Latest posterity shall say
What hath Jehovah wrought!
He hath the faithful seed increased,
Ten thousand souls forgiven;
With perfect love His people bless'd.
And caught them up to heaven.

poems.title: Numbers 24:15, 16: The man whom God so freely loved
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The man whom God so freely loved,
And bade his sin depart.
Opening his eyes, he found removed
The blindness of his heart;
He heard the word, "Let there be light,"
He felt the' almighty grace.
And saw, transform'd, the glorious light
Of his Redeemer's face.

poems.title: Numbers 24:17: I shall see Him, but not now, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Happy soul, enjoy thy lot,
Finding Him thou soughtest not:
O that I with thee could say,
"I shall see Him in that day!"
When He doth on earth appear,
O might I behold Him near,
Now, like the old seer, forgiven,
Snatch'd as out of hell to heaven!

poems.title: Numbers 24:17: There shall come a Star out of Jacob, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Foretold by the converted seer
The Star is out oi Jacob come,
The King from Irsael did appear.
His church's foes received their doom.
And Christ, our manifested God,
Hath Satan with his works destroy'd.

Yet come, Thou radiant morning Star,
Again in human darkness shine;
Arise, resplendent from afar.
Assert Thy royalty Divine,
Thy sway o'er all the earth maintain.
And now begin Thy glorious reign.

Smite down the strength of Moab's pride,
The sons of Sheth their walls o'erthrow,
(Whate'er the world and church divide,)
That every soul its Lord may know,
Thee, Jesus, King of kings adore.
Till time and death shall be no more.

poems.title: Numbers 24:18: Thy kingdom, Lord, we long to see
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thy kingdom, Lord, we long to see:
Thy sceptre o'er the nations shake,
(To' erect that final monarchy)
Edom for Thy possession take,
Take, for Thou didst their ransom find,
The purchased souls of all mankind.

poems.title: Numbers 24:18: Now let Thy chosen ones appear
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Now let Thy chosen ones appear,
And valiantly the truth maintain,
Dispread Thy gracious kingdom here,
Fly on the rebel sons of men.
Seize them with faith divinely bold,
And force the world into Thy fold.

poems.title: Numbers 24:19: Jesus, Thy coming we confess
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thy coming we confess
To reign in every faithful heart:
Thou hast subdued our wickedness;
Yet now Thy farther grace impart,
Take this indwelling sin away,
And all its cursed relics slay.

poems.title: Numbers 24:20: Amalek was the first of the nations, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Too well that Amalck I know
Who still maintains the war within,
Thy people's first and sorest foe:
But Thou, O Christ, shalt end my sin,
Destroy my nature's enmity.
And reign, for ever reign in me.

poems.title: Numbers 24:24: The powers that did from Chittim come
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The powers that did from Chittim come,
O'erran and deluged all the East:
The' avenging arms of pagan Rome
Ebcr's degenerate sons oppress'd,
Slaughter'd, or chased through earth abroad
Those murderers of incarnate God.

While Satan fills the' unerring chair,
They still afflict the chosen seed,
The inward Jews they vex and tear,
The faithfiil Israelites indeed;
That papal beast the saints o'erpowers,
And with his iron teeth devours.

But Jesus, our triumphant Lord,
Soon as the witnesses are kill'd,
Arm'd with His Spirit's flaming sword,
In glorious majesty reveal'd,
Shall slay the antichrist of Rome,
And seal his everlasting doom.

poems.title: Numbers 25:17: Thy word, O God, as right and just
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thy word, O God, as right and just
We faithfully receive,
Who wouldst, that no enticing lust
Should unmolested live:
A Midianife we will not spare,
(If Thou Thy grace supply,)
But all that did our souls ensnare
On Jesu's cross shall die.

poems.title: Numbers 32:23: My sin will find me out, unless
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
My sin will find me out, unless
I first find out my sin, and mourn,
Forsake it, ere the judgment seize.
And to the mighty Fortress turn:
My City of defence is sure.
To which I now by faith repair,
I dwell in Jesu's wounds secure,
And sin shall never find me there.

poems.title: Numbers 33:55: Ah! foolish souls, the' accursed race
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Ah! foolish souls, the' accursed race
Who will not utterly expel,
But suffer sin to keep its place,
But let it in your border dwell I
The' indwelling sin for which ye plead
Shall pierce you through with cruel pains,
Shall make your heart and conscience bleed,
And plague you with its dire remains.

Will ye the hateful relics spare,
And say, it is the Saviour's will?
The thorns ye for yourselves prepare
Your wounded sides and eyes shall feel;
Vex'd by the foes ye leave within,
In vain for rest, or help ye cry.
For you, who choose to live with sin,
There's no redemption — till you die!

poems.title: Numbers 33:56: The sins which men at Thy command
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The sins which men at Thy command
Refuse, O God, to' expel.
Shall sweep them off the promised land.
Shall drive them out to hell;
The lusts which for the Saviour's sake
They will not mortify,
Shall bring Thy threaten'd curse, and make
Their souls for ever die.

poems.title: Numbers 35:12: They shall be unto you cities of refuge, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Our City of defence, to Thee
From the avenger, Lord, we flee.
Who in Thy death confide;
Justice Divine pursues in vain
The men who God Himself have slain,
When shelter'd in Thy side.

poems.title: Numbers 35:27: But lest we from our City stray
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
But lest we from our City stray,
And justice stern the straggler slay,
Thy hallowing grace bestow.
Bind us with cords of perfect love,
And hide our spotless souls above,
And never let us go.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 1:8: Behold, I have set the land before you, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The pleasant land display'd before
Our eyes of faith we see;
And God, the God of Abraham, swore
To give it unto me:
I now go up, the perfect peace,
The perfect love to feel,
And in that land of righteousness
I shall for ever dwell.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 1:28: Our brethren, of their foes afraid
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Our brethren, of their foes afraid,
Have us by their report dismay'd;
And listening to their lie,
That " sin can never be brought down,"
Faint-hearted slaves, we must sin on,
Till in despair we die.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 1:29, 30: Dread not, neither be afraid of them., &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thy messenger we hear,
Who tells us better things,
Numbers xxxv. 27 — Deuteronomy ii. 7.
Who in Thy name forbids our fear,
And joyful tidings brings:
The Lord our God and Guide,
Thou dost prepare our way;
Our Captain fights on IsraePs side.
And Christ shall win the day:

By Thee from Egypt led
We on to conquer go,
Confident in Thy strength to tread
On each devoted foe;
Thine arm stretch'd out again
Shall put forth all its power.
Till every Canaanite is slain.
And sin exists no more.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 2:7: The Lord thy God hath blessed thee, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Yes, the Lord my God hath bless'd
"Whate'er my hand hath done,
Seen me labouring after rest,
And all my walking known:
In this ghastly wilderness
Thou hast my kind Preserver been,
Nourish'd with sufiicient gi-ace.
And licld me back from sin.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 2:7: These forty years the Lord thy God, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lost, perplex'd with doubts and fears,
By endless troubles tried.
Thee for more than forty years
I own my secret Guide:
The borders of that heavenly place.
Wait to cross at Thy command.
And see my Leader's face.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 3:6: Who dares blame Thy justice, Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who dares blame Thy justice, Lord,
Which when their sin was full,
Slew Thy foes with Israel's sword.
And cut off every soul!
Vengeance swept the old away,
But mercy will'd the young to die.
From, though in, the evil day
It snatch'd them to the sky.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 3: Arm'd with Jesu's two-edged sword
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Arm'd with Jesu's two-edged sword
We now His charge fulfil,
All the' inhabitants abhorr'd
Of cursed Canaan kill;
Mercy, Lord, we will not show,
But execute Thy righteous mind,
Root and branch destroy the foe,
Nor leave a sin behind.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 3:22: We' in our Lord's command
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
We' in our Lord's command
A gracious promise hear.
The people of the land,
He saith we shall not fear;
And I shall more than conqueror be,
Since Jesus fights Himself for me.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 3:25: I pray thee, let me go over and see the good land, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lo! in longing hope I stand.
To enter, Lord, the goodly land,
Land of liberty and peace,
Happy land of righteousness!
Me who have rebellious been,
Bring into the rest from sin,
Into the rest of ripest love,
Into the rest of saints above.

For Thy people's rest I sigh,
Ready on Jordmis brink to die:
Must I, Lord, excluded be.
Never tread the land I see?
O for mercy's sake revive.
Bid me in Thine image live,
And then in perfect peace depart,
Holy, and just, and pure of heart.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 3:27: Get thee up into the top of Pisgah
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Fain would I, Lord, from earth remove,
Made meet before Thy face to' appear;
But tell me first Thy name is love.
But show me all Thy goodness here:
Borne on the wings of faith and hope,
I then shall to the mountain fly.
And yield my raptured spirit up.
And fainting on Thy bosom die.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 4:2: Self Thy word would fain diminish
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Self Thy word would fain diminish,
Pride Thy word would fain increase.
But what Thou art pleased to finish
Never can be more or less;
All Thy word without addition
Renders us for glory meet.
Fits us for the blissful vision,
Makes the man of God complete.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 4:6: Keep and do them, for this is your wisdom
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Obedience is our pure delight,
Our wisdom, glory, gain,
Unblamable in Jesu's sight
We all with Him obtain:
For while we out of love obey,
Unto salvation wise
We walk in wisdom's pleasant way,
Which leads us to the skies.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 4:7: What nation is there so great who hath God, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Greater than ancient Israel, we
With open face His glory see,
And God more intimately nigh
Doth now our every want supply,
The Spirit of His Son imparts,
And prays Himself in all our hearts.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 4:29: If from thence thou shall seek the Lord, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
From hence, most gracious Lord, from hence
The land of my captivity,
I wail my complicate offence,
And turn from every sin to Thee;
Mine utmost strength (which is not mine)
In striving against sin exert,
And weep, and pray for love Divine
With all my soul, and all my heart.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 4:30, 31: When thou art in tribulation, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O'erwhelm'd alas, with deep distress,
O'ertaken by Thy plagues I mourn,
And lo! in these my latest days
To Thee, my pardoning God, I turn:
Obedient now Thy voice I hear;
I will with all Thy words comply:
Avert the punishment I fear,
Nor leave me in my sins to die.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 5:27: Gracious Lord, who stand'st between
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Gracious Lord, who stand'st between
The great God and sinful men,
Thee we joyfully will hear;
Speak, Divine Interpreter,
Speak whate'er He speaks to Thee,
Then we shall obedient be.
Then our answering heart shall prove
All the law fulfill'd in love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy: Be it according to Thy will
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Be it according to Thy will.
According to Thy soul's desire
The gracious principle instil.
The tender awe Thou dost require;
I want an heart to fear my Lord:
O take this heart of stone away,
And let me tremble at Thy word,
And only live Thy word to' obey.

poems.title: Deuteronomy: That it might be well with them for ever
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, Thy merciful design
We see, and joyfully approve.
Thou kindly dost Thy laws enjoin,
To make us happy in Thy love:
With joy we own the gracious end
For which Thy laws were all bestow'd,
Thou dost by each command intend
Our present and eternal good.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 6:5: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, I believe Thy mercy's power
Shall every obstacle remove,
I trust Thy promise to restore
In me the kingdom of Thy love:
Jesus, Thy word cannot be vain;
Truth, power, and love Divine Thou art;
And I shall love my God again.
With all my mind, soul, strength, and heart.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 6:6: These words which I command thee, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The table of my heart prepare,
(Such power belongs to Thee alone,)
And write, O God, Thy precepts there.
To show Thou still canst write in stone,
So shall my pure obedience prove
All things are possible to love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 6:7: Father, instruct my docile heart
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, instruct my docile heart.
Apt to instruct I then shall be,
I then shall all Thy words impart,
And teach (as taught myself by Thee)
My children in their earliest days.
To know, and live the life of grace.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 6:7: When quiet in my house I sit
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
When quiet in my house I sit.
Thy book be my companion still.
My joy Thy sayings to repeat.
Talk o'er the records of Thy will,
And search the oracles Divine,
Till every heartfelt word is mine.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 6:7: O Might the gracious words Divine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O Might the gracious words Divine
Subject of all my converse be,
So would the Lord His follower join,
And walk, and talk Himself with me,
So would my heart His presence prove,
And burn with everlasting love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 6:7: Oft as I lay me down to rest
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Oft as I lay me down to rest,
O may the reconciling word
Sweetly compose my weary breast,
While on the bosom of my Lord
I sink in blissful dreams away,
And visions of eternal day.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 6:7: Rising to sing my Saviour's praise
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Rising to sing my Saviour's praise.
Thee may I publish all day long.
And let Thy precious word of grace
Flow from my heart, and fill my tongue.
Fill all my life with purest love,
And join me to Thy church above.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 7:7, 8: The Lord did )iot set His love upon yon, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What angel can explain
The love of God to man,
The secret cause assign
Of charity Divine?
Nothing in us could move,
Deserve, or claim His love:
Tis all a mystery.
And must for ever be!

poems.title: Deuteronomy 7:22: Tis not a sudden stroke of grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Tis not a sudden stroke of grace
Destroys at once the cursed race,
When first to Christ we come;
But by degrees insensible
The Lord shall all our sins expel,
And utterly consume.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 7:23: The Lord thy God shall deliver them, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
So be it Lord; my foes bring down,
And bid me go victorious on
To my last victory;
Jesus, destroy whom Thou hast bound,
Till not a single sin is found
To stir, or breathe in me.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 7:24: He shall deliver their kings into thine hand, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Deliver'd now into mine hand.
Not one of all my foes shall stand,
Or dare his conqueror meet,
My reigning lusts shall reign no more,
For ever stripp'd of all their power,
And gasping at my feet.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 7:24: Jesus, I in Thy promise trust
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, I in Thy promise trust,
No bosom-sin, no darling lust
Too strong for me shall prove,
Till Thou their nature hast destroy'd.
And fill'd my soul's unbounded void
With all Thy perfect love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 8:2: Can I forget the wondrous ways
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Can I forget the wondrous ways
By which Thou hast Thy servant led
Through a long lonely wilderness!
How strangely kept, how strangely fed,
Tempted, and proved by hopes and fears,
I roved for more than forty years!

Provoked, Thou didst not quite depart,
But farther yet Thy Spirit tried.
And show'd the evil of my heart,
The stubbornness, deceit, and pride,
While still I cast Thy grace away.
And would not, when I might, obey.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 8:3: Saviour, my nature's pride to' abase
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Saviour, my nature's pride to' abase,
Thou oft hast seem'd my soul to leave.
Withheld the comforts of Thy grace,
And suffer'd me to pine, and grieve:
But when Thou dost my pride destroy,
Thy sweetness I shall always prove,
And fill'd with righteousness, enjoy
The manna of Thy perfect love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 8:16: Long in a tempted state forlorn
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Long in a tempted state forlorn
Thou hast my kind Supporter been,
Yet suffer'd me at times to mourn,
To feel that all my heart is sin;
My depth of unbelief to prove,
And groan for all Thy humbling love.

I now Thy love's design perceive;
Me to myself Thy love hath shown.
Thou didst in love Thy servant leave,
To come again and claim Thine own.
To save, when all my griefs were pass'd,
And do mc endless good at last.

A NOVICE, to myself unknown,
That endless good I could not prove,
Or, when my race was scarce begun.
Attain the goal of perfect love:
But on Thy promise I depend
To bless me at my latter end.

Saviour, my latter end is come,
Now to my parting soul appear.
The root, the man of sin consume.
And let me sink to nothing here,
Resorb'd into perfection's sea,
And lost, for ever lost in Thee!

poems.title: Deuteronomy 8:16: I My latter end is come
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I My latter end is come:
But where 's the promised good?
Ah, do it. Lord, and take me home
Through Thy all-cleansing blood!
The gracious work remains
Unfinish'd, and undone:
Fill up my faith, fill up my pains,
And take me to Thy throne.
I By Thy own Spirit's might
The work of faith fulfil,
With love's habitual, pure delight
I then shall do Thy will.
I then my God shall see,
With raptured saints adore,
And plunge in Thy immensity.
And bathe for evermore!
Deuteronomy viii. i6 — ix. 6. yu

poems.title: Deuteronomy 8:18: Thou shall remember the Lord thy God, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Think, thou busy, prosperous man,
From whence thy goods increase,
All thy diligence were vain.
If God refused to bless:
Wealth thou dost through Him acquire,
That all thy soul may heavenward move.
Wing'd with infinite desire
Of Jesu's richest love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 9:3: Jesus, taught by Thee we know
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, taught by Thee we know
The wonders of Thy name,
Thou before our face dost go
As a consuming flame:
Burn with fire unquenchable
Our foes whom Thou dost first o'ercome,
Sin out of our hearts expel,
And root and branch consume.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 9: Faith lays hold on Thy great might
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Faith lays hold on Thy great might.
And forth to battle goes,
Arm'd herewith we put to flight
And triumph o'er our foes.
Trusting in lliy faithful word
We Thine almighty arm employ.
Slay them with Thy Spirit's sword,
And all our sins destroy.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 9: Understand, that the Lord thy God, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Mv merit, Lord, and righteousness
I utterly disclaim,
Whate'er I am, whate'er possess,
By grace I have and am;
By grace enabled, I receive
Thy blessings from above,
And wait, till Jesu's grace shall give
The crown of perfect love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 9:7: Thou need'st the kind command repeat
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou need'st the kind command repeat,
So apt the sinner to forget
His former trespasses:
But lest I cast them still behind.
Saviour, bring all my sins to mind.
And on my heart impress.
;i9. Fi'om the day that thou didst depart, &c.— x. 7.

I NOW reflect with grief and shame.
That since I out of Egypt came,
I have rebellious been.
Provoked Thee in the wilderness.
And wearied out Thy patient grace
By adding sin to sin;

A rebel to this present hour!
Yet now for all Thy mercy's power
I ask with contrite sighs
To end my sin, but not my pain:
I would lament till death,'-' and then
Rejoice in paradise.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 10:12: And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What doth the Lord require of man?
From sin if we can never cease,
Or do the things His laws ordain,
He asks impossibilities!
But if Thou ask them. Lord, from me,
Impossibilities shall be.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 10:12, 13: What doth the Lord thy God request, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O My most condescending Lord,
He humbly stoops to ask my love!
Tis no impracticable word;
I may, I will obedient prove,
His grace accept, His power exert,
And serve my God with all my heart.

Full of Thy holy love I rise,,
To worship spiritual and true.
On eagle's wings my spirit flies,
Whate'er my Lord commands to do,
To answer all my Saviour's will,
And perfectly His law fulfil.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 10: Jesus, Thou dost not sue in vain
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thou dost not sue in vain.
Or ask what I can never give:
Thyself hast placed the power in man
His proffer'd Saviour to receive.
While knocking at the door Thou art.
And criest " My son, give Me thy heart I"
Come in, Thou Supplicant Divine,
I hear Thy voice and open now:
I'ake my poor heart, no longer mine.
Enter with all Thy fulness Thou;
Take my poor heart, ('tis all Thine own.)
And never leave Thy humble throne.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 10:16: If Thou command it, Lord, we may
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
If Thou command it, Lord, we may
With our transgressions part:
We do cut off, and cast away
The foreskin of our heart;
Our stiff-neck'd souls we bow to Thee,
And trusting in Thy power,
We need no more rebeUious be,
We will rebel no more.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 11:25: Lord, Thy saying I embrace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, Thy saying I embrace,
And 'gainst my threefold foe,
Trusting the sure word of grace,
To certain conquest go;
Till bound, and vanquish'd by Thy power.
Feeble sin shall faint, and die.
And fall to rise no more.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 12:25: Teach me, O God, Thy will to do
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Teach me, O God, Thy will to do,
To love myself aright,
My real interest to pursue
By walking in Thy sight:
Walking in all the ways Divine,
O may I thus ensure
A blessing. Lord, on me and mine,
Which always shall endure.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 18:13: Than shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Shall, (when He who saith I shall.
Hath with Himself bestow'd
Sufficient strength to walk in all
The righteous ways of God,)
I shall attain my heart's desire,
And serve like those above,
Complete in His whole will, entire
And perfect in His love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 18:18: I 'will raise them up a Prophet, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, Thou hast raised Him up,
That Prophet of the Lord,
Every heart's desire and hope,
Thine own eternal Word:
In our feeble flesh array'd
We own the Filial Deity,
Jesus like His brethren made,
To make us all like Thee.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 18:18: Speak, Thou true Interpreter
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Speak, Thou true Interpreter,
Those gracious words Divine,
Give our listening hearts to hear
The Father's voice in Thine;
Now declare the mystery.
And make His utmost counsel known,
Make Thy people one with Thee,
As Thou and Clod are one.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 18:19: Woe to them who will not own
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Woe to them who will not own
The Truth, the Life, the 'ay,
Will not the eternal Son
As God supreme obey I
Judge of all He soon shall come,
The dreadful penalty require.
Every unbeliever doom
To everlasting fire.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 19:9: Thou shall keep all that commandment Heb. ', &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
All that command is love!
Which now I long to' obey,
And trust Thee, Saviour, to remove
Whate'er obstructs the way:
Obedient to Thy will
Which doth my heart incline,
I shall by loving Thee fulfil
The perfect law Divine.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 23:9: The host is now gone forth: to fly
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The host is now gone forth: to fly;
Or fight? to conquer; or to die?
O, let us cast our sins away,
That God may hear His servants pray.
May us with more than conquest bless,
AVith glorious and eternal peace.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 23: Strengthen'd by Thy command
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Strengthen'd by Thy command
Against my wickedness.
Henceforth I every sin withstand
Through Thy sufficient grace:
I lay the sin aside
Which caused my frequent fall,
And wait to feel the blood applied
That cleanses me from all.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 25:18: This be ever on my mind
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
This be ever on my mind.
And fill my heart with fear,
Lest again I lag behind.
And loiter in the rear;
Let me, Lord, unwearied press
Toward the things before, above.
With the foremost strive to seize
The prize of perfect love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 30:6: On Thee, O God, my soul is stay'd
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
On Thee, O God, my soul is stay'd.
And waits to prove Thine utmost will:
The promise by Thy mercy made
Thou canst. Thou wilt in me fulfil:
No more I stagger at Thy power,
Or doubt Thy truth, which cannot move:
Hasten the long-expected hour.
And bless me with Thy perfect love.

One of the stubborn, harden'd race.
Now, Lord, on me the work begin,
And by the Spirit of Thy grace
Cut oft" the foreskin of my sin:
My stiff'-neck'd heart to circumcise,
Thy sanctifying power exert,
And I shall then attain the prize,
And love my God with all my heart.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 30:14: My God, from whom the precept came
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
My God, from whom the precept came,
Doth power Divine therewith impart.
When Jesus I desire, and name.
The word is in my mouth and heart;
I feel it intimately near,
Soon as my heart believes Him true,
And conscious of His presence here,
Through Jesus I can all things (.lo.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 30:19: I have set before you life and death, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
WouLDST Thou insult the fallen man,
The work of Thy own hands,
Or mock us, Lord, with offers vain,
If Thy decree withstands?
Thou canst not thus our souls deceive,
(Though men their God behe,)
Thou canst not bid us choose to live.
Whom Thou hast doom'd to die.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 30: Have we not then a power from Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Have we not then a power from Thee
Our Saviour, to refuse
The death, the curse, the misery,
And endless life to choose:
May I not turn from sin and live,
And taste how good Thou art?
O let Thy love this moment give
The answer in my heart.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 31:14: Behold, thy days approach that thou must die
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, I know my day is nigh.
And by Thy justice doom'd to die,
The sentence I receive:
But ere I yield my fleeting breath,
O let my soul redeem'd from death
By faith in Jesus live.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 31:16: Behold, thou shall sleep with thy fathers
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
By mercy seal'd in lasting sleep.
Mine eyes shall then no longer weep;
My flesh in hope shall rest
Blended with my forefathers' dust.
Till waked by Him in whom I trust,
I mingle with the bless'd.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:4: He is the Rock, His work is perfect
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Son of God, Thou art
Omnipotence Divine,
Tell it to my faithful heart
That what Thou art is mine;
Rock of everlasting love.
If on Thee my hopes I build,
I Thy perfect work shall prove
With all Thy fulness fill'd.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:5: Their spot is not the spot of his children, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Their sinful spot the heathen have;
But whom Thou dost redeem,
Jesus, omnipotent to save.
It cannot cleave to them:
Thou shedd'st Thy blood (and not in vain
Did the rich current flow)
To make us clean from every stain,
Thy spotless church below.

No wrinkle of the Adam old
Shall on Thy saints be seen;
The sons of God are pure as gold,
When grown to perfect men:
And if I in Thy word confide.
Thou, Lord, shalt say to me,
"Thou art all fair. My love, My bride,
There is no spot in thee!"

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:10: He found him in a desert land, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
He found me in a desert place,
Where far from God I roved.
And led mc through the legal maze.
And chasten'd whom He loved;
Kept as the apple of His eye,
With tenderest care caress'd,
And saved my soul, while sin was nigh.
And hid me in His breast.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:11, 12: The eagle fond her charge awakes
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The eagle fond her charge awakes
Where in the nest they doze,
And while her fluttering plumes she shakes
The v ay to fly she shows;
She spreads her wings, her young to bear.
Before their own they try,
And takes them up, and cleaves the air,
And soars above the sky.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32: TwAS thus in nature's sleep I lay
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
TwAS thus in nature's sleep I lay.
When Christ His Spirit shed:
His Spirit stirr'd me up to pray.

And hover'd o'er my head,
Infusing the first gracious hope
He spread His wings abroad.
And train'd His infant-pupil up
To seek the face of God.
The object of His kindest care
He never yet forsook,
But did Himself my weakness bear.

And all my burden took.
He bore me up, from earth He bore
On wings of heavenly love.
And taught my callow soul to soar
To those bright realms above.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32: The Spirit of redeeming grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The Spirit of redeeming grace
Hath been my sure defence,
And through the pathless wilderness
Led on my innocence,
When simple as a little child
All idols I abhorr'd,
And saw, as my Redeemer smiled,
 Iy paradise restored.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:13, 14: When first He freely justified
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
When first He freely justified,
And did my pardon seal,
O'er earth's strongholds He bade me ride,
O'er all the powers of hell:
Butter and milk He made me eat,
And lifted up on high
I saw the moon beneath my feet,
I soar'd above the sky.

With all the new-born babes I fed
Upon the milky word.
Partaker of the children's bread,
The favour of my Lord;
I feasted on the Paschal Lamb
Who all my wants supplied,
And with the sweetness of His name
My soul was satisfied.
The bliss of those above I knew,
The angels' food partook,
Fresh oil, and sweetest honey drew
Out of the heavenly Rock;
The joy, and love from Jesus flow'd,
And tasting Him as mine,
I drank the purest richest blood
Of that immortal Vine.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:15: And have not I ungrateful been
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
And have not I ungrateful been,
Basely forsook my God for sin.
My God who form'd me man,
Abused my Saviour's pardoning grace.
And turn'd it into wantonness,
And murder'd Him again!

Thee that I may no more forsake,
O Rock of my salvation, take
And keep me in Thy side;
There in the open cleft secure
My contrite heart, my spirit poor
From sin for ever hide.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:36: The Lord shall repent Himself, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Dost Thou not. Lord, with pity see
My helplessness and misery,
Dost Thou not hear Thy servant groan,
And know, that all my power is gone?
Returning now in tenderest love.
Thy judgments with their cause remove,
Take my oppressive sin away,
And give me back an heart to pray.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:39: I kill, and I make alive
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thy killing and Thy quickening power,
Jesus, in me display.
My life of nature, from this hour,
My pride and passion slay;
Then, then, my utmost Saviour, raise
My soul with saints above
To serve Thy will, and spread Thy praise.
And sing Thy perfect love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:39: I wound, and I heal
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Deepen the wound Thy hands have made
In this weak helpless soul.
Till mercy with its balmy aid
Descend to make me whole:
The sharpness of Thy two-edged sword
Enable me to' endure.
Till bold to cry " My hallowing Lord
Hath wrought a perfect cure!"

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32:49, 50: Get thee up and die
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Is it a thing so small,
So easy to comply,
When summon'd by a sudden call
To get us up, and die?
For those who humbly keep
The faith by Christ bestow'd,
To die is but to fall asleep
In the soft arms of God!

O could I thus sink down
To everlasting rest.
Without a lingering sigh or groan,
On my Redeemer's breast!
Jesus, Thy blood apply,
Thy mind and Spirit give,
Then shall I get me up and die.
Then shall I truly live.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 32: Thrice welcome word to those who live
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thrice welcome word to those who live
By faith in Him, their hearts receive
With true affection fill'd,
Who feel redemption in His blood,
And happy in the peace of God
Enjoy their pardon seal'd.

Before I render up my breath
Stronger than sin, and hell, and death.
Thy love I long to know.
Thy love omnipotent impart,
To strengthen and renew my heart,
And let my spirit go.

poems.title: Deuteronomy: The people out of Egypt brought
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The people out of Egypt brought.
Whose burdens He removed,
Whom with a thousand pangs He bought,
More than His life He loved.
Stronger than death His love was shown:
And still He doth defend.
And having freely loved His own.
Will love them to the end.

Whom Jesu's blood doth sanctify
Need neither sin nor fear;
Hid in our Saviour's hands we lie,
And laugh at danger near.
His guardian hand doth hold, protect,
And save by ways unknown.
The little flock, the saints elect,
Who trust in Him alone.

Our Prophet, Priest, and King, to Thee
We joyfully submit;
And learn, in much humility,
Our lesson at Thy feet.
Spirit and life Thy words impart,
And blessings from above;
And drop in every listening heart.
The manna of Thy love.

Now, Lord, with simple faith divine,
Thy lessons we receive,
Rule upon rule, line upon line,
And by Thy Spirit live.
Till late to all Thy life restored,
And ripen'd for the sky,
We hear that last, and sweetest word,
"Go, get thee up and die."

poems.title: Deuteronomy 33:25: As thy days, so shall thy strength be
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
As my day my strength hath been,
And shall for ever be,
Grace, an overmatch for sin.
Will still deliver me;
Every day the truth I prove
Of Jesus my almighty Friend,
Kept by Him, whose constant love
Shall keep me to the end.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 33:26: God of the upright ones
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
God of the upright ones,
Who can with Him compare I
He makes the house of Israels sons
His everlasting care:
Jehovah's rapid course
What can resist, or shun,
When heaven is His managed horse,
And brings the Thunderer down!

Glorious in majesty,
He takes the whirlwind's wings.
Sublime He rides upon the sky,
And help to Israel brings;
His people's sure defence
He takes them to His breast;
And safe in His omnipotence
They shall for ever rest.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 33:27: The eternal God is thy refuge, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Secure in Christ I dwell,
Jeshurim s God is mine,
I feel it now, by faith I feel
The' eternal strength Divine;
My refuge in distress,
In every trying hour,
Jesus, Thy saving name I bless.
And shout within my tower.

From sin preserved in Thee,
Thy fulness I embrace,
And wait for more than victory.
For all Thy hallowing grace:
I laugh at hell and death,
And every moment prove
The everlasting arms beneath.
The everlasting love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 33: Eternal God, my refuge now
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Eternal God, my refuge now
In trouble and temptation Thou:
Though still to sin inclined,
Safe from the snares of hell and death
Thine everlasting arms beneath
My sinking soul I find.

Yet, Lord, I ask a further grace:
The guilt original efface,
The inbred foe exclude;
I then shall dwell conceal'd with Thee
In spiritual serenity.
In blissful solitude.

Happy as the first sinless man,
I then my paradise regain
And rival those above,
Inflamed with pure seraphic zeal,
To do Thine acceptable will
In innocence and love.

In the highway of holiness
I walk with Christ in perfect peace.
Contemplating the prize,
Smooth as on eagle's wings ascend.
Translated with my heavenly Friend.
And grasp Thee in the skies.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 33:27: Lord, I Thy truth proclaim
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, I Thy truth proclaim.
And all-sufficient grace,
Kept by the virtue of Thy name
To perfect holiness:
Till Thou Thyself reveal,
I on the promise feed,
Thou wilt the enemy expel,
And slay the cursed seed:

The enemy within
He shall not long annoy.
Thou surely wilt extirpate sin.
And utterly destroy.
Thou wilt my soul defend.
Fulfil Thine own design,
My unbelief and troubles end.
And make me all Divine.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 33:28: Israel then shall dwell in safety alone
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thyself impart.
The world and sin to' exclude.
And let me find it in my heart
The long-sought solitude,
The still sequester'd shade
For which Thy people pine,
The bower for weary spirits made
