By the celestial Vine!

That secret place afford.
That shelter in Thy side.
And by Thy constant presence, Lord,
My soul for ever hide:
Secure I then shall dwell,
Delightfully alone.
Till Thou Thy glorious life reveal,
And take me to Thy throne.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 33:28: Meanest oi Jacob's race
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Meanest oi Jacob's race
y Jordatis stream I stand,
And lo! mine eye of faith surveys
The wide extended land!
A land of corn and wine
Our spirits to sustain,
And fill with vigorous life Divine
The gladden'd heart of man:

There the soft dew distils,
The soul-reviving bliss,
And Christ His pardoning grace reveals.
And whispers I am His,
Till God His Spirit pours,
His fulness from above,
In streams of righteousness, and showers
Of everlasting love.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 33:29: Happy art thou, O Israel, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Israel, exult to prove
How dear to God thou art,
Object of His peculiar love
Who made thee pure in heart;
Feel all thy happiness,
When Christ is form'd in thee,
Consummate joy, and perfect peace,
And spotless charity:

Saved to the utmost here,
When Christ is fully thine.
And meet before thy God to' appear,
In righteousness Divine,
Clothed with that heavenly Sun,
Behold His brightest blaze,
Go put thy robes of glory on.
And see Him face to face.

poems.title: Deuteronomy 33:29: How safe, when God hath seal'd
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How safe, when God hath seal'd
And hid our life above,
We rest surrounded with the shield
Of His almighty love!
Arm'd with His Spirit's sword,
Which slays the man of sin.
We prove the truth of Jesu's word,
Redeem'd and saved within:

Flesh, earth, and Satan join'd,
Cry out, it cannot be!
But them we soon shall liars find,
From sin entirely free:
Through the great strength of God
We trust to tread them down.
And triumph o'er our foes destroy'd.
And take the starry crown.

poems.title: Deuteronomy: Moses, when dead, himself survives
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Moses, when dead, himself survives.
He always in his precepts lives;
Though sinners dream his office o'er,
He loses nothing of his power.
His sight is as the eagle's strong,
And Sinai thunders in his tongue.

Think not the law through faith made void,
Its vigour cannot be destroy'd:
It marks our hearts with quickest eye,
And doth our smallest faults espy,
It seizes with almighty hands,
And holds us in eternal bands.

It holds us, when by grace set free
From curse, and fear, and penalty;
The easy yoke of Christ we prove,
Bound to obey the God we love;
And when these heavens are pass'd away.
We still shall glory to obey.

poems.title: Joshua 1:3: Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The land of uprightness
I set my foot upon,
By faith I touch it, Lord, and seize,
And take it for my own!

poems.title: Joshua 1:5: I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The promise to myself I take,
Me, me Thou never wilt forsake
Who on Thy Son depend:
Thy faith is plighted to my Lord,
And safe I hang upon the word
Of mine eternal Friend.

poems.title: Joshua 1:7: By faith I on His strength lay hold
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
By faith I on His strength lay hold,
And walk in Christ my way,
Divinely confident, and bold
His perfect law to' obey;
I shall perform His utmost will.
As sure as God is true,
And do the thing impossible
Which Jesus bids me do.

poems.title: Joshua 1:9: Be strong and of a good courage, be not afraid, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Arm'd with the presence of my Lord
I must be of good cheer,
Confiding in Thy faithful word,
I cannot faint or fear:
Go with me then where'er I go,
And lo! I sink, and rise,
And pass the gates of hell below,
And mount to paradise.

poems.title: Joshua 5:14: As Captain of the host of the Lord am I now come
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Chief Captain of Jehovah's host,
Jehovah we adore,
In Thee our real Joshua trust,
And prove Thy matchless power;
We now embrace and follow Thee
By Thy great Father given:
Led on to certain victory.
To holiness, and heaven.

poems.title: Joshua 6:15: Shall our corruptions stand
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Shall our corruptions stand.
Till death the walls o'erthrow?
Who bow io Joshua's high command,
We have not leain'd Him so:
We compass them about,
Day after day surround,
And wait the' appointed sign to shout.
The trumpet's sacred sound:

We wait in patient pain.
Our toilsome week fulfil;
Yet still the walls entire remain,
And undemolish'd still:
But though our nature's haste
Can never sin remove,
The seventh is the day of rest.
And brings the perfect love.

poems.title: Joshua 6:20: When the people heard the sound of the trumpet, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I Then let us urge our way,
And work, and sufier on.
Nor dream, the first, or second, day
Will throw the bulwarks down:
We on the sacred morn
Our sevenfold toil repeat,
Expecting that the latest turn
Our labour shall complete.

Then, then we shall obtain
The victory one and all,
The number of perfection gain.
And see the city fall,
Partakers of our hope
Our calling's glorious prize.
To finish'd holiness go up,
And then to paradise.

poems.title: Joshua 7:9: Jesus, as taught by Thee I plead
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, as taught by Thee I plead.
If vanquish'd by my foes I am.
My foes, which on Thy servant tread.
Will pour contempt on Thy great name:
Ah! leave me not engaged in fight
To lose my shield, and turn my back,
But arm. with all Thy Spirit's might.
And save me — for religion's sake!

poems.title: Joshua 7:10, 11: What profits prayer itself, unless
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What profits prayer itself, unless
We put the cursed thing away?
Lord, let us first the sin redress.
And then against the judgment pray.

poems.title: Joshua 7:13: The secret curse, the bosom sin
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The secret curse, the bosom sin
Through faith in Jesus I remove.
And sure the victory to win,
And more than conqueror to prove,

poems.title: Joshua 9:15, 123: Gainst Satan and the world I go
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Gainst Satan and the world I go,
(My Lord hath both for me o'ercome,)
And trample on my latest foe,
And march with Christ triumphant home.

poems.title: Joshua 7:18: Lord, if some secret sin of mine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, if some secret sin of mine
Doth now for public judgments call,
Obstruct the course of grace Divine,
And bring Thy righteous wrath on all;
Before the dreadful day o'ertake,
When sinners shall their doom receive,
O may I here confess, forsake,
Abhor the cursed thing, and live.

poems.title: Joshua 7:21: "I Saw, and coveted, and took!"
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
"I Saw, and coveted, and took!"
The progress this of every sin;
While death, admitted by a look.
Lets everlasting judgments in:
But if an eye of faith on Thee
I turn, directed by Thy word,
Jesus mine Advocate I see,
I see, desire, and take my Lord.

poems.title: Joshua 9:15: Condemn'd to die, of death afraid
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Condemn'd to die, of death afraid.
Our heavenly yi v/zz/rt- we address.
In rags of our own vileness clad.
Undone, if Thou refuse us peace.
But if Thy hand. Thy word Thou give.
We may, we shall for ever live.

poems.title: Joshua 10:6: The men of Gibeon sent unto Joshua, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Besieged by all the powers of night
For having made a peace with God,
Unequal to our foes in fight,
To Joshua in His high abode
Our prayers, as messengers, we send,
And trust Thou wilt Thine own defend.

Slack not Thine hand, but hasten down
To save Thy servants in distress.
By mercy bound to help Thine own.
Bound by Thy covenant of peace,
Thou canst not fail the souls, who trust
That Thou art good, that Thou art just.

poems.title: Joshua 10:12: Jesus, Thy sovereign will
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thy sovereign will
Doth nature's course control;
O bid my sun of life stand still.
And stop my parting soul:
My soul in life detain.
Till Thou hast all subdued.
Avenged me of my foes, and 'slain
The whole accursed brood.

O that the work were done.
That sin were all destroy'd!
How swiftly should I then go down,
How gladly set in God:
Sure with the morning rays
Of that great day to rise,
And bright with borrow'd glory blaze
Eternal in the skies.

poems.title: Joshua 10:24: Put your feet upon the necks of these kings
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Pride, and nature's various lusts
O'er infidels may reign,
We, who serve the Lord of hosts,
Their slavish yoke disdain;
See the tyrants fierce o'erthrown,
Compell'd by Joshua to submit.
All our sins we trample down
As dirt beneath our feet.

poems.title: Joshua 10:24: Jesus, command us to draw near
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, command us to draw near,
With confidence that casts out fear,
To trample on our foes o'erthrown.
To tread the kings of Canaan down,
As sharers of Thy victory.
And more than conquerors through Thee.

Thy mighty arm, in IsraePs sight.
Hath put the alien hosts to flight,
Hath seized the chiefs, and captive led
Or but for execution freed;
Thine arm hath dragg'd them out again,
To fall, and die for ever slain.

But first, through virtue of Thy word.
And strong in our almighty Lord,
Before their final doom they meet,
Upon their necks we set our feet,
The tyrant-lusts and passions spurn,
Which rule in all of woman born.

poems.title: Joshua 10:26: Jesus, now on sin we tread
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, now on sin we tread.
But still we look to Thee:
Conqueror of our foes, proceed
To more than victory.
Spirit and soul-dividing Word,
Thine utmost energy display,
Smite them with Thy two-edged sword,
And sin for ever slay.

poems.title: Joshua 10:40: Joshua from above, Thy will
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Joshua from above, Thy will
Concerning us we know,
Thou wilt the destruction seal
Of all our sins below;
None shall in our flesh remain,
All shall die a perfect death
By Thy brightest presence slain.
And by Thy glorious breath.

poems.title: Joshua 11:18: Grace which sure salvation brings
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Grace which sure salvation brings.
Doth long the war maintain.
Fights those other lords and kings,
Who over us did reign:
He who leads the hosts of God,
Conquers, and reconquers all.
Till hy Joshua's sword destroy'd
They into nothing fall.

poems.title: Joshua 11:21: At that time came joshua, and cut off the Anakitns
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Come, victorious Captain, come
In Thine appointed day.
Execute their righteous doom,
The sons of A?tak slay;
Now these tallest giants kill.
Who longest in the land abide.
All my stubbornness of will.
And all my strength of pride.

poems.title: Joshua 11:23: Jesus, full of truth and grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, full of truth and grace,
Among the sanctified
The true Israelitish race,
Thou dost the land divide:
O might I, even I obtain
The bliss to all Thy people given,
Bless'd, for ever bless'd, to gain
The meanest lot in heaven.

poems.title: Joshua 11:23: We wrestle not with flesh and blood
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
We wrestle not with flesh and blood,
The world and Satan are subdued.
And can no more molest,
When Christ hath made an end of sin,
And brought His hallow'd people in
To that remaining rest.

Intestine wars and fightings cease,
When Jesus doth with perfect peace
His throne in us maintain.
King of the saints beneath, above,
In all the majesty of love
He shall for ever reign.

poems.title: Joshua 14:10: Behold, the Lord hath kept me alive, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Kept by the almighty Lord,
My Keeper I admire,
(Christ by highest heaven adored)
And praise Him in the fire;
Who so long hast saved me here,
A few more days preserve Thine own,
Till by Thee prepared to' appear,
And sing before Thy throne.

poems.title: Joshua 18:3: Backward alas, too long, and slack
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Backward alas, too long, and slack
To' accept the grace bestow'd,
The pardon now we gladly take,
The purity of God;
Boldly go up, in Jesu's name
Our portion to possess.
And confident, the land we claim
Of perfect righteousness.

poems.title: Joshua 20:4: When he that doth flee unto one of those cities, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let heaven my sad confession hear!
I at the city's gate appear,
All stain'd with guiltless blood!
Alas, I have my brother slain.
And knew not that the slaughter'd Man
Was the eternal God.
A trembling, persecuted slayer,
Father, I now my cause declare;
Admit the fugitive,
From vengeance screen'd by Christ alone
And in Thy well-beloved Son
Let me for ever live.

poems.title: Joshua 20:7: Holy and Just, I fly to Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Holy and Just, I fly to Thee,
Thy name shall my protection be.
When guilty terrors press;
I leave the' avenger far behind.
Soon as by humble faith I find
The Lord my righteousness!

poems.title: Joshua 20:7: Sole Governor of earth and skies
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Sole Governor of earth and skies,
The burden on Thy shoulder lies
AVho all our sins didst bear,
Securely shelter'd in Thy breast,
Hid by almighty Love, I rest.
Thine everlasting care.

poems.title: Joshua 20:7: Thee, Saviour, I my refuge make
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thee, Saviour, I my refuge make;
And when Thy nature I partake.
And all Thy fulness feel,
From fear, and sin, and sorrow free.
In perfect fellowship with Thee
I shall for ever dwell.

poems.title: Joshua 20:8: Jesus, Thy name my Bezer stands
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thy name my Bezer stands,
A fort which earth and hell commands.
To trembling sinners given;
Salvation doth, as walls, surround,
And I, within these bulwarks found.
Shall mount from hence to heaven,

poems.title: Joshua 20: Thee, Saviour-Prince, our souls adore
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thee, Saviour-Prince, our souls adore.
Exalted by almighty power
To succour and forgive!
We now are to our city come,
A.nd by Thy death returning home.
We soon in heaven shall live.

poems.title: Joshua 20:8: Who to Thy wounds for refuge flee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who to Thy wounds for refuge flee,
Pardon'd we glory, Lord, in Thee,
With ecstasies unknown,
Fulness of joy in Thee possess,
And lodged within Thine arms confess
That Thou and heaven are one.

poems.title: Joshua 23:10: One of you shall chase a thousand
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Subscribing to Jehovah's word
The feeblest Israelite.,
Led on by his ahuighty Lord,
Shall put an host to flight:
By faith the promise I receive
From age to age the same,
And conqueror of the world I live,
Who trust in Jesu's name.

poems.title: Joshua 23:14: Pass a few swiftly-fleeting years
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Pass a few swiftly-fleeting years.
And all that now in bodies live,
Shall quit, like me, the vale of tears,
Their righteous sentence to receive:
But all, before they hence remove,
May mansions for themselves prepare
In that eternal house above:
And O! my God, shall I be there!

poems.title: Joshua 23:14: You know in all your hearts, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thy perfect love reveal.
My Alpha and Omega be,
And I Thy blessed words shall feel,
And witness them fulfiU'd in me:
"Nothing hath fail'd of all the good.
My Saviour hath perform'd the whole,
I know it in my heart renew'd,
I know it in my sinless soul!"

poems.title: Joshua 24:14: Fear the Lord, and serve Him in sincerity, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, that I may truly fear.
Serve Thee with an heart sincere.
Me with legal awe inspire,
Give the thing Thou dost require:
Jos ma xxiii, lo — Judges /. 15.
But that I may worship Thee
With the best sincerity,
Sin by hoHness remove,
Servile fear by perfect love.

poems.title: Joshua 24:14: Willing made my God to' obey
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Willing made my God to' obey,
Now I put my sins away,
Now with every idol part,
Serve Thee with my life and heart:
But that I may serve aright,
Let me in Thy will delight,
Serve a Father reconciled.
Serve as Thy beloved child.

poems.title: Joshua 24:15: Trusting in the strength Divine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Trusting in the strength Divine
I vow to serve the Lord,
Christ shall be by me and mine
Acknowledged and adored:
Jesus, to my house and me
Now let Thy salvation come.
Now prepare our hearts to be
Thine everlasting home.

poems.title: Judges 1:15: A Pleasant heritage is mine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
A Pleasant heritage is mine.
In a fair land and good;
I ask'd and gain'd the gift Divine,
For Jesus' sake bestow'd.
Father, Thou hast my sins pass'd by.
To me a pardon given.
And conscious of Thy favour, I
Enjoy the smiles of heaven.

Yet still I humbly sue for more,
A larger benefit;
A second blessing I implore,
To make the first complete;
In all His fulness from above.
The Comforter impart.
And let the well of life and love
Spring up within my heart.

Thy presence. Lord, the fountain brings
Of purest holiness,
The upper and the nether springs,
The heights and depths of grace:
O might I into nothing sink.
Before the God unknown;
And rise the crystal stream to drink,
Which gushes from Thy throne.

poems.title: Judges 2:23: Therefore the Lord left those nations
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Refusing with our sin to part,
If still we hug it in our heart.
Though infinite in grace
God will not utterly expel.
But leave it in our flesh to dwell,
And plague us all our days.

poems.title: Judges 3:20: Jesus, Thine efficacious word
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thine efficacious word
(If Thou with the deliverer art)
Comes, as a message from the Lord,
A dagger to the faithless heart:
But when it hath the sinner slain.
It brings the dead to life again.

poems.title: Judges 5:20: The malice of Thy church's foes
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The malice of Thy church's foes
In every age we see,
For who Thy people dare oppose
Are fighting found with Thee:
Before Thy face, as chaff they fail,
Before the whirlwind driven:
For how should worms of earth prevail
Against the Lord from heaven?

poems.title: Judges 5:20: Who musters the celestial host
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who musters the celestial host,
He sets them in array.
To blast the persecutor's boast.
And give His church the day:
The stars upon our foes in fight
Their baleful influence shed,
The lightnings wither all their might,
And strike opposers dead.

poems.title: Judges 5:21: Have oft victorious been
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Have oft victorious been
Through the Invincible,
Trampled down the strength of sin,
The powers of earth and hell:
Still on all my foes I tread,
Till He, who hath my sins subdued,
Root out every evil seed,
And fill my soul with God.

poems.title: Judges 5:31: Jesus, let all Thy lovers shine
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, let all Thy lovers shine
Illustrious as the sun,
And bright with borrow'd rays Divine
Their glorious circuit run,
Beyond the reach of mortals, spread
Their light, where'er they go,
And heavenly influences shed
On all the world below.

As giants may they run their race,
Exulting in their might,
As burning luminaries chase
The gloom of hellish night,
As the great Sun of Righteousness
Their healing wings display;
And let their lustre still increase
Unto the perfect day.

Such honour all Thy saints receive,
Who Thee sincerely love
Dispensers of Thy gifts we live,
And general blessings prove;
And when our useful course is run,
Enjoy the kingdom given,
Bright as the uncreated Sun
In the eternal heaven.

poems.title: Judges 6:14: Great Angel of the Lord most high
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Great Angel of the Lord most high,
I wait the influence of Thine eye!
Thy weak, expecting servant see,
And cast the gracious look on me.
The look that may Thy virtue dart,
Thy life and love into my heart,
My strength renew, my mission seal.
And all the mind of God reveal I

poems.title: Judges 6:31: Will ye plead for Baal?
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Will ye plead for sinning on,
For Satan's service plead?
Rather throw his altar down,
And on his worship tread:
Us that he may never more
As advocates for sin employ,
Jesus, come, o'erturn his power,
And all his works destroy.

poems.title: Judges 7:2: Too strong I was to conquer sin
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Too strong I was to conquer sin,
When 'gainst it first I turn'd my face,
Nor knew my want of power within,
Nor knew the' omnipotence of grace.
In nature's strength I fought in vain.
For, what my God refused to give,
I could not then the mastery gain.
Or lord of all my passions live.

But, for the glory of Thy name
Vouchsafe me now the victory;
Weakness itself. Thou know'st, I am.
And cannot share the praise with Thee:
Because I now can nothing do,
Jesus, do all the work alone.
And bring my soul triumphant through,
To wave its palm before Thy throne.

poems.title: Judges 7:15: The sword of the Lord and of Gideon
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What power against a worm can stand
Arm'd with Jehovah's sword?
And all who bow to Christ's command
Are champions of the Lord!
Arm'd with His word and Spirit's might
We shall the battle gain,
And sin, that tempting Midianite,
Shall be for ever slain.

poems.title: Judges 8:4: Faint, yet pursuing
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Often faint, yet still pursuing,
On, like Gideon's men, I go,
Satan and the world subduing,
Pride, and self, and every foe;
Wresde on in prayer unceasing,
Till I see the last destroy'd,
Bless'd with all the victor's blessing,
Crown'd with all the life of God.

poems.title: Judges 10:13: Ye have forsaken Me, and served other gods, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Again to Satan's yoke I bow;
But mercy I implore:
Ah! do not in Thine anger vow
To save my soul no more!
Or if the word Thy lips hath pass'd,
And for Thy loss I mourn,
Thou wilt, O God, repent at last.
Thou wilt again return.

poems.title: Judges 10:15: Lord, I have sinn'd, but now relent
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, I have sinn'd, but now relent,
And groan beneath my guilt;
Humbly accept my punishment.
Do with me what Thou wilt:
For this, and only this I pray,
"From all my sins release,
And save throughout my evil day,
And bid me die in peace.

poems.title: Judges 10:16: Father, though late, I turn to Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, though late, I turn to Thee,
With all my idols part;
O let my helpless misery
Affect Thy pitying heart!
Grieved at Thine ancient people's woe,
Be grieved again at mine.
And force my sins to let me go,
Redeem'd by blood Divine.

poems.title: Judges 11:31: The beast that meets him shall be slain
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The beast that meets him shall be slain;
Resign'd to God the child of man,
A living sacrifice, restored
Entire, devoted to the Lord:
The Lord, he knows, so kind and good,
Hath no delight in human blood.
Or pleased accepts of One alone,
That offering of His slaughter'd Son.

poems.title: Judges 11:39: His hands he wash'd not in her blood
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
His hands he wash'd not in her blood,
But gave his child, his hope, to God,
(Hope of a long-continued line,
Hope of the promised Seed Divine,)
His heart's delight, his age's prop,
His only child he render'd up.
An offering worthy of the sky,
A virgin pure to live and die.

poems.title: Judges 13:8: Who for their unborn children care
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who for their unborn children care,
How happy and how wise!
They find, in answer to their prayer.
Instructions from the skies:
Their babes they from the birth restore
To Him who first bestow'd,
To witness His almighty power,
To fight and die for God.

poems.title: Judges 13:12: The child whom struggling into light
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The child whom struggling into light
We soon expect to see,
How shall we order it aright,
And train it up for Thee?
A candidate for heaven to breed,
Alas, we know not how!
But show us at our greatest need,
Who seek direction now.

poems.title: Judges 13:23: If the Lord were pleased to kill lis, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Me, if purposed to destroy
For past unfaithfulness,
Would my God vouchsafe to' employ,
And still so strangely bless?
Take, O Lord, the servant take,
Who dost the services receive.
With Thyself, for Jesu's sake,
Eternally to live.

poems.title: Judges 15:14: The Philistines shouted against him, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
So by the Spirit of holiness
0/tr Sanisofi did Himself release.
Burst all the bands of death, and rose
The conqueror of His shouting foes,
To slay by means contemptible,
And triumph o'er the hosts of hell.

poems.title: Judges 15: Spirit of faith, come down on me
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Spirit of faith, come down on me,
For where Thou art is liberty.
Thy presence looses all my bands,
And melts the fetters from my hands,
Consumes like flax the cords of sin,
And burns up all my foes within.

poems.title: Judges 16:3: See the great Antitype arise
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
See the great Antitype arise,
While darkness yet involves the skies.
His Israel from their foes to save.
He bursts the barriers of the grave.
Puts forth His strength invincible,
And tears up all the gates of hell!

Triumphant o'er His baffled foes,
The trophies openly He shows:
And daily, in His people's cause.
He spreads the victory of His cross.
And still He takes the spoils, and still
He bears them up the heavenly hill!

poems.title: Judges 16:19: His strength 'Lvent from him
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
His Strength in his obedience lay,
And when his vow he broke,
He cast the slighted gift away.
He first his God forsook.
Sunk into nature's helplessness,
Could neither fight, nor fly:
And such are all who fall firom grace,
And such alas, am I!

poems.title: Judges 16:20: Weaken'd by my bosom-sin
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Weaken'd by my bosom-sin,
Have not I like Samson been.
Went a while securely on.
Wist not that the Lord was gone,
Sport of the Philistines made,
Groan'd my soul itself to feel
Left by heaven, and seized by hell!

poems.title: Judges 16:21: Thine own in Samsoti's, state behold
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thine own in Samsoti's, state behold,
Impotent wretch, by sin allured.
To Satan and his children sold.
Blinded, in brazen chains secured.
Thy loss of liberty and sight,
The wages of thy folly feel.
And groan consign'd to endless night.
The scorn of earth, and drudge of hell!

poems.title: Judges 16: Ah, woe is me, by lust enticed
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Ah, woe is me, by lust enticed!
The Philistines their foe have found.
Dreaded of late, but now despised,
A feeble slave, in prison bound.
Ruled by my haughty tyrant's will,
Forsaken by my angry Lord,
Compell'd I grind at Satan's mill,
And serve the sins I once abhorr'd.

poems.title: Judges 16:22: His anger will the Lord retain
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
His anger will the Lord retain,
A poor dark soul for ever leave?
Gall'd by my hellish master's chain,
After a pardoning God I grieve:
Mock'd by my foes, imprison'd, blind.
Of all my gracious vigour shorn;
Yet lo! a springing hope I find
That Jesus will at last return.

poems.title: Judges 16:28: O Lord God, remember me, I pray Thee, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father of Christ, the sinner's Friend,
My Friend, my Advocate with Thee,
Deliverance to Thy servant send,
And oh! in death remember me!
The wretched thrall of Satan's host.
To me once more Thy Spirit give;
The strength which by my sin I lost,
O let me by Thy grace retrieve.

poems.title: Judges 16:29, 30: Samson took hold of the two pillars, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The Lord resolved in death to save
The vessel of His grace and power,
Pardon in a commission gave,
Inspired, and strengthen'd him once more
To deal the vengeful wrath of God,
And write his victory in blood.

poems.title: Judges 16: My God, my God, on Thee I call
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
My God, my God, on Thee I call,
To bless me with an end like his;
With conquest dignify my fall.
Crown all my former victories,
Strong in Thy might at last may I
Thy champion, though in fetters, die!

poems.title: Judges 16: Samson the theatre o'erthrew
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Samson the theatre o'erthrew,
And thousands at his death he slew:
But lo! our Sa7fison from the skies
A more triumphant conqueror dies,
A nobler victory obtains,
And heaven for all His Israel gains.

He by the pangs of death oppress'd
With outstretch'd hands the pillars seized,
Compass'd with foes He bow'd His head,
For mercy, not for vengeance, pray'd,
And groan'd His last expiring groan,
And pull'd the' infernal kingdom down.

The author dire of sin and death
He slew by yielding up His breath,
The powers of darkness He destroy'd.
And made their hellish boastings void,
Died with the Philistines — but rose
Triumphant o'er His slaughter'd foes.

poems.title: Ruth: A Poor afflicted sojourner
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
A Poor afflicted sojourner
I see the meaning of Thy love;
It strips me of my comforts here,
To mind me of the joys above:
I answer to the call Divine,
After my old companions come,
And for that better country pine,
And hasten to my heavenly home.

poems.title: Ruth 1:13: I! The hand of the Lord is gone out against me
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Gone out against my body, Lord,
Thy chastening hand I feel in pain,
That wounded by Thy Spirit's sword
My soul might perfect health obtain;
Thy hand is contrary to 7?ie,
That / may all be lost in Thee.

poems.title: Ruth 1:16: Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou canst not, Lord, a beggar spurn
That courts Thy company.
Wherefore I never will return
From following after Thee;
Resolved, where'er Thou goest, I go,
In all Thy footsteps tread,
And glad like Thee to want below
A place to lay my head.

poems.title: Ruth 1:16: Thy people by the world abhorr'd
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thy people by the world abhorr'd
I for my people take,
And serve the servants of my Lord,
For their dear Master's sake:
Appeased and reconciled to me,
Through Thine atoning blood,
Thy Father and Thy God shall be
My Father and my God.

poems.title: Ruth 1: Determined after Thee I bear
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Determined after Thee I bear
My cross to Calvary,
And come Thy bitterest cup to share.
And with my Saviour die:
The place where once Thy body lay,
The place it did perfume,
There will I drop my breathless clay.
And rest within Thy tomb.

poems.title: Ruth 1:17: The Lord do so to me, and more also, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
If now Thou dwellest in my heart.
And I in Thee abide,
Nor life, nor death itself shall part
Or tear me from Thy side:
What sets me from my prison free
In closer bonds shall join
This disembodied soul to Thee,
Through endless ages mine.

poems.title: Ruth 1:20: Taught as by thorns and briars, we know
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Taught as by thorns and briars, we know
Thy wisely tender love
Embitters all the joys below,
To' endear the joys above.

poems.title: Ruth 1:21: Went out full of youthful hope
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Went out full of youthful hope,
But empty I return,
My sanguine confidence give up,
My blasted comforts mourn:
A few more days of sad distress
I travel towards a tomb;
But trust to reach in final peace
Mine everlasting home.

poems.title: Ruth 2:3: Casual howe'er our steps may seem
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Casual howe'er our steps may seem,
Directed and o'erruled by Him
Who for His people cares,
Where Providence appoints we go;
He orders all our ways we know.
And numbers all our hairs.

In small events we daily prove
The wisdom of our Father's love;
We own the work is His
From trivial incidents to raise
Matter for His eternal praise.
And our eternal bliss.

poems.title: Ruth 2: By Boaz., yet divinely, taught
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
By Boaz., yet divinely, taught,
Father, we for our servants pray,
Let all their works in Thee be wrought
Thee let them still in us obey,
And find, partakers of the Lord,
In life and death their full reward.

poems.title: Ruth 2:4: Under the yoke, O God, to Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Under the yoke, O God, to Thee
We humbly for our betters cry,
Bless them with true felicity,
With showers of blessings from the sky.
Thy grace be to our masters given;
Our lords on earth be kings in heaven!

poems.title: Ruth 2:10: She Ixnved herself to the ground
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Religion pure rejects the dress
Of rude illiberal clownishness,
Nor calls it sinful courtesy
To' incline the head, or bow the knee;
Well-taught by her, respect we show,
And honour give where'er 'tis due,
But gladly pay to true desert
The humblest homage of the heart.

poems.title: Ruth 2: I Too have left my worldly home
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I Too have left my worldly home,
My old idolatry.
And to Thy people join'd, am come
To put my trust in Thee:
In Thee I seek my full reward
With all Thy saints above:
But tell me now. Thou art my Lord,
And bless me with Thy love.

poems.title: Ruth 2:19: At evening to myself I say
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
At evening to myself I say,
My soul, where hast thou glean'd to-day.
Thy labours how bestow'd?
What hast thou rightly said, or done?
What grace attain'd, or knowledge won,
In following after God?.

poems.title: Ruth 3:4: Jesus, we claim Thee for our own
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, we claim Thee for our own,
Our Kinsman near allied in blood.
Flesh of our flesh, bone of our bone,
The son of man, the Son of God,
And lo, we lay us at Thy feet.
Our sentence from Thy mouth to meet.

poems.title: Ruth 3:9: Spread thy skirt over thine handmaid, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Partaker of my flesh below.
To Thee, O Jesus, I apply;
Thou wilt Thy poor relations know.
Thou never canst Thyself deny,
Exclude me from Thy guardian care,
Or slight a sinful beggar's prayer.

Thee, Saviour, at my greatest need
I trust my faithful friend to prove:
Vow o'er Thy meanest servant spread
The skirt of Thy redeeming love,
Under Thy wings of mercy take,
And save me for Thy nature's sake.

Hast Thou not undertook my cause.
Lord over all, to worms allied?
Answer me from that bleeding cross,
Demand Thy dearly-ransom'd bride.
And let my soul, betroth'd to Thee,
Thine wholly, Thine for ever be!

poems.title: Ruth: I have bought all that was Elimelech's, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O Jesus, full of richest grace,
In pity to our fallen race,
Thou didst at infinite expense
Redeem our lost inheritance,
Thine own inheritance forego,
A poor afflicted man below,
For us procure with all Thy blood
The God of heaven, and heaven of God.

Strangers, and foreigners we were.
Who now Thy purchased people are,
Forlorn, abandon'd, and despised,
Yet by our great Redeemer prized:
Patron of friendless poverty.
The widow now betroth'd to Thee,
Thy church, with heavenly gifts endow'd,
Is made the glorious spouse of God.

Our dead in sin and buried race
Thy brethren. Lord, Thou dost confess,
Nor sufifer'st that our name should be
Cut off to all eternity:
Thy nature with our nature join'd
Preserves the half-extinguish'd kind;
Jesus, Thy name to mortals given.
Exalts both ours, and us, to heaven.

poems.title: 1 Samuel: O Take this plague away
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O Take this plague away!
Afflicted by my God,
In bitterness of soul I pray,
O lay aside the rod!
Or if Thou still reprove,
Let my extreme distress
Bring forth at last the fruit of love,
And perfect righteousness.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 1:18: Her countenance was no more sad
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Beneath a mountain-load of grief,
Subdued, submissive, and resign'd,
I find in prayer my sure relief.
Returning peace with Christ I find:
Soon as on Him I cast my care.
My care doth all at once depart,
My visage can no more declare
The sadness of a broken heart.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 1:23: Not like the mothers in our day
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Not like the mothers in our day.
Who of all care themselves divest,
And thrust their new-born babes away.
And hang them on another's breast.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 1:27: For this child I prayed; and the Lord, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Whate'er I ask, I surely know.
And steadfastly believe.
Thou wilt the thing desired bestow,
Or else a better give;
To Thee I therefore. Lord, submit
My every fond request,
And own, adoring at Thy feet.
Thy will is always best.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 1:28: Since what I lend or give to Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Since what I lend or give to Thee,
Was first Thy precious gift to me,
In this irrevocable loan,
Father, I render Thee Thine own;
Assured Thou wilt in life's short day
My loan an hundred-fold repay,
And crown me, when Thy Son comes down,
With glorious life's eternal crown.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:2: There is Jione holy as the Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Holy as Thee, O Lord, is none;
Thy holiness is all Thine own,
A drop of that unbounded sea
Is ours, a drop derived from Thee:
And Avhen Thy purity we share,
Thine only glory we declare.
And humbled into nothing, own
Holy and pure is God alone.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:2: There is Jione beside Thee: neither is there any, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Sole, self-existing God and Lord,
By all Thy heavenly hosts adored.
Let all on earth bow down to Thee,
And bless Thy peerless majesty,
Thy power unparallel'd confess,
Establish'd on the Rock of peace,
The Rock that never shall remove.
The Rock of pure almighty love.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:3: The Lord is a God of knowledge, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What man or angel can explore
Thy wisdom's unexhausted store,
Thy strict unerring justice trace
Which all our thoughts and actions weighs,
And renders every man his due;
As that decisive day shall show,
Thy providential ways explain,
Thy justice and Thy love to man.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:6: When mortal man resigns his breath
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
When mortal man resigns his breath,
Tis God directs the shafts of death.
Casual howe'er the stroke appear.
He sends the fatal messenger:
The keys are in that Hand Divine;
That Hand must first the warrant sign,
And arm the death, and wing the dart,
Which doth His message to our heart.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:6: Who first inspired the breath of lives
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who first inspired the breath of lives,
The living kills, the dead revives,
Brings to the margin of the grave.
And shows us there His power to save:
From hence if Thou my body raise,
I '11 publish my Restorer's praise,
My life at Thy dear hands receive,
And only for Thy glory live.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:7: Great God, who dost the proud abase
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Great God, who dost the proud abase.
And giv'st to humble souls Thy grace,
Bring down my nature's virtuous boast,
And lay mine honour in the dust;
Then answer a mere sinner's cry,
Where in the lowest deep I lie.
Then from the gates of hell bring back.
And save me for my Saviour's sake.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:8: Most destitute, most helpless
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Most destitute, most helpless I,
A beggar, at the point to die!
Sunk in the deepest poverty,
I all things want by wanting Thee!
Jesus, Thou know'st my desperate case;
Out of my own foul dunghill raise,
Lift up the poor by grace Divine,
And speak the heavenly kingdom mine.

Lord, if I have with Thee found grace,
Lower and lower still abase.
Till by humility made meet
Among Thy priestly kings to sit:
Then wilt Thou lift Thy servant up
Partaker of my holiest hope.
And bid me with Thyself sit down,
A sharer of Thy brightest throne.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:9: Less than the least of saints, on me
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Less than the least of saints, on me
Thy word fulfiU'd I daily see,
Kept by Thy love's almighty zeal,
Preserved from falling into hell:
And still I trust Thy faithful grace
To' uphold my goings in Thy ways,
Till walking with my God, I see
The glorious place prepared for me.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:9, 10: Not all the powers of earth and hell
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Not all the powers of earth and hell
Shall against Jesu's church prevail,
Who bruises with His iron rod
The world, and their infernal god;
The stubborn He in pieces breaks,
But peace to prostrate rebels speaks,
And stretches o'er the faithful race
The golden sceptre of His grace.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:10: The Lord shall judge the ends of the earth, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
All power, O God, in earth and heaven
Thou hast to Thy Messias given.
And bade the' almighty Son of man
At Thy right hand in glory reign:
Our Saviour-Prince shall thence descend.
His sway from east to west extend.
And reign o'er all the earth alone,
Triumphant on the great white throne.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:24: Nay my sons: for it is no good report that I hear
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The fruit of your indulgence see.
Whoe'er in ElPs footsteps tread.
Ye curse your fondled progeny.
Ye pull destruction on their head;
The wrath of an almighty Lord,
Your lenity's effect, they feel:
It fattens for the slaughtering sword,
It softly lets them down to hell.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 2:26: The child Samuel grew on, and was in favour, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Holy Child, our children take
With Thyself on us bestow'd,
Partners of Thy nature make.
Bless, and bring them up for God,
Give them in Thy grace to grow.
Favourites of the Deity,
Favourites of Thy saints below,
Perfectly conform'd to Thee.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 3:18: Of my extreme distresses
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Of my extreme distresses
The author is the Lord:
Whate'er His wisdom pleases,
His name be still adored!
If still He prove my patience,
And to the utmost prove.
Yet all His dispensations
Are faithfulness, and love.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 4:18: When he made mention of the ark of God, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
"Israel before their foes are fled!"
Composed the tidings he receives:
Whole troops; and both thy sons are dead!"
He hears the fatal news, and lives:
"The ark is taken by the foe,
And God doth with His ark depart!"
This, this inflicts the mortal blow.
And breaks his trembling, faithful heart.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 5:3: Great is the truth, and must prevail
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Great is the truth, and must prevail
O'er error, and the gates of hell.
While Dagofi, tumbled from his shrine.
Bows down before the ark Divine,
And Satan's kingdom falls before
Our Prince whom earth and heaven adore.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 5: Idols may triumph for an hour
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Idols may triumph for an hour,
But vanquish'd by almighty power
They to the living God shall bow:
And Dagon stoops to Jesus now;
And till an end of sin I see,
Corruption bows to grace— in me.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 6:20: Who can Thy strict tribunal face
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who can Thy strict tribunal face,
Or stand before the' Almighty's frown,
Approach Thee in Thy brightest place,
Look full upon Thy glorious throne!
God inaccessible Thou art;
Yet who by faith Thy Son receive,
Perfect in love, and pure in heart.
They here shall see Thy face, and live.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 7:2: Touch'd from above with sacred woe
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Touch'd from above with sacred woe
O that we might incessant mourn,
After the Lord lamenting go.
Till Jesus, the true Ark, return!
The contrite heart, the grief sincere,
Jesus, to all our Israel give.
And then display Thy presence here.
And in Thy saints for ever live.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 7: An Advocate in heaven we have
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
An Advocate in heaven we have.
Who pleads for IsracVs faithful race,
And God shall to the utmost save
The souls for whom our Prophet prays:
From sin, the world, and Satan's powers
He now doth to our rescue come.
And when the greedy tomb devours,
Redeems us from the greedy tomb.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 7:9: SINNERS, behold the sacred flame
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
SINNERS, behold the sacred flame
Ascending from the slaughter'd Lamb,
The Lamb of God for Israel given,
Who oflers up Himself to heaven;
Mix'd with the smoke His prayers arise,
And God accepts the sacrifice.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 7:10: Father, Thou dost our Prophet hear
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, Thou dost our Prophet hear,
While now the Philistines draw near;
The offering, which for us He pleads.
Brings down Thy blessing on our heads.
Brings down Thy thunder on our foes,
And all the hellish host o'erthrows.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 7:12: Kept by constant miracle
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Kept by constant miracle,
And succour'd hitherto,
Jesus, I set to my seal
That Thou art good and true.
Trust Thou never wilt depart,
And glad my monument to raise.
Thank Thee with a loving heart,
And with a life of praise.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 10:9: God gave him another heart
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thy call, O God, to man conveys
Sufficiency of gifts and grace:
Wherefore to me Thy Spirit impart.
And bless me with a pastor's heart;
The servant of Thy people I
Shall then rejoice to live and die.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 10:12: Is Saul also among the prophets!
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Yes; if the Lord His mind reveal.
E'en to the meanest of the throng:
Their Father sends by whom He will,
And teaches babes the gospel song;

poems.title: 1 Samuel 12:24, 157: Not to the prophets' schools confined
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Not to the prophets' schools confined,
He gives to the unlearn'd His word;
And lo, they now declare His mind.
And husbandmen proclaim their Lord!

poems.title: 1 Samuel 10:26: The good in man is not his own
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The good in man is not his own.
But freely flows fi-om grace alone.
If to the right our hearts incline,
They own a secret touch Divine;
And Britain's boasted loyalty,
O King of kings, is all from Thee.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 11:7: The fear of the Lord fell on the people, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Pierced with the true religious fear.
We must our king and country love.
Their interests serve with heart sincere.
And swift to their assistance move:
Let all the people of this land
Thus, I ord, to Thee their homage show,
And, duteous to Thy dread command.
Revere Thy delegate below.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 12:20: Ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Vilest of the sinful race.
Plunged in desperate wickedness.
Shall I let my Saviour go?
No: His bowels answer No!
After all that I have done.
Still He bids me follow on.
Till I know the God who died,
Till I find Him — pacified.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 12:24: If mercies without end could move
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
If mercies without end could move
So Ijase, so hard an heart as mine,
Its whole capacity of love
Had surely long ago been Thine:
Lord, for Thine endless mercies' sake,
My stubborn misery relieve.
And to Thyself this moment take
The heart which I can never give.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 13:13, 14: What lost the king his regal power
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What lost the king his regal power?
The want of patience for an hour:
And who for Christ refuse to stay,
With patience cast their souls away,
The cross they hastily lay down.
And forfeit an immortal crown.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 13: After we have endured a while
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
After we have endured a while,
The Lord rewards our patient toil.
Establishes our hearts with grace.
And perfects us in holiness;
But if impatiently we rise
To offer sinless sacrifice,
The power we shall not long maintain,
Or kings without our Saviour reign.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 15:9: Saul spared Agag
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How fond the self-deceiver's hope,
By partial righteousness,
By giving grosser evils up
An holy God to please!
Our vulgar sins we slay in vain,
And every lust beside,
If still we suffer self to reign,
Or spare the life of pride.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 15:22: Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How.shall we offer to the skies
That better, more, than sacrifice?
Jesus, with heavenly wisdom bless,
And teach us how Thyself to please:
O work in me to will and do;
Spiritual adoration true
In perfect love I then shall pay,
And Thee with all my heart obey.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 15:32: Surely the bitterness of death is past
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Sinner, alarm'd by judgment near,
Who fold'st thine arms for sleep again,
As far from death's superfluous fear
And hell's imaginary pain.
No more with harden'd heart presume,
But tremble at thine instant doom.

In pride and delicacy bred,
Secure of a long length of days.
Justice Divine will strike thee dead;
And when thou goest to thy own place,
That bitterness is never o'er,
That death shall last for evermore.

But all who Jesus' spirit breathe,
By faith on Jesus' passion cast.
With them the bitterness of death,
The bitterness of life, is pass'd;
And O! for ever happy, I,
With these indulged to live and die.

poems.title: 1 Samuel: gainst the man of sin in me
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
gainst the man of sin in me,
O Lord, Thine arm make bare,
End his life and tyranny
Whom I reserve and spare:
Agag is the reigning lust;
O let him feel Thy Spirit's sword,
Sacrificed to God the just,
Devoted to the Lord.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 16:23: When the evil spirit was upon Saul, David, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Music, as first by heaven design'd
To calm the tumult of the mind.
Relieves us by its sacred aid.
As Saul was well when David play'd:
But if it takes the tempter's part,
And softly steals from God the heart.
It chases the good Spirit away,
And courts the evil one to stay.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 17:37: Mindful of my rescues pass'd
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Mindful of my rescues pass'd,
When sin and hell were near,
Lord, on Thee my soul I cast.
And no Goliath fear;
Thou, in whom I put my trust.
Wilt still Thy guardian power display.
Save from every giant-lust,
And keep me to that day.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 18:4: Our Prince and Friend enthroned above
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Our Prince and Friend enthroned above
Did thus His zeal for man express,
He stripp'd Himself of all but love,
To clothe us with His righteousness:
Kinder ih.ax Jonathan, He wore
The rags of our humanity.
Self-emptied, sorrowful, and poor,
That all my God might dwell in me.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 20:3: Thanks to my redeeming Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thanks to my redeeming Lord!
Late by Thee to sight restored,
Life itself I plainly see
One short step 'twixt death and me:
While this one short step I take,
Keep me for Thy mercy's sake;
Furnish'd then with wings to fly,
Bear me, Saviour, to the sky.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 22:2: Fly, sinners, fly to David's Son
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Fly, sinners, fly to David's Son,
Distress'd, indebted, and undone.
Him for your Captain choose.
Let Him your ruin'd cause maintain;
The worst, and most forlorn of men
He never will refuse.

If such Thou wilt indeed receive.
Captain, to Thee my name I give.
The poorest outcast I;
And joining now the desperate band.
And subjected to Thy command,
With Thee I live and die,

poems.title: 1 Samuel 22: In want and murmuring distress
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
In want and murmuring distress,
In debt to sovereign righteousness,
A wretched, desperate outcast, 1
To David for protection fly.

Jesus, the Antitype Thou art,
J 'he David after God's own heart,
Commander of the helpless band,
Enlist me under Thy command.

Assure me, Thou my debt hast paid,
Hast for my sins atonement made.
And on Thyself my burden take.
And save me for Thy mercy's sake.

Captain of my salvation, show
Thy strength against my threefold foe,
And, sure of final victory.
In life and death, I follow Thee.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 23:16: O May I thus confirm my friend
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O May I thus confirm my friend.
And teach on Jesus to depend.
On Jesus turn his heart and eye
Who only doth our wants supply,
And makes His strength in weakness known.
And all our works effects alone.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 27:1: So oft preserved in perils pass'd
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
So oft preserved in perils pass'd,
Why should I despond at last.
And cast my faith away?
I cannot help this abject fear,
For still the hellish Saul is near
My hunted soul to slay.

Thou seest my feebleness of heart;
Do not, do not, Lord, depart
In life's extremity;
But stand another hour between,
Another hour my weakness screen.
And take my soul to Thee.

poems.title: 1 Samuel: No wily fiend, by magic spell
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
No wily fiend, by magic spell
Evoked from his infernal cell,
To personate the prophet true.
But Samuel's self appears in view;
I Samuel xxiii. i6 — 2 Samuel i. 17.
To make the prostrate king relent,
Humbly accept his punishment,
To warn him of his instant doom.
But not denounce the wrath to come.

poems.title: 1 Samuel 28:19: To-morrow shall thou and thy sons be with me
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What do these solemn words portend?
A gleam of hope when life shall end:
"Thou and thy sons, though slain, shall be
To-morrow, in repose with me!"
Not in a state of hellish pain,
If Saul with Sa?nuel doth remain,
Not in a state of damn'd despair,
li lowing Jonathan is there!

poems.title: 1 Samuel 30:5: Let earth and hell their powers engage
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let earth and hell their powers engage.
And fierce temptations rise,
Above their impotence of rage
My soul to Jesus flies:
Louder than all their threats I hear
The voice of Love Divine,
Nor can I faint nor can I fear.
Who know that God is mine.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 1:17: For evil may I good return
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
For evil may I good return,
Kindness for bitter hatred show,
With pious grief sincerely mourn
The fall of my relentless foe,
His faults with tenderest love conceal,
His shining qualities commend,
And cordial consolation feel
In hope — that hope was in his end.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 1:26: When lovely Jonathan is dead
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
May I not (?/ my comfort fled,
When lovely Jonathan is dead?
God unprovoked my sorrow sees,
Jesus allows the soft distress:
Hence o'er the pleasing past I rove.
Recall the wonders of his love,
And till my life of mourning end.
Lament for a departed friend!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 3:1: Let the house of Saul give place
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let the house of Saul give place.
And David grow in power.
Nature yield, and stronger grace
Wax stronger every hour,
Grace prevail, till sin depart:
Come, Lord, and rule the land alone,
Come, and 'stablish in my heart
Thine everlasting throne.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 6:7: God smote Uzzah
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
A Voice is in his blood!
Smote for the rash offence.
He warns us to rejoice in God
With deepest reverence.
And trembling at the sign
Of our Creator near,
To treat the holy things Divine
With wise and holy fear!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 6:7, 165: Samuel i., &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
With forward zeal well meant
I oft have evil done,
But could not by a good intent
For a bad act atone:
Yet still my gracious Lord
Hath suffer'd me to live,
And all my sins in deed, and word,
And thought, He doth forgive.
Behold your due in Uzzah dead
For touching an external sign.
You that the priestly right invade,
And minister in things Divine!
Will ignorance your bodies save?
Inquire of Uzzah in his grave.
"But lo! unless our hands sustain.
The tottering ark will strike the ground!"

God cannot need the help of man:
A thousand ways with God are found
His church in danger to defend.
And bear her up, till time shall end.
Unauthorised by right Divine
Dost thou not on the word lay hold,
Who claim'st q, promises for thine
With ignorance profanely bold,
But dost not with the terms comply?
Forbear to touch the ark — or die!
So sacred if the symbol be,
What the true living Ark of God!
And O! how sore the penalty
For trampling on the covenant-blood
Familiarized by common sounds:
Woimds, wounds, and nothing else but icounds!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 6:11: If but one Christian soul appear
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
If but one Christian soul appear
Beneath my roof, the Ark is here:
Jesus, the real Ark Thou art,
Set up in every faithful heart!
And where Thy Godhead doth reside,
Mercy and grace are multiplied.
Fulness of gospel-blessings flow.
And make a little heaven below.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 6:14: He laid his purple robes aside
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
He laid his purple robes aside.
Nor shame, nor diminution fear'd.
Put off the pomp of regal pride.
And servant of the ark appear'd;
In holy services Divine
That we might all our strength employ,
Might body, soul, and spirit join.
And dance before the Lord for joy.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 6:16: Perhaps she thought, religion's law
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Perhaps she thought, religion's law
Might keep the vulgar herd in awe,
But shall so great a man as he
Forget his royal dignity?
Shall David do so mean a thing,
The soldier, statesman, and the king
Lead up the superstitious crowd.
And play, and leap, and dance — for God!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 7:13, 167: The great, who lay their greatness by
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The great, who lay their greatness by.
In presence of the Lord most high,
Nor man regard, if God approve
The' expressions of their warmest love!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 6:22: Let heathen scorn and vilify
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let heathen scorn and vilify
The zealous servants of the Lord,
More zealous, more determined I
Hold fast the faith, and keep the word,
Bolder confess my Saviour's name.
And triumph in the glorious shame.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 6:22: Great in the field of battle, great
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Great in the field of battle, great
The monarch on his judgment-seat
His dread authority maintains.
And conscious of his grandeur reigns:
But before Him who rules the skies,
Humbled as in the dust he lies.
Dares, in the meanest services.
The least of all himself confess.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 7:13: He shall build an house for My name
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Come, Thou heavenly Solomon,
Thou Prince of life and peace,
David's, God's eternal Son,
Who hast the promises,
Thine it is Thy house to build,
To consecrate the human shrine,
With the name, the nature fill'd,
The holiness Divine.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 7:13: Son of God's eternal love
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Son of God's eternal love,
In glorious state descend,
Bring Thy kingdom from above.
That Satan's power may end;
Universal Monarch reign,
And put the worldly kingdoms down,
Fix in every heart of man
Thine everlasting throne.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 11:4: David sent, and took Bathsheba
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Is this the man to God so dear,
So just, and after His own heart!
O what are saints, the most sincere,
The strongest, if their Lord depart!
Left to ourselves one moment, we
Into the foulest crimes should fall,
And thus our helplessness we see.
And feel that Christ is all in all!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 11:15: O Tell it not in Gath, nor spread
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O Tell it not in Gath, nor spread
Through Askelon the direful deed.
Lest harden'd infidels in ill
Rejoice, and grow more harden'd still!
Alas, the record of his crimes
Preserved through all succeeding times.
Savour of life or death must be,
And offer heaven, or hell, to me!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 11:27: The thing that David had done displeased the Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The Lord allows of sin in none.
But most abhors it in His own:
These do His Spirit the worst despite.
These sin against the clearest light,

poems.title: 2 Samuel 12:14, 169: Betray the honour of His name
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Betray the honour of His name,
Expose their Lord to open shame,
Murder afresh the Son of God,
And trample on His richest blood.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 12:7: Thou art the man!
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou art the man — in David'' s case.
Whose careless soul is fallen from grace.
Fallen into heart-adultery!
The curse of God abides on thee;
Till with thy bosom-sin thou part,
The offering of a broken heart
Present before that gracious throne,
And plead the death of David's Son!
Thou art the man — that lives secure
Under the guilt of sin!
Thy heart and conscience is impure,
Thy nature all unclean:
Thou art the man He calls His own
Who bought thee with His blood;
Condemn thyself, and kiss the Son,
And cry, My Lord, my God!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 12:13: I Too have sinn'd against the Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I Too have sinn'd against the Lord,
And struck, and sentenced by Thy word,
To Thee for mercy cry;
The dreadful penalty remit.
And tell a mourner at Thy feet
Thou wilt not let me die.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 12:14: Vouchsafe the grace for which I pray
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Vouchsafe the grace for which I pray,
In mercy put my sin away,
I nothing ask beside;
But chasten'd by a pardoning God,
