Adore Thy hand, and kiss the rod,
Though pain till death abide.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 12:14: By this deed thou hast given great occasion, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Haters of God, who still blaspheme
His glorious name for David's fall.
As ye have sinn'd, repent like him,
Or judgment shall o'erwhelm you all:
From David'' s fall occasion take
For mercy in faint hope to cry,
Or deeper plunging in the lake,
And doubly damn'd, for ever die!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 12:22: While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
For a departing friend I grieve.
Or pray, my stricken child may live;
But when Thy mind is known,
I yield, I patiently submit,
And cry, adoring at Thy feet.
Father, Thy will be done!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 12:23: I shall go to him
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Steadfast in faith, I rest resign'd,
Joyful in hope my babes to find
For whom no more I grieve,
Assured I soon to them shall go.
Assured who infants died below
With God in glory live.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 24:10, 171: Let Shimei curse: the rod he hears
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let Shimei curse: the rod he hears
For sins which mercy had forgiven,
And in the wrongs of man reveres
The awful righteousness of heaven.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 16:10: The Lord hath said Hiito him, Curse David
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, I adore Thy righteous will,
Through every instrument of ill
My Father's goodness see,
Accept the complicated wrong
Of ShimePs hand, and Shimei'' s tongue.
As kind rebukes from Thee.

poems.title: 2 Samuel 18:5: Full of unutterable grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Full of unutterable grace
Thus the true King of Israel prays,
That those who seek His life may live.
Father, My murderers forgive,
Deal gently with them, for My sake,
And to Thine arms the rebels take.
Whene'er my Father in the skies
Is forced this rebel to chastise,
He makes His goodness known;
And while my feeble flesh He grieves,
A charge with the affliction gives,
"Deal gently with My son!"

poems.title: 2 Samuel 24:10: David's heart smote him
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O That my faltering heart may smite
And make me inly groan,
Whene'er I vainly take delight
In aught I call my own!
Harden'd by sin's deceitfulness
O may I never be,
But miss my comfort and my peace,
Whene'er I turn from Thee!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 24:16: He saw the one great Sacrifice
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
He saw the one great Sacrifice
There to be offer'd up for all.
He heard His Son's expiring cries
For mercy and forgiveness call!
Oui' lives, though forfeited. He spares,
For Jesus, our Atonement, died,
His blood was mingled with His prayers.
And God the just is satisfied!

poems.title: 2 Samuel 24:25: David built there art altar unto the Lord, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou, O Christ, our altar art.
And Priest, and sacrifice.
Thou dost by Thy death avert
The vengeance of the skies:
Through Thy grand atonement, Lord,
We gain the pardoning grace Divine,
Scape the cherub's flaming sword.
And live for ever Thine.

poems.title: 1 Kings: His father had not displeased him at any time, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The parent indolently mild
May here his fatal dotage see:
Afraid to vex thy darling child,
Thy darling child shall trouble thee,
Make his indulgent father smart,
And break thy old, fond, foolish heart.

Samuel xxiv. i6 — i Kings vi. 7.

" What pity 'tis, to cross his will,
His clamorous appetites deny,
Restrain the acts of childish ill,
And make the fretted infant cry, 1
Harshly his little faults reprove!
How can I grieve the son I love?"

Continue then thy son to please.
Leave him to nature's discipline,
Till ripe in full-grown wickedness
He claims the wages of his sin.
The wrath of heaven's impartial Lord,
The edge of the Avenger's sword.

poems.title: 1 Kings 3:5: God said, Ask what I shall give thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
THOUbidd'st me ask whate'er I will.
Thou wilt the thing required bestow:
I ask Thy hallowing Spirit's seal,
I ask. Thy precious Self to know,
I ask an humble, perfect heart.
With all Thou hast, and all Thou art.

poems.title: 1 Kings 6:7: David's true, celestial Son
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
David's true, celestial Son
Carries thus His building on.
Joins the stones before prepared,
By the line and plummet squared:
Who the sure foundation lays,
He completes the work of grace,
He brings forth the crowning-stone,
Perfects all His saints in one.

poems.title: 1 Kings 6: Lo! the house of holiness
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lo! the house of holiness,
Founded, built, by just degrees.
Shows the' original design,
Speaks the Architect Divine!
Silenced by His secret power
Hurrying man is heard no more,
All the workmen's noise is still'd,
All the house with glory fiU'd!
Jesus, bid our hearts be still,
Calmly wait Thine hallowing will.
Till brought forth in us we own
Thee the head, and corner stone:
Then the living stones cry out.
Then with one consent we shout,
God, and giver of all grace,
Take our everlasting praise!

poems.title: 1 Kings 8:12: The Lord said that He would dwell, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Darkness and clouds around me roll,
But God shall in the clouds appear,
In this thick darkness of my soul
The great Invisible is near:
He now in His pavilion dwells;
And when He doth the veil remove,
And when His glory He reveals.
My fear shall all be lost in love.

poems.title: 1 Kings 8:22: Solomon stood before the altar, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lo! the pious monarch stands.
And lifts his heart and eyes,
Spreads to heaven his praying hands.
To Him who fills the skies!
Never king appear'd so great!
Himself not half so glorious shone,
Clad in all his robes of state,
And on his ivory throne.

poems.title: 1 Kings 8: See, through him, the heavenly King
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
See, through him, the heavenly King
Who for His subjects prays!
IsraeVs Intercessor sing,
And magnify His grace.
Praise our Lord, who ever Hves
To save and bless His saints forgiven,
Till He to Himself receives,
And blesses us in heaven.

poems.title: 1 Kings 8:27: He did: the King invisible
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
He did: the King invisible,
Jehovah, once on earth did dwell.
And laid His majesty aside:
Whom all His heavens cannot contain,
For us He lived, a mournful man,
For us a painful death He died!

Still the great God resides below,
(And all His faithful people know
He will not from His church depart,)
The Father, Son, and Spirit dwells,
His kingdom in the poor reveals.
And fills with heaven the humble heart.

poems.title: 1 Kings 8:29: That Thine eyes may be open toward this house, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, Thine eyes are open now.
And mark the Place to which I bow.
To which direct my prayer.
The Temple never built with hands.
Before Thy glorious throne it stands,
And all Thy name is there!

There in the temple of Thy Son,
I still for mercy, mercy groan,
Till Thou my guilt remove;
The grace for Jesus' sake I claim,
Through Him declare to me Thy name,
And manifest Thy love.

poems.title: 1 Kings 8:38, 39: O God, take all my sins away
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O God, take all my sins away!
Instructed by Thyself I pray,
Spread forth my hands and heart;
Its secret plague too well I know:
Mercy on Thy poor servant show,
And bid my sins depart.

I turn to the true House of God,
The Temple for three days destroy'd,
And then raised up to heaven:
Father, regard that glorious Shrine
Fill'd with the plenitude Divine,
And speak my sins forgiven.

poems.title: 1 Kings 10:8: Meanest of that happy band
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Meanest of that happy band
Who in Jesu's presence stand,
O might I, even I appear,
Wisdom's self in Jesus hear!
Humbly weeping at Thy feet,
Lord, I wait a look to meet.
By a smile Thy servant raise.
Lift me up, to see Thy face.

poems.title: 1 Kings: On the first early dawn of grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
On the first early dawn of grace,
Alas! who can depend.
When the wise monarch's youthful days
In shameful dotage end!

poems.title: 1 Kings 17:16, 177: O never, Lord, my soul forsake
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O never, Lord, my soul forsake,
Nor let me rest secure
Of heavenly bliss,- till death shall make
My perseverance sure.

poems.title: 1 Kings: But kings may spare their labour vain
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
But kings may spare their labour vain,
For in such happy times as these
The vulgar can themselves ordain,
And priests commence, whoever please.

poems.title: 1 Kings 13:34: Was it a sin in Nehafs son
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Was it a sin in Nehafs son,
A sin which all his house destroy'd,
(What safely may by us be done)
To make Divine appointments void?
Fearless oi Jeroboam'' s fate
Shall men without commission dare
Priests from the crowd to consecrate.
And place them in the' apostle's chair?

poems.title: 1 Kings 17:3: Hide thyself
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Me if Thou in the desert hide.
Or lay Thy servant quite aside,
I patiently submit;
For Thee if I must work no more,
For Thee I suffer, and adore
In silence at Thy feet.

poems.title: 1 Kings 17:16: That thy stock may never cease
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
That thy stock may never cease,
That thy little may increase.
Gladly of that little gi e,
Poor thyself, the poor relieve;
The great Prophet entertain,
Sure eternally to gain
All the infinite reward,
All the glory of Thy Lord.

poems.title: 1 Kings 17:18: To bring my former sins to mind
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
To bring my former sins to mind.
My comforts, Lord, Thou dost remove,
Revoke Thy gifts, severely kind.
And chasten me in jealous love:
The father's sin hath slain the son:
And if it still my offspring slays,
Deep humbled in the dust I own
Righteous and good are all Thy ways!

poems.title: 1 Kings 17:21: Tis thus the Lord my God descends
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Tis thus the Lord my God descends
To raise a sinner from the dead.
His goodness over me extends.
And covers with His Spirit's shade.
Himself amazing grace!) applies,
Lispires me with celestial powers.
And bids my quicken'd spirit rise.
And to my Father's arms restores.

poems.title: 1 Kings 18:38: The fire of the Lord fell, and consumed, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Without that sin-consuming fire,
And teach, as taught by the old liar,
"Sin cannot be consumed in man!"
But who ElijaJCs God believe.
And wait His coming from above,
We shall the Holy Ghost receive.
The Spirit pure of burning love.

poems.title: 1 Kings 19: Thou God, that answerest by fire
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou God, that answerest by fire,
On Thee in Jesu's name we call,
Fulfil our faithfiil heart's desire.
And let on us Thy Spirit fall:
Bound on that altar of Thy cross
Our old offending nature lies;
Now for the honour of Thy cause
Come, and consume the sacrifice.

Consume our lusts as rotten wood,
Consume our stony hearts within,
Consume the dust, the serpent's food,
And lick up all the streams of sin,
Its body totally destroy.
Thyself the Lord, the God approve,
And fill our hearts with holy joy,
And fervent zeal, and perfect love.

poems.title: 1 Kings 18:39: O Th. T the fire from heaven might foil
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O That the fire from heaven might foil.
Our sins its ready victims find.
Seize on our sins, and burn up all,
Nor leave the least remains behind!
Then shall our prostrate souls adore.
The Lord, He is the God, confess.
He is the God of saving power.
He is the God of hallowing arace I

poems.title: 1 Kings: While wandering in the wilderness
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
While wandering in the wilderness,
Such was my clamour to expire.
Not the deliberate wish of grace,
But nature's passionate desire:
Father, my peevish haste forgive,
And strengthen'd by Thy Spirit's supply,
Patient, at Thy command, I live,
Joyful, at Thy permission, die.

poems.title: 1 Kings 19:10: Like him, in piety's decay
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Like him, in piety's decay
I made my solitary moan.
Thou heard'st Thy desolate servant say,
I, even I am left alone!
But now with open heart and eyes
Thousands I in our Israel see.
Who idols hate, the world despise.
Its god renounce, and follow Thee.

poems.title: 1 Kings 19:12: Not in the strong impetuous wind
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)

poems.title: 1 Kings 19:13: That voice which speaks Jehovah near
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
That voice which speaks Jehovah near,
That still small voice I long to hear:
O might it now the Lord proclaim,
And fill my soul with holy shame!
Ashamed I must for ever be,
Afraid the God of love to see,
If saints and prophets hide their face.
And angels tremble, while they gaze.

poems.title: 1 Kings 19:13: I Ask my soul, What dost thou here
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I Ask my soul, What dost thou here,
Thou poor, afflicted sojourner?
My soul returns the sad reply,
I wander, wish, yet fear to die;
The burden of the' Almighty bear,
Consign'd to temporal despair,
Throughout this endless desert rove.
And pine, and faint for want of love.

Zealous I for my Lord have been,
Against the advocates of sin
Defied the world and Satan's frown.
And thrown their impious altars down;
And now of second death afraid,
I seek the shelter of the shade.
My hoary, hated head conceal,
And life's severest evils feel.

O might the hidden God unknown,
For whom I make my ceaseless moan,
The fugitive in pity see.
And manifest Himself to me!
That still, small voice I pant to hear.
Which speaks Him mercifully near.
Covers with guiltless shame the face.
And wraps the soul in silent praise.

Speak, Lord, that I my work may know,
May suffer out my time below,
Perform Thine acceptable will,
And all Thine after-pangs fulfil;
Tell me, Elijah's God is mine,
And strengthen'd by the voice Divine,
My course I shall with comfort end,
And on the fiery car ascend.

poems.title: 1 Kings 19:18: Even in the most degenerate days
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Even in the most degenerate days
Some witnesses reserved shall be,
Some vessels of peculiar grace,
Conceal'd from man, but known to Thee;
Thou only canst their number tell:
O may they prosperously go on,
Till thousands into millions swell,
And all mankind in Christ are one.

poems.title: 1 Kings 19:20: Go back again: for what have I done to thee?
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou know'st what Thou to me hast done,
Thou hast my carnal soul pass'd by,
And after Thee I swiftly run,
Thy resolute disciple I,
Wrapp'd in a covering from above,
Caught by the mantle of Thy love!

Thy dying love my heart constrains:
My all for Thy dear sake I leave,
Participate my Saviour's pains.
And with the Man of Sorrows grieve,
Accept Thine every state below:
But back from Thee I cannot go.

poems.title: 1 Kings 20:11: Scarce have we put the harness on
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Scarce have we put the harness on.
When nature thinks, the work is done.
Defies the world and Satan's hosts,
And of her own perfection boasts:
But veterans in the service know
Their work is never done below;
And when to Christ their spirits they give,
They cease at once to fight and live.

poems.title: 1 Kings 20:31: We have heard that the kings of Israel, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Worthy of death, afraid to die,
To Israels gracious King I cry
The grace Thou hast to others show'd,
O might it be on me bestow'd!
My cause of hope is all in Thee;
O God, be merciful to me,
I pray Thee let the sinner live,
And for mere mercy's sake forgive.

poems.title: 1 Kings 21:29: Doth God regard the outward show
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Doth God regard the outward show?
There must be some remorse within,
Some dread (if it no farther go)
Of judgment hanging o'er his sin:
Righteous the judgment he confess'd,
Pray'd"that on him it might not come,
And mercy stoop'd to his request,
And respited the tyrant's doom.

Humbled like him, the Lord I fear.
And softly in His presence go,
With horror mark His judgments near,
His arm made bare to give the blow!
OThou who didst an A/iab spare,
A partial penitent reprieve,
Break, and inspire my heart with prayer,
And then for 'I'hy own sake forgive.

poems.title: 2 Kings: Such is the heart of man to God
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Such is the heart of man to God,
So haiden'd in his bold offence.
As resokite not to be subdued,
Or baffled by Omnipotence!
But from His angry presence driven,
Who will not here His judgments feel,
Unconquer'd by the fire from heaven
They perish by the fire of hell.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:8: When God receives His servants up
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
When God receives His servants up,
As at the stream of death we stop.
On Jordan's brink a moment stay:
But Jesus, our immortal Guide,
Did by His death the waves divide.
And shows our souls an open way.

Christ and the promised land in view,
His ransom'd pass securely through,
Howe'er the idle billows roar;
In our Elijah's mantle clad,
By His eternal Spirit stay'd.
We reach with songs the heavenly shore!

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:9: Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Before the saints to glory go.
We may implore their aid;
Christ doth on us the gifts bestow.
For which on earth they pray'd:
But when He doth our friends remove.
Himself their place supplies.
Our only Advocate above,
Who prays us to the skies.

Kings i. II — a. II.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:9: "Ask what ye will," 'tis Jesu's word
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
"Ask what ye will," 'tis Jesu's word
To all the followers of their Lord;
He speaks with confidence Divine,
"To give the Holy Ghost is Mine!"
And Thou who didst to heaven go,
Wilt on Thy church the Spirit bestow,
To bless, and sanctify, and seal,
And all our souls for ever fill.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:10: Hard it is, but not for Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Hard it is, but not for Thee
Clothed with full authority.
Hard for sinners to receive,
Easy for my Lord to give:
Sent, in answer to Thy prayer,
Let the promised Comforter
Tell me. Saviour, who Thou art,
Show Thy glory to my heart.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:10: If thou see me, when I am taken from thee, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thee Thy first disciples saw,
When Thou didst from earth withdraw.
Prostrate they received the sign.
Then the plenitude Divine:
Still our faith with joyful eyes
Sees our parting Master rise.
Thus assured Thy Spirit shall come.
Make us His eternal home.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:11: Not in contemplating, or prayer
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Not in contemplating, or prayer,
Their charge the flaming convoy find,
But labouring on with restless care.
And uickening whom He leaves behind,

poems.title: 2 Kings 2: Employ'd, and useful to the end
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Employ'd, and useful to the end:
And thus, my God, may I ascend!

Suitable grace to him is show'd.
Who burn'd with fervent zeal for God,
By heavenly fire refined, removed,
Translated to the God he loved,
He without pain obtains the prize,
And mounts immortal to the skies.
Seraphs the fiery horses were.
And cherubs form'd the heavenly car;
And lo, in state Elijah rides
To where the glorious God resides!
And thus the everlasting Son
Return'd in triumph to His throne!

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:11: That chariot, in my life's short day
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
That chariot, in my life's short day
I oft have seen descend,
To tear my other self away,
To part me from my friend:
But lo, it comes my soul to' unite
With those that went before.
It whirls me to my friends in light.
Where we shall part no more.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:11: He leap'd the fatal ditch, where all
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
He leap'd the fatal ditch, where all
Our death-devoted race must fall!
Who once so fondly wish'd to die,
He went, not downward, to the sky,
And show'd the way by heaven desigiid
To save our whole translated kind.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2: See the true Elijah flies
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
See the true Elijah flies,
Lord of those unfolding skies!
Swifter than the whirhvind's wings,
Flies the glorious King of kings,
Girt with flames of living fire,
Higher still He soars and higher.
Till He gains His bright abode.
Carries up our hearts to God!

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:12: My father, my father!
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, dear departing Lord,
Hang we on Thy latest word.
Us who can Thy word receive.
Fatherless Thou wilt not leave:
Though we may a moment mourn,
Yet we look for Thy return.
Now enjoy the earnest given.
Then ascend with Thee to heaven.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:12: Lord of hosts, to Thee we bow
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord of hosts, to Thee we bow,
Israels car and horsemen Thou!
Shall we not Thy loss deplore,
Whom we see on earth no more?
Ever mindful of Thine own.
Thou for us to heaven art gone.
Gone but to prepare our place.
Room for all the ransom'd race.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:13: He took up the mantle of Elijah
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
We gather up with pious care
What happy saints have left behind.
Their writings in our memory bear.
Their sayings on our faithful mind;
Their works which traced them to the skies
For patterns to ourselves we take,
And dearly love, and highly prize
The mantle for the wearer's sake.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:13: He took up the mantle that fell from him
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Ascending to be clothed upon
With purest robes of heavenly light,
(Robes that outshine the noonday sun,)
He drops his mantle in his flight!
Divested of mortality
He needs it not to wrap his face,
Allow'd his God unveil'd to see,
And strong to bear the glorious blaze!

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:14: Where IS the Lord God of Elijah?
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
When saints forsake our mean abode.
Our hearts should after them ascend,
Inquire, Where is Elijah s God,
The God of my translated friend?
His God, and mine, for ever lives,
Giver of immortality.
And who but now my friend receives,
Shall send the chariot soon — for me!

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:17: They sought, but found him not
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
To traverse hills and dales is vain,
Or search the world around,
It cannot bring us to the man
On earth no longer found:
But following him in holy love,
In zeal, and faith, and prayer,
We soon shall find the seer above,
And share his raptures there.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:21: Jesus, Thy salvation bring
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, Thy salvation bring,
Cast the salt into the spring,
In my heart Thy love reveal,
Nature's bitter waters heal:
Let the principle of grace
Bring forth fruits of righteousness,
Then the barren curse is o'er.
Sin and death are then no more.

poems.title: 2 Kings 2:24: He cursed than in the name of the Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Regardless of a private wrong,
No personal revenge he seeks:
Vengeance doth unto God belong.
And mock'd He in His prophet speaks:
Jehovah speaks the direful word.
That old and young, that great and small
May quake before their righteous Lord,
Who hates, and visits sin in all.

poems.title: 2 Kings: Three kings expecting at his gate
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Three kings expecting at his gate
The prophet's needful help implored,
Elijah's successor so great,
So great a servant of the Lord!

poems.title: 2 Kings 3:15: Hark! the sacred minstrel plays
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Hark! the sacred minstrel plays.
And sings the great Jehovah's praise
See the soothed attentive seer
Ready now his God to hear!
All his powers in concert join,
Passive to the touch Divine,
Admit the everlasting Guest,
And heaven is open'd in his breast.

poems.title: 2 Kings 3: When by the harp's harmonious aid
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
When by the harp's harmonious aid
The fluttering of his spirit is laid,
When nature's latest tumult ends,
The Lord upon his soul descends,
Whose visit greater honour brings
Than three of earth's attending kings!

poems.title: 2 Kings 4:6: When the vessels were full the oil stayed
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Straiten'd in God we cannot be,
No bounds His power and bounty know.
His grace is an exhaustless sea.
Which flows, and shall for ever flow;
And if its course suspended seem.
The hindrance is in us, not Him.

All in ourselves the straitness lies,
Our faith, and not His promise, fails.
He blesses us with fresh supplies
Of joy out of salvation's wells;
And when our heart with joy runs o'er,
Enlarges, and still gives us more.
Above what we can ask or hope,
The God of grace delights to give.
To fill the empty vessels up:
And when we grace for grace receive,
Enough in Christ remains behind,
To fill the souls of all mankind.
Long as our faith's capacity
Is stretch'd to' admit the blessing given,
We drink the streaming Deity,
And gasp for larger draughts of heaven!
But when we lose our emptiness.
The oil, the joy, the Spirit stays!

Empty us then, most gracious Lord,
And keep us always empty here,
Till Thee, according to Thy word,
We see upon the clouds appear,
Thy glorious fulness to reveal.
And all Thy saints for ever fill.

poems.title: 2 Kings 4:19: He said unto his father. My head, my head
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
To whom with my complaints should I,
But to my heavenly Father, go?
Father, to Thee in pain I cry.
My heart, my heart to Thee I show!
It breaks, if Thou Thy help delay,
The soul which Thou hast made expires.
My spirit faints and sinks away,
Implunged in everlasting fires.

poems.title: 2 Kings 4:31: Souls from the death of sin to raise
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Souls from the death of sin to raise
What can a servant of the Lord?
The staff we lay before their face.
We minister the gospel-word.
Wait for the Saviour-God, from whom
Proceeds the animating power;
And Jesus to the dead doth come,
And by the Spirit of life restore.

poems.title: 2 Kings 4:33: He prayed unto the Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Type of Christ, the servant gains
Power from heaven to raise the dead,
Power the Son Himself ordains,'
Lord of life, and Fountain-head!
"Maid," the Saviour saith, "Arise!"
With Divine authority,
Lazarus, come forth," He cries,
"Find thy life derived from Me!"

poems.title: 2 Kings 4:35: The child opened his eyes
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
See the power of God display'd,
The mortal, quickemng power!
He the Hving kills, the dead
He doth to life restore!
The great power of faith confess,
Reversing laws to nature given!
Power of prayer, which hath the keys
Of death, the womb, and heaven!

poems.title: 2 Kings: Take up thy son
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Woman, thy faith is great.
Receive thy dead restored!
And so shall I, who humbly wait
On mine almighty Lord:
That twice dead son of mine,
Jesus, on Thee I cast.
And trust the power of Love Divine
To raise his soul at last.

poems.title: 2 Kings: Death in the pot! 't is always there
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Death in the pot! 't is always there,
The bane of all our food.
When we partake it without fear,
Without an eye to God:
Unless He sanctify the meat.
And bless us from the sky.
Unless we to His glory eat,
Our souls by eating die.

poems.title: 2 Kings: Is it not Thy blessing, Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Is it not Thy blessing, Lord,
Which makes the wholesome food?
Speak the sanctifying word
O'er this on us bestow'd;

poems.title: 2 Kings 5:19, 193: Kings, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Now into our hearts convey
The virtue which proceeds from Thee,
Every creature then shall say
"There is no harm in me!"

poems.title: 2 Kings 5:12: No: for the Lord is not in them
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
No: for the Lord is not in them,
x. Joi'daii s consecrated stream:
And by the means Himself ordains
We all may wash away our stains,
A leprous world may be restored
By virtue of the gospel-word,
Our spirit, soul, and flesh renew'd
In the pure laver of His blood.

poems.title: 2 Kings 5:13: To cure the spirit's leprosy
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
To cure the spirit's leprosy
Easy the way and plain:
Wouldst thou be heal'd? the method see,
And perfect soundness gain:
Wash in the Fountain, and be clean,
Repent, and be forgiven.
Believe, and be redeem'd from sin.
Love, and be rapt to heaven!

poems.title: 2 Kings 5:16: I will receive none
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Accepting what the poor bestow'd,
He spurn'd the riches of the great.
To show the world, a man of God
Trampling as dirt beneath his feet
The things they ignorantly prize,
Lays up his treasure in the skies.

poems.title: 2 Kings 5:19: Go in peace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What saith a younger prophet's zeal?
Not "go in peace" but " go to hell! ''
"And would an hoary seer allow
That Naaman should to Rinimon bow?"
No; but he did his weakness spare,
Glad that his convert went so far,
The evil saw, the good confess'd.
And trusted God to do the rest.

poems.title: 2 Kings 6:6: Deep sunk in nature's base desire
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Deep sunk in nature's base desire,
The sinful mud, the worldly mire,
What but the casting in of grace
This stony, iron heart, can raise,
To heavenly turn my earthly love,
And lift my soul to things above?

poems.title: 2 Kings 6:16: Thick swarming from the dark abyss
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thick swarming from the dark abyss
What troops our soul assail,
Rulers and principalities
And all the fiends of hell!
But Israel's God, supreme in might.
Their countless host o'erpowers.
Single He puts them all to flight;
And IsracFs God is ours.

poems.title: 2 Kings: How safe the man in Jesus found
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How safe the man in Jesus found.
Who keeps his Saviour's word!
Angelic hosts his soul surround,
The chariots of the Lord,
Myriads of flaming guards he sees.
In earth and hell's alarms,
And feels beneath, the Rock of peace.
The everlasting arms!

poems.title: 2 Kings 6:31: By all who neither love nor fear
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
By all who neither love nor fear
Our God, the righteous are abhorr'd,
As authors of their evils here,
They hate the servants of the Lord:
"Away with them," the Avorld exclaim,
"The Christians to the lions cast!"
The stream is troubled by the lamb.
And must be so, while time shall last.

poems.title: 2 Kings 7:2: Thou shall see it with thine eyes, but shall, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The world, O Lord, will not receive
Thy word to sinners given;
They see Thy church in plenty live,
And fed with bread from heaven:
Yet though Thou dost Thy blessings pour.
Incessant from the sky.
They never taste the gracious shower,
But unbelievers die.

poems.title: 2 Kings 8:13: How should we place to Satan give
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How should we place to Satan give,
Or sin to such excess?
We cannot now the depths conceive
Of our own wickedness;
Ourselves so skilful to conceal.
So exquisite our art,
God only knows the utmost hell
Of the deceitful heart.

But now, whate'er was done by man,
Divinely taught I see,
What most my soul abhors, I can
Commit, if left by Thee:
Ah, do not, Lord, forsake Thine own.
And I shall never fall.
Urged to all sins shall yield to none,
I'hough capable of all.

poems.title: 2 Kings 9:30: Who in the painting art excel
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Who in the painting art excel.
Fair rivals of a Paga?i fair,
Look in the glass oi Jezebel,
Admire her lovely likeness there!

poems.title: 2 Kings 10:11: Thus will I, Lord, Thy grace employ
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thus will I, Lord, Thy grace employ,
My former master to destroy,
Drive on, determined not to spare,
And shoot, and stab, and kill, and tear,
Till all of AhaVs house is slain,
And not one single sin remain:
Thou, Saviour, then shalt reign alone,
And call me up to share Thy throne.

poems.title: 2 Kings 10:15: If mine were right, it could not be
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
If mine were right, it could not be.
Good God, so contrary to Thee,
So prone to every sin:
It must remain an evil heart,
Till Thou Thy hallowing grace impart,
And Christ is form'd within.

poems.title: 2 Kings 13:14: Can all her fleets and armies save
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Can all her fleets and armies save
Britannia from her foes?
No confidence in these we have.
When Rome and hell oppose:

poems.title: 2 Kings 13:21, 197: Kings, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What is it then that stands between,
Our nation's sure defence?
The prayers of a few righteous men,
Back'd with Omnipotence!

poems.title: 2 Kings 13:18: He smote thrice, atid stayed
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Like him, I smote, engaged with sin.
Like him I follow'd not my blow
Rekindled hence the war within,
Revived again the vanquish'd foe:
But now I tvill Thy word obey,
I will pursue my victory,
And still smite on, and never stay,
Till sin is all consumed in me.

poems.title: 2 Kings 13:20: But lo, the Lord for ever lives
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
But lo, the Lord for ever lives.
And freely still His Spirit gives.
Who never ties to one His grace,
Can other faithful prophets raise:
He doth His labourers remove.
Yet carries on His work of love.
By whom He will delights to send,
And bless His church, till time shall end.

poems.title: 2 Kings 19:10: Our God almighty to redeem
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Our God almighty to redeem
All gracious we believe.
And know, who humbly trust in Him
He never can deceive.

poems.title: 2 Kings 20:1: My house I may in order set
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
My house I may in order set.
Thou only canst my soul prepare;
O make me for Thy glory meet,
And send the welcome messenger,
That when I my discharge receive.
With Thee I may for ever live.

poems.title: 2 Kings 20:19: Howe'er Thou may'st to-morrow deal
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Howe'er Thou may'st to-morrow deal
With a degenerate race.
Thy goodness, Lord, to-day we feel,
Thy present goodness praise;
Thy truth in this our day we know,
Thy people's peace we prove.
And hand in hand through life we go
To' enjoy Thine heavenly love.

poems.title: 2 Kings 22:19, 20: How went he to his grave in peace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
How went he to his grave in peace,
Who by the sword in battle fell?
Mercy, which sign'd his soul's release,
Did pardon on his conscience seal;

poems.title: 2 Kings 25:27–29, 199: He felt the peace of those that live
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
He felt the peace of those that live
Triumphant in eternal day,
Peace which the world can never give,
Which death can never take away!

O FOR that tenderness of heart
Which bows before the Lord,
Acknowledges how just Thou art,
And trembles at Thy word!
O for those humble contrite tears
Which from repentance flow,
That consciousness of guilt, which fears
The long suspended blow!

Saviour, to me in pity give
The sensible distress,
The pledge Thou wilt at last receive,
And bid me die in peace,
Wilt from the dreadful day remove
Before the evil come.
My spirit hide with saints above,
My body in the tomb.

poems.title: 2 Kings 25:27–29: King of kings, I cry to Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
King of kings, I cry to Thee,
Turn my long captivity.
Break the Babylonish chain.
Lift Thou i my head again;
Thou my kind Redeemer art,
Speak forgiveness to my heart.
Change the prisoner's sordid dress.
Robe me in Thy righteousness.

Me an hoary, captive king,
Out of Satan's dungeon bring,
Raise me, Saviour, to a throne.
Make me partner of Thine own.
Let me at Thy table sit
Nourish'd with immortal meat,
Let me there partake of Thee,
Feast to all eternity.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 4:10: O That Thou wouldst Thy servant bless
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O That Thou wouldst Thy servant bless
With all the blessings of Thy love,
My heart enlarge, my faith increase,
Evil, and pain far off remove,
Keep by the presence of Thy power.
That sin may never grieve me more.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 5:20: They cried to God in the battle, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Sore assail'd, o'erpower'd, oppress'd
I in the battle cry:
Saviour, grant me my request;
Who on Thy aid r ly:
Weak, and helpless as I am.
Yet, Lord, I must victorious prove
Trusting in Thy saving name,
Thy true almighty love.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles: Great God of hosts, against my foe
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Great God of hosts, against my foe.
At Thy command and cost I go,
Commission'd by Thy word, engage
A just and holy war to wage:

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 12:40, 201: And if I fight sustain'd by Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
And if I fight sustain'd by Thee,
I must obtain the victory,
Must more than victory obtain.
And see my sins for ever slain.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 12:18: Thine are we, David, and on thy side, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
David's Son by heaven adored,
We for our King receive,
Unto Thee our sovereign Lord
In life and death we cleave,
Loving, true allegiance bear.
And to Thy will ourselves resign.
Thine without reserve we are.
Irrevocably Thine.

Jesus come. Thy kingdom here
Set up we long to see.
Forward on Thy side to' appear,
O'erjoy'd to act for Thee:
In Thy word of riglUeousness
Ride on. Thy royal right maintain,
Bless'd of God, and sent to bless
The nations with Thy reign!

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 12:40: When the loving King of kings
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
When the loving King of kings
In us erects His throne,
Peace unspeakable it brings,
And glorious joy unknown;
Toasting then His gospel-word.
With all His gracious fulness bless'd,
Keep we with t)ur heavenly Lord
An everlasting feast.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 15:26: In every sacred exercise
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
In every sacred exercise
We need the succour of the skies,
But chiefly when we preach Thy word;
Or bear the vessels of the Lord:
Our power and whole sufficiency,
Jesus, is still derived from Thee;
And if we minister Thy grace,
Thine, only Thine, be all the praise.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 16:43: If in David's steps we tread
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
If in David's steps we tread,
And pay our public vows,
Public doth not supersede
Thy worship in our house:
Joining with Thy sacred word
The voice of fervent praise and prayer,
Daily there we seek our Lord,
And find Thy blessing there.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 21:13: Let me fall into the hand of the Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Gracious Thou, when most severe:
Let me, Lord,' myself resign,
(If I must be punish'd here)
Fall into the Hands Divine,
Hands that this frail creature made,
Hands that still my soul sustain,
Hands which for my folly bled;
Bled the balm that heals my pain.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:9, 203: He loved us, not for faith foreknown
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
He loved us, not for faith foreknown,
But freely in His favourite Son:
Us to our Head His Spirit unites,
In us as part of Christ delights,
Elected, with that perfect Man,
In everlasting bliss to reign.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 28:9: Do we not all from Thee receive
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Do we not all from Thee receive
The dreadful power to seek, or leave?
The dreadful power through grace I use.
And chose of God, my God I choose:
Thee will I seek while life shall last;
Ah! do not from Thy presence cast.
But now, even now be found of me.
And let my soul be hid in Thee.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:5: Lord, in the strength of grace
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, in the strength of grace,
With a glad heart and free
Myself, my residue of days,
I consecrate to Thee;
Thy ransom'd servant I
Restore to Thee Thine own,
And from this moment live, or die.
To serve my God alone.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:9: The Lord a cheerful giver loves
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The Lord a cheerful giver loves;
A cheerful giver loves the Lord,
And while by works his faith he proves.
Receives an hundred-fold reward.
With joy restores what God had given,
Bless'd with anticipated heaven.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:10, 11: Bless'd be our everlasting Lord
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Bless'd be our everlasting Lord,
Our Father, God, and King,
Thy sovereign greatness we record.
Thy glorious power we sing;
By Thee the victory is given,
The majesty Divine,
And strength, and might, and earth and heaven,
And all therein is Thine.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:11, 12: The kingdom, Lord, is Thine alone
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The kingdom, Lord, is Thine alone
Who dost Thy right maintain,.
And high on Thine eternal throne
O'er men and angels reign:
Riches, as seemeth good to Thee,
Thou dost, and honour give;
And kings their power and dignity
Out of Thine hand receive.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:13: Thou hast on us the grace bestow'd
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou hast on us the grace bestow'd
Thy greatness to proclaim.
And therefore now we thank our God,
And praise Thy glorious name;
Thy glorious name and nature's powers
Thou hast to man made known,
And all the Deity is ours,
Through Thine incarnate Son.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:14: O May I never, never seek
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O May I never, never seek
Myself to aggrandise.
But meanly think, and humbly speak,
As vile in my own eyes:
I Chronicles xxix. lo, ii — 20.
What am I, Lord, but sinful dust?
Yet, bought with blood Divine,
If in Thy only Son I trust,
Whate'er Thou art is mine.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:14: God hath all our actions wrought
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
God hath all our actions wrought;
Thou with every gracious thought,
Thou with every good desire
Dost our feeble hearts inspire;
Pay we then our thankful rent,
Praises to our Lord present.
Gladly give Thee back Thine own.
Live and die to God alone.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29: The angels are at home in heaven
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The angels are at home in heaven.
The saints unsettled pilgrims here:
Our days are as a shadow, driven
From earth, so soon we disappear,
We no abiding city have.
No place of resting, but the grave.

Transient our life, and dark, and vain,
With empty joy and solid woe.
It never can return again.
Soon as our dream is pass'd below.
Its darkness ends in perfect night.
Or glorious everlasting light.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:20: O Lord our God, we bless Thee now
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O Lord our God, we bless Thee now.
To Thee our souls and bodies bow,
With humblest awe foil down before
Thy throne, and joyfully adore;
God of our ancestors we praise,
The Father, Son, and Spirit of grace,
One glorious God in persons three.
Our God through all eternity.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:20: Whoe'er the King of kings adore
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Whoe'er the King of kings adore.
Must reverence His vicegerent here.
Not earth and hell with all their power
Can separate loyalty and fear:
And hence the man set up by Thee,
Great God, Thy faithful people own.
In him Thy royal image see.
And bow before the British throne.

poems.title: 1 Chronicles 29:28: He died, full of days, riches, and honour
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Full, but not satisfied
With wealth and pomp, he died:
Wealth, and pomp, and length of days,
Could not fill a deathless soul
Made to feast on Jesu's grace,
While eternal ages roll.

Jesus, my soul to fill
Thy blessed Self reveal,
Come, and bring me from above
All the life of righteousness,
All the riches of Thy love.
All the glories of Thy grace.
O 'tis enough! I ask no more.
Full of a few sad sinful days.
Sated with life, till life is o'er
I languish to conclude my race.
I Chronicles xxix. 20 — 2 Chronicles vi. 20, 21.
And silently resign my breath,
And sink into the shades of death.

This earth without regret I leave,
Impatient for my heavenly rest:
Saviour, my weary soul receive,
Take a sad pilgrim to Thy breast,
Vho only live, and die, to be
Restored, resorb'd, and lost in Thee.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 1:10: Wisdom Divine I long to know
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Wisdom Divine I long to know:
The wisdom which Thou art,
Jesus, on a poor worm bestow,
And speak into my heart:
I never can be satisfied.
Till Thou art fully given;
On earth I nothing want beside,
Nothing besides in heaven.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 1:12: Wisdom and knowledge is, granted unto thee, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Wisdom, because we ask, He gives,
Riches, because we ask them not:
Riches of grace whoe'er receives,
Above whate'er he wish'd or thought,
Will find, with Jesu's kingdom given.
Peace upon earth, and joy in heaven.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 6:20, 21: That Thine eyes may be open upon this house, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father of everlasting grace,
Be mindful of Thy changeless word;
We worship toward that holiest Place,
In which Thou dost Thy name record.
Dost make Thy gracious nature known,
That hving temple of Thy Son.

Thou dost with sweet complacence see
That Temple fill'd with light Divine:
And art Thou not well pleased with me,
Who turning to that heavenly Shrine,
Through Jesus to Thy throne apply.
Through Jesus for acceptance cry?

With all who for redemption groan,
Father, in Jesu's name I pray;
And still we cry and wrestle on.
Till mercy takes our sins away:
Hear from Thy dwelling-place in heaven.
And now pronounce our sins forgiven.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 6:33: Respecting Jesus in our prayer
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Respecting Jesus in our prayer.
For this, O God, we call on Thee,
Thy name throughout the earth declare.
That all may Thy salvation see.
May all, like us. Thy goodness prove.
And feel the fear which flows from love.

Our prayer, presented through Thy Son,
Answer on all the ransom'd kind.
Collect Thy scatter'd sheep in one,
To Jesus, and Thy people join'd,
Let every soul Thy nature know.
And see the King of saints below.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 6:36: No: every fallen child of man
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
No: every fallen child of man
Must sin in thought, and word, and deed
But bursting our oppressor's chain
When Jesus hath His prisoners freed,

Chronicles vi. i i — x- 6.
The dire necessity is o'er,
And born of God we sin no more.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 6:41: Let Thy priests be clothed with salvation, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, the word of mercy give,
And let it swiftly run,
And let the priests themselves believe,
And put salvation on:
Clothed with the Spirit of holiness
May all Thy people prove
The plenitude of gospel-grace,
The joy of perfect love.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 6:42: Jesus Thine anointed One
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus Thine anointed One
For helpless sinners prays:
Canst Thou disregard Thy Son,
Or turn away His face?
Him Thou always hear'st well-pleased,
My Intercessor at Thy side;
Save me then, the soul distress'd
For whom Messias died.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 9:6: I Drawn by Thy messengers' report
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I Drawn by Thy messengers' report,
I hearken, Lord, to Thee:
But O! their word how faint, how short
Of what I hear and see!
True Son of David, I confess
Thou far exceed'st the fame:
Not angel-tongues could half express
The wonders of Thy name.

Vhat wisdom from Thy lips distils,
So full of glorious grace!
The glory all Thy household fills
Reflected from Thy face:
Thy charms the seraphs' thought transcend,
And dazzle all above,
For only saints can comprehend
The mystery of Thy love.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 12:7: They have humbled themselves, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I Cannot, Lord, in judgment stand,
I sink beneath Thy mighty hand.
And guilty, guilty plead;
Righteous in all Thy ways art Thou,
And wouldst have had me live, if now
Thy justice strike me dead.

Yet if I do at last relent,
And by a power from Thee repent
Of all that I have done,
An humbled soul Thou wilt not slay.
But turn Thy righteous wrath away.
And give me to Thy Son.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 12:8: An abject slave I long have been
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
An abject slave I long have been
To Satan, and the world, and sin,
As by my God forsook.
Who would not to my Saviour stoop,
The burden of His cross take up.
Or bear His easy yoke.

The difference now I know and feel;
Jesus, to serve Thy foes is hell;
But once again forgiven,

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 14:11, 211: O let me find in serving Thee
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O let me find in serving Thee
The glorious, perfect liberty,
The happiness of heaven.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 13:14, 15: They cried unto the Lord, and gave a shout
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
By numbers urged, o'erpower'd we are,
But, Jesus, on Thy name we call,
Thy Spirit in the cry of prayer.
And shout of faith, shall conquer all.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 14:11: Lord, it is nothing with Thee to help, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Be they strong, or void of might.
Many, O Lord, or few.
Thou dost for Thy people fight,
And all their foes subdue:
Thou wilt more than conquer mine,
Who weak as helpless infancy,
Apprehend through faith Divine
The power of God in Thee.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 14:11: Lord of hosts, and God of love
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord of hosts, and God of love,
To Thee for help we cry,
Send us succour from above
Who on Thyself rely j
Earth, and sin to Thy great name,
And all the powers of darkness bow:
Jesus, evermore the same,
Appear our Saviour now!

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 14:11: Father, help, by covenant ours
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, help, by covenant ours.
Nor let Thy promise fail.
Let not earth's confederate powers
Against Thy church prevail;
If to Christ our Head we join,
One spirit if with Christ we be,
Conquering us in Jesus Thine,
Great God, they conquer Thee.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 15:2: By humble faith and active love
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
By humble faith and active love
Long as we stay with Thee,
Thou wilt not from Thy church remove,
Thou wilt abide with me:
With Thee that I may still remain,
And never more depart,
Jesus, create my soul again,
And dwell within my heart.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles: Justly, O Lord, Thou dost require
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Justly, O Lord, Thou dost require
The industry of man.
And seeking with our whole desire
We cannot seek in vain:
Thee if we follow on to know.
We must Thy sweetness prove,
And find our paradise below
The' experience of Thy love.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles: But if ye forsake Him, He will forsake you
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Faithful, O God, Thy threatening word,
And righteous Thy decree,
Whoe'er deny their gracious Lord
Shall be denied by Thee:
His pardon, who to sin turns back,
Thou surely wilt revoke,
The' apostate utterly forsake
And blot out of Thy book.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 16:9: The eyes of the Lord run to and fro, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
O Thou, whose eyes run to and fro
To mark Thy worshippers below,
Who Thee sincerely love,
Thou dost in their behalf appear,
While sin, the world, and hell are near,
And hide their lives above.

Omniscient God, to me impart
The blessing of an upright heart,
And then Thine eyes will see
With kind regard my favour'd soul.
And Jesus will put forth His whole
Omnipotence in me.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 16:12: The' incurable disease
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The' incurable disease
Which baffles human art.
The Healer of mankind can ease,
Or bid it all depart:
I hang upon Thy breath!
And let Thy will be done,
In ease and pain, in life and death,
I seek to God alone.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 19:3: Ah, how can I my heart prepare
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Ah, how can I my heart prepare
To seek my Lord aright?
Jesus, the Way, Thyself declare
In pure unerring light.
Giver of true repentance, break
This stubborn heart of stone,
Then shall I leave my sins, and seek,
And find Thee all my own.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 20:6: Power and might are in Thy hand
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Power and might are in Thy hand
Which gives the victory,
None is able to withstand
An host sustain'd by Thee:
Show Thyself the Lord most high,
Exert Thine arm in our defence,
Jesus come, and glorify
Thine own omnipotence.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 20:12: So powerful both by sea and land
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
So powerful both by sea and land,
Can Britain say, Ave have no might?
None, none against our foes to stand.
Unless the Lord for Israel fight:
We have no might wherein to trust,
And will, if bless'd with victory,
Jesus, of Thy protection boast,
And all the praise ascribe to Thee.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 20:12: Thou know'st, I know not what to do
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou know'st, I know not what to do.
But turn on Thee my wishful eye.
The help of man, the means, look through.
On Thee, on Thee alone rely:
Mine eye of faith, desire and prayer
For ever fix'd on heaven, attends,
Till saved I find a Spokesman there,
And God into my heart descends.

Caught in the toils of hell and sin.
One farther step I cannot go;
What shall I do my God to win?
My God, and none beside can show:

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 26:16, 215: Saviour, my helpless desperate state
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Saviour, my helpless desperate state
Thou dost, Thou dost this moment see:
And lo, I every moment wait
To know what Love designs for me.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 20:17: Bewilder'd, lost, I must stand still
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Bewilder'd, lost, I must stand still,
Alas I can no farther go;
Wilt Thou not, Lord, Thyself reveal?
I want, I wait Thyself to know:
This moment if Thou ready art
To make a worm Thy humble home,
Break in even now upon my heart.
My Saviour and salvation, come.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 20:20: Jesus, on Thee our souls are stay'd
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, on Thee our souls are stay'd.
Who hast the sure foundation laid,
Thou wilt complete the work begun
Our Saviour still through faith alone,
Confirm the grace to sinners given,
And build Thy temples up to heaven.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 20:21: Let all in joyful songs record
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Let all in joyful songs record
The mercy of our common Lord,
The God of everlasting grace
He claims our everlasting praise.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 26:16: When he was strong, his heart was lifted, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Weakest, when I strongest seem,
Fallen alas I am through pride,
Sinless then myself I dream,
Pure, and wholly sanctified,
Fold my arms, and take my ease,
Safe in perfect holiness.

Wake my soul to sleep no more,
Give me back my poverty,
Till the kingdom Thou restore:
When it is restored in me.
Give me, Lord, myself to feel
Weak, and poor, and nothing still.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 26:18: "But now (the warm Enthusiast cries)
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
"But now (the warm Enthusiast cries)
The office to myself I take,
Offering the Christian sacrifice.
Myself a lawful priest I make.
To me the honour appertains;
No need of man, when God ordains.

"Though kings may not so far presume,
Tis no presumption in a clown:
And lo, without a call from Rome,
My flail, or hammer I lay down!
And if my order's name ye seek,
Come see a new Melchizedek!"

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 26:21: Ye upstart priests, your sentence know
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Ye upstart priests, your sentence know,
The marks you can no longer hide.
Your daring deeds too plainly show
The loathsome leprosy of pride;
And if ye still your crime deny.
Who lepers live, shall lepers die.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 28:22: I Just such a wretch am
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
I Just such a wretch am I,
Who underneath the rod
Sin on self-harden'd, and defy
The utmost wrath of God:

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 32:31, 217: The deeper in distress
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The deeper in distress,
The farther I rebel,
As bent to claim for my own place
The hottest place in hell.

Tis not in pain to move
This most obdurate heart;
Only the power of bleeding love
Can stone to flesh convert,
Bid my rebellions end,
And wash the Eihiop white.
And change a foul incarnate fiend
Into a child of light.

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 32:31: God left him, to try him, that he might, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
May'st Thou not still conceal Thy face,
Withdraw the sweet delights of grace,
And from Thine own depart,
To try, and seal them for Thine own.
To show the sin which lurk'd unknown
In my deceitful heart?

Surely, before my Lord withdrew,
Hid from myself I never knew
What now I groan to feel:
Thy absence hath my pride bewray'd.
And thus convinced, I see display'd
The depths of my own hell.

Left to myself, I now confess.
My heart is desperate wickedness.
But trust Thy gracious power
To make an utter end of sin,
Thou wilt at last appear within.
And never leave me more,

poems.title: 2 Chronicles 33:12, 13: Viler than Manasses
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Viler than Manasses I,
Forced by deep affliction pray.
Prostrate in Thy presence cry
Take Thy heavy plague away,
If Thou canst intreated be,
Hear, my God, and pardon me.

To mine inmost soul restore
Forfeited felicity,
Fulness of victorious power,
Peace and joy reveal in me,
Give the gracious kingdom back,
Save me now for Jesu's sake.

poems.title: Ezra 3:11: All the people shouted, because the foundation, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Rock of eternity.
Thy church is built on Thee,
Thou the Foundation art,
Laid in the faithful heart,
And fill'd with glorious joy unknown.
We shout to see Thy house begun.

The sure Foundation laid
Makes all Thy people glad,
Who wait, with joy renew'd.
To see the house of God
In finish'd holiness arise,
By just degrees to reach the skies.

Chronicles xxxiti. 12, 13 — Ezra in. 22.

poems.title: Ezra 5:5: What but Thy strength-inspiring eye
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
What but Thy strength-inspiring eye
Thy weakest servants could sustain?
Jesus, Thou dost with grace supply,
And lo, the heathen rage in vain.
They cannot make the workmen cease,
Or stop Thy preaching witnesses.

poems.title: Ezra: In vain we offer sacrifice
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
In vain we offer sacrifice
To God who rules both earth and skies.
Unless our loyal hearts revere
His image and vicegerent here;
But when for conscience we obey,
Long live our king on earth, we pray,
Long live our king, and late remove
To claim his crown of life above!
686 The Lord turned the heart of the kin unto, &c.—. 22.
X Thou that by a touch Divine
Dost the heart of kings incline,
See, with smiles of favour see
Whom our faith presents to Thee:
Mould, and turn his heart and will
All Thy counsel to fulfil,
Honour'd with his God to join,
Glad to second Thy design.

By his gracious wise commands
Strengthen Thou the workmen's hands,
Who, as instruments of grace,
Under Thee Thy temple raise:
Or if so Thy will ordain
Not to' accept the help of man,
Only Thou Thy servants own,
Build the house Thyself alone.

poems.title: Ezra 7:6: The king granted him all his request, according, &c
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Jesus, with Thine o'ershadowing hand,
With Thine almighty favour bless'd.
Thy servants before kings shall stand,
And prosper'd in their just request,
Boldly dispense that gospel-word,
Which builds the temple of the Lord.

poems.title: Ezra 7:9: Conducted by His gracious power
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Conducted by His gracious power.
Where'er our Lord directs we go.
Secure in danger's blackest hour.
And careless of our ambush'd foe,
Whom Jesus -covers with His hand,
We reach the holy, heavenly land.

poems.title: Ezra 7:27: The' external house of the Most High
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
The' external house of the Most High
Cyrus may build, or beautify,
Jesus, 'tis Thine alone to raise
The living temples of Thy grace.
To' adorn our souls, when cleansed from sin.
And make us glorious all within.

poems.title: Ezra 8:22: Lord, we before the world profess
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Lord, we before the world profess
Our trust in Thine almighty grace
Which for Thy servants cares;
Thou, while we trust on Thee alone,
Dost bring the blind by ways unknown,
And number all our hairs.

Ah, leave us not in danger's day,
By fear Thine honour to betray,
By base mistrust to' offend
The strangers to Thy pardoning love;
But let us still consistent prove,
And faithful to the end.

poems.title: Ezra 8:22: Father, in Christ we seek Thy face
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Father, in Christ we seek Thy face;
Stay by Thine outstretch'd hand of grace
The weak, and lead the blind,
In every trying hour defend.
Till the high prize we apprehend,
And heaven in Jesus find.

poems.title: Ezra 9:8: Favour, and grace to Israel shown
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Favour, and grace to Israel shown
Is from the Lord our God alone,
Whatever hand Thy blessing brings,
Or Persia's, or Britantiia's kings,
The Fountain in the streams we see.
And all our good derived from Thee.

poems.title: Ezra 9:8: To leave us a remnant to escape
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Thou lately, Lord, in special grace.
Hast visited our captive race.
The remnant left in Babylotu
And made Thy pardoning mercy known.
And help'd us to escape away
By the first dawn of gospel-day.

poems.title: Ezra 9:8: Ercy hath a sure nail bestow'd
poems.author: Charles Wesley
poems.collection: Short Hymns on Select Passages of the Holy Scriptures (1762) · Osborn ed., vol. 9 (1870)
poems.text:
Ercy hath a sure nail bestow'd
And fix'd us in the House of God,
Where Thou Thy glories dost reveal.
In Christ the holy Place we dwell.
